summary: Qian proves that every semisimple residual representation of the absolute Galois group of a CM field into GL_n(F_{l^s}), l odd, becomes ordinarily automorphic after a CM extension avoiding a given field (Theorem 1.1), using an asymmetric Dwork family and a switch between two coefficient primes. With ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 he deduces potential automorphy of suitable ordinary l-adic representations (Theorem 1.4), which the paper proves only for l > n (E2). Corrected in place by the independent review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: 145 items, 16 routes (12 source routes, the new Part II of Dwork switching motives, and joins of three existing proposals), 48 confirmed mistakes (E10 withdrawn). Not formalised.

items.name: Continuous residual representation and residual semisimplification
items.statement: Let Γ be a profinite group and l a prime. In the paper Γ is G_F for a number field F, or a decomposition group G_{F_v}. A residual representation is a continuous homomorphism r̄: Γ → GL_n(F̄_l), where GL_n(F̄_l) carries the discrete topology. Its image is finite, so r̄ takes values in GL_n(k) for some finite subfield k ⊂ F̄_l; in Theorem 1.1, k = F_{l^s}. Now let r: Γ → GL_n(Q̄_l) be continuous. By the Baire category theorem, r takes values in GL_n(E) for some finite extension E/Q_l. By compactness of Γ, it preserves an O_E-lattice in E^n, where O_E is the ring of integers of E. The residual representation r̄: Γ → GL_n(F̄_l) of r is the semisimplification of the reduction of this lattice modulo the maximal ideal of O_E, with coefficients extended to F̄_l. By the Brauer–Nesbitt theorem, r̄ is well defined up to isomorphism: it depends neither on E nor on the lattice. Following ACC+ §1.2, a bar over an l-adic representation (as in Definition 1.3 and Theorem 1.4) denotes this residual representation. A lift of a residual representation r̄ is a continuous r: Γ → GL_n(Q̄_l) whose residual representation is isomorphic to r̄.
items.locator: Implicit in Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 and Definition 1.3, pp. 1239–1241; the bar convention is that of ACC+ §1.2 (Notation), p. 905

items.note: Planned at ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1. In arbitrary finite rank n, R01.1 plans invariant lattices for field coefficients by compactness, and 'reduction followed by semisimplification' with independence of the lattice by characteristic polynomials and the characteristic-p Brauer–Nesbitt theorem. Its descent clause, 'Prove descent of a continuous representation into GL₂(F̄_p), with discrete target, to a finite coefficient field', covers only rank 2. The rank-n descent must be added to R01.1: a continuous r̄: Γ → GL_n(F̄_l) with discrete target takes values in GL_n(k) for a finite field k. Theorem 1.1 needs it, because it takes r̄ with values in GL_n(F_{l^s}), and so does Theorem 1.4, where r̄ is the residual representation of r. R01.1 also does not state explicitly that a continuous representation into GL_n(Q̄_l) takes values in GL_n(E) for a finite extension E/Q_l, which the reduction step needs. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, planning stages.

items.name: Regular ordinary local Galois representation
items.statement: Let L be a finite extension of Q_p and ρ: G_L → GL_n(Q̄_p) a continuous representation. ρ is ordinary with regular Hodge–Tate weight if there is a weight λ = (λ_{τ,i}) ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(L,Q̄_p)}, where Z^n_+ = {(a_1,…,a_n) ∈ Z^n : a_1 ≥ … ≥ a_n}, with the following two properties. First, ρ is isomorphic to an upper-triangular representation whose diagonal characters are ψ_1,…,ψ_n in this order, so ψ_1 is a subrepresentation and ψ_n a quotient. Second, for each i = 1,…,n the character ψ_i: G_L → Q̄_p^× agrees, on an open subgroup of the inertia group I_L, with σ ↦ ∏_{τ ∈ Hom(L,Q̄_p)} τ(Art_L^{-1}(σ))^{−(λ_{τ,n−i+1}+i−1)}. Here Art_L is the local Artin map normalized to send uniformizers to geometric Frobenius elements, the convention of ACC+ §1.2. The paper does not restate this normalization, and it matters: the other normalization inverts Art_L^{-1} on inertia and so reverses the sign of every exponent. The condition is the local form of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2(2), with the same formula. Potential semistability is not part of the definition; Theorem 1.4 and ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 impose it separately.
items.locator: Definition 1.2, p. 1240 (the same condition as ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2(2), pp. 1029–1030)

items.name: Automorphic Galois realization
items.statement: Let E be a CM or totally real number field, l a prime and ι: Q̄_l ≅ C. For each regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(A_E) there is a unique continuous semisimple representation r_{l,ι}(π): G_E → GL_n(Q̄_l) with the following property. For every rational prime p ≠ l above which π and E are unramified, and every place v | p of E, r_{l,ι}(π) is unramified at v and r_{l,ι}(π)|^{ss}_{W_{E_v}} ≅ ι^{-1} rec_{E_v}(π_v ⊗ |det|_v^{(1−n)/2}), where rec_{E_v} is the local Langlands correspondence. Existence is the main theorem of Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne. Uniqueness follows from the Chebotarev density theorem and the Brauer–Nesbitt theorem. Nothing is asserted at ramified places or about the monodromy operator.
items.locator: §1, p. 1240 (the paragraphs after Theorem 1.1), citing [9] (Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne, On the rigid cohomology of certain Shimura varieties), main theorem

items.name: Ordinarily automorphic representations (residual and l-adic)
items.statement: Let E be a CM or totally real field, l a prime and ι: Q̄_l ≅ C the fixed isomorphism. A residual representation r̄: G_E → GL_n(F̄_l) is ι-ordinarily automorphic if it has an automorphic lift r ≅ r_{l,ι}(π) (Definition 1.3) such that π is ι-ordinary at every place v | l, in the sense of Geraghty [8, Definition 5.3]. This is a condition on the eigenvalues of the normalized Hecke operators on π_v, not on r|G_{E_v}. Applied to an l-adic representation r: G_E → GL_n(Q̄_l), the same term means that r ≅ r_{l,ι}(π) for a regular algebraic cuspidal π that is ι-ordinary at every v | l. The paper uses it in this sense in Lemma 4.3 and in the conclusion of Theorem 1.4 without defining it separately, and it is the form of the conclusion of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2. Ordinarity of r_{l,ι}(π)|G_{E_v} for v | l does not replace this condition. As Remark 4.4 explains, the local–global compatibility that would deduce automorphic ordinarity from it assumes polarizability.
items.locator: Definition 1.3, p. 1241 (last sentence, citing [8] = Geraghty, Definition 5.3); l-adic use in Lemma 4.3 and its proof, p. 1273, and in the conclusion of Theorem 1.4, p. 1241; Remark 4.4, p. 1274; compare the conclusion of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2, p. 1030

items.name: Local genericity away from the coefficient prime
items.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic p, l ≠ p a prime, and K/Q_l a finite extension with residue field k_K. A continuous representation r: G_K → GL_n(k) is generic if it is unramified and the eigenvalues α_1,…,α_n ∈ k̄ of r(Frob_K), listed with multiplicity, satisfy α_i/α_j ≠ #k_K for all i ≠ j, where #k_K is read in k. A ramified representation is never generic. The condition runs over all ordered pairs i ≠ j, so it is the same whether Frob_K is an arithmetic or a geometric Frobenius. Repeated eigenvalues are allowed when #k_K ≢ 1 (mod p). The letters are those of ACC+, where k has characteristic p and the local field lies over the other prime l. Just before Definition 4.3.1 (p. 972), ACC+ notes that, compared with its source, 'the roles of p and l are reversed'. In Theorem 1.4 the letters are swapped again: the residual representation r̄ has coefficients of characteristic l, and genericity is tested on r̄|G_{F_v} for places v of F above a prime p ≠ l.
items.locator: ACC+ Definition 4.3.1(1), p. 972; hypothesis of Theorem 1.4, p. 1241

items.name: Decomposed genericity
items.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic p, L a number field and r: G_L → GL_n(k) a continuous representation. A prime l ≠ p is decomposed generic for r if l splits completely in L and r|G_{L_v} is generic (ACC+ Definition 4.3.1(1)) for every place v | l of L. r is decomposed generic if some prime l ≠ p is decomposed generic for r. The letters are those of ACC+, where k has characteristic p and the witness prime is l; just before Definition 4.3.1 (p. 972), ACC+ notes that 'the roles of p and l are reversed'. In Theorem 1.4 the roles are swapped. There r̄: G_F → GL_n(F̄_l) has coefficients of characteristic l. Its image is finite, so it takes values in GL_n(k) for a finite subfield k ⊂ F̄_l, and the condition does not depend on the choice of k. r̄ is decomposed generic if some prime p ≠ l splits completely in F and r̄|G_{F_v} is generic for every place v | p of F.
items.locator: ACC+ Definition 4.3.1(2)–(3), p. 972; hypothesis of Theorem 1.4, p. 1241

items.name: Enormous residual image
items.statement: For an algebraic extension k/F_p and absolutely irreducible H⊂GL_n(k), put ad0=ker(tr:End_k(k^n)→k) with conjugation action. H is enormous when it has no nontrivial p-power-order quotient, H^0(H,ad0)=H^1(H,ad0)=0, and for each simple k[H]-submodule W⊂ad0 there is regular semisimple h∈H with W^h≠0. This condition is not merely adequacy, and is impossible when p divides n.

items.name: Residual potential ordinary automorphy
items.statement: Let F be a CM number field, F^av/F a finite extension, n ≥ 2, l an odd prime, s ≥ 1, and r̄: G_F → GL_n(F_{l^s}) a continuous semisimple representation. Then there is a finite CM extension F'/F, Galois over F and linearly disjoint from F^av over F, such that r̄|G_{F'}, viewed with values in GL_n(F̄_l), is ι-ordinarily automorphic in the sense of Definition 1.3. The theorem prints only 'ordinarily automorphic'. Here ι: Q̄_l ≅ C is the isomorphism fixed in §1 just after the theorem (p. 1240), where it is introduced without a name and then written ι. The proof in §4 never specializes ι, so the conclusion holds for every choice of ι, and the proof of Theorem 1.4 uses it for the ι fixed there. No residual irreducibility, polarization, regularity or enormous-image hypothesis is imposed.

items.name: Potential ordinary automorphy of ordinary l-adic representations (for l > n)
items.statement: Let F be a CM number field, F^av/F a finite extension, n ≥ 2 an integer, l a prime with l > n, and ι: Q̄_l ≅ C. Let r: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_l) be a continuous representation with residual representation r̄: G_F → GL_n(F̄_l), and suppose: (1) r is unramified at all but finitely many places of F; (2) for each place v | l of F, r|G_{F_v} is potentially semistable and ordinary with regular Hodge–Tate weight in the sense of Definition 1.2; (3) r̄ is absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic (ACC+ Definition 4.3.1(3)), and r̄(G_{F(ζ_l)}) is enormous (ACC+ Definition 6.2.29); (4) there is σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_l)} such that r̄(σ) is a scalar. Then there is a finite CM extension F'/F, Galois over F and linearly disjoint from F^av over F, such that r|G_{F'} is ι-ordinarily automorphic. That is, r|G_{F'} ≅ r_{l,ι}(Π) for a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_n(A_{F'}) that is ι-ordinary at every place above l.
items.locator: Theorem 1.4, p. 1241; proof in the last paragraph of §4, p. 1274; the bound l > n is the second sentence of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2(4), p. 1030 (E2)
items.proofOutline: The residual representation r̄ has finite image, so it takes values in GL_n(F_{l^s}) for some s ≥ 1 (item 001). It is semisimple because it is absolutely irreducible. Run the proof of Theorem 1.1 (item 009) for this r̄, the given F^av and the isomorphism ι fixed in Theorem 1.4; that proof never specializes ι. Its avoidance field F^avoid is the normal closure over Q of F^av F^{ker r̄}(ζ_l) (p. 1268). The proof produces the CM field F' = L'EF^suff = FK, where K = L'LF^suff(ζ_N) is a finite Galois extension of Q (item 081). F' is Galois over F and F' ∩ F^avoid F^avoid_2 = F (p. 1272). The proof also gives χ̄_1^{-1}V[λ]_t ≅ r̄|G_{F'} with V_{λ,t} ⊗ χ_1^{-1} ι-ordinarily automorphic (pp. 1272–1273). So r̄|G_{F'} is ι-ordinarily automorphic for the fixed ι, which is condition (5) of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 over F'. Since F'/F is Galois and F' ∩ F^avoid = F, F' is linearly disjoint over F from F^avoid, and hence from F^av and from F^{ker r̄}(ζ_l). The theorem on linearly disjoint restriction then gives four properties of r|G_{F'}: it is unramified almost everywhere; it is potentially semistable and ordinary at every place w | l of F', with the restricted weight; r̄(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) = r̄(G_{F(ζ_l)}) is enormous; and r̄(σ') is a scalar for some σ' ∈ G_{F'} − G_{F'(ζ_l)}. The computation on p. 1274 gives K ∩ F^avoid = Q. As F^avoid is Galois over Q, K is linearly disjoint over Q from F^avoid, which contains the normal closure over Q of F^{ker r̄}(ζ_l). ACC+ Lemma 7.1.7 (item 089) then shows that r̄|G_{FK} = r̄|G_{F'} is absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic. The hypothesis l > n supplies the rest of condition (4). Apply ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 (item 072) to F', p = l and ρ = r|G_{F'}. It gives r|G_{F'} ≅ r_{l,ι}(Π) for a regular algebraic cuspidal Π that is ι-ordinary at every place above l, so r|G_{F'} is ι-ordinarily automorphic (item 005).
items.note: Missing. Routed to ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 ('Potential automorphy assembly'), together with Theorem 1.1 (item 009); ML.2's acceptance criterion is automorphy after the specified extension. The item states Theorem 1.4 for l > n, the range in which its proof applies. Condition (4) of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 (p. 1030) includes 'We have p > n', and the proof takes p = l. The printed Theorem 1.4 assumes only that l is odd. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, name, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Linear disjointness
items.statement: For subextensions A,B of an ambient field over C, A and B are linearly disjoint if their multiplication map A⊗_C B→AB is injective; equivalently a C-linearly independent family in A remains B-linearly independent.

items.name: Disjointness and intersection for finite Galois extensions
items.statement: Let A and B be extensions of C inside a common field. If A and B are linearly disjoint over C, then A ∩ B = C. Conversely, if A ∩ B = C, both A and B are finite over C, and one of them is Galois over C, then A and B are linearly disjoint over C.

items.name: Base change of linear disjointness
items.statement: Let A, B, C and D be subfields of a common field with C ⊂ B ⊂ A and C ⊂ D. If A and D are linearly disjoint over C, then A and BD are linearly disjoint over B; in particular A ∩ BD = B.

items.name: Roots of finite-field-valued characters with avoidance
items.statement: Let M be a CM field, F_0/Q a finite Galois extension, l an odd prime and k a finite field of characteristic l. Let n be a positive integer, written n = l^a m with l ∤ m, and suppose m | #k − 1 (equivalently, k contains all n-th roots of unity of an algebraic closure). Let χ: G_M → k^× be a continuous character with values in the subgroup (k^×)^n of n-th powers. Then there are a finite totally real Galois extension L/Q, linearly disjoint from F_0 over Q, and a continuous character ψ: G_{LM} → k^× with ψ^n = χ|_{G_{LM}}.
items.locator: Lemma 2.1, p. 1244; proof pp. 1244–1248 (for the roots-of-unity condition as used in §4, see E5)

uses.how: Input to Residual potential ordinary automorphy.
Input to Simultaneous determinant twists and CRT representation.

items.proofOutline: Since x ↦ x^{l^a} is an automorphism of k^×, the n-th power map k^× → (k^×)^n is surjective with kernel μ_m(k) ≅ Z/mZ. Hence χ|_{G_{F_1}} has an n-th root exactly when δ(χ) ∈ H^2(G_M, Z/mZ) restricts to 0 on G_{F_1}. First step: δ(χ) has nonzero localization at only finitely many places. Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemma 4.1.2 gives a totally real Galois L_2, linearly disjoint from F_0, whose completions above the relevant rational primes make [F_{2,w} : M_v(ζ_m)] divisible by m. Then, over F_2 = ML_2, the restriction of δ(χ) lies in Ш^2(F_2, Z/mZ). Second step: write m = 2^r m′ with m′ odd. The same lemma gives a totally real Galois L_1, linearly disjoint from F_0F_2(μ_{2^r}), with a completion of even degree over F_2 at one prime. For F_1 = F_2L_1, (2.1) shows that corestriction kills Ш^1(F_1, μ_m), and Poitou–Tate duality then kills the restriction of Ш^2(F_2, Z/mZ) to F_1. Finally, L = L_1L_2 meets F_0 only in Q by the tower property of linear disjointness, so it is linearly disjoint from F_0.
items.note: Because k^× is cyclic of order prime to l, x ↦ x^{l^a} is an automorphism of k^×. So (k^×)^n = (k^×)^m, and μ_n(k) = μ_m(k) has order m; only the prime-to-l part m of n matters. The field LM, written F_1 in the paper, is again a CM field. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Continuous first cohomology carrier
items.statement: Let G be a topological group acting continuously on a topological abelian group M. The continuous 1-cocycles are the continuous maps f: G → M with f(gh) = f(g) + g·f(h) for all g, h ∈ G. The 1-coboundaries are the maps g ↦ g·x − x for x ∈ M, and H^1(G, M) = Z^1/B^1 is the quotient group. In the paper G is a Galois group with its Krull topology and M is a finite discrete module; only the group structure of H^1 is used.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 2.1, pp. 1245–1247, and of Lemma 2.2, p. 1247 (first cohomology of Galois groups with finite coefficients)

items.name: Character-root obstruction
items.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic l and n a positive integer, written n = l^a m with l ∤ m, and suppose m | #k − 1. Then x ↦ x^n maps k^× onto its subgroup (k^×)^n of n-th powers, with kernel μ_m(k) ≅ Z/mZ. So for every profinite group G, in particular G = G_M, there is a short exact sequence 0 → Z/mZ → k^× → (k^×)^n → 0 of discrete G-modules with trivial action. For a continuous character χ: G → (k^×)^n, regarded as a class in H^1(G, (k^×)^n), let δ(χ) ∈ H^2(G, Z/mZ) be its image under the connecting map. Then χ = ψ^n for a continuous character ψ: G → k^× if and only if δ(χ) = 0. Since δ commutes with restriction, for a closed subgroup H ⊂ G the restriction χ|_H has a continuous n-th root if and only if δ(χ) restricts to 0 in H^2(H, Z/mZ). When m = 1 the power map is bijective and δ(χ) = 0.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1, pp. 1244–1245 (the short exact sequence of trivial G_M-modules and the segment H^1(G_M, F_{l^r}^×) → H^1(G_M, (F_{l^r}^×)^m) → H^2(G_M, Z/mZ) of its long exact sequence)

items.name: Locally trivial global cohomology
items.statement: For a number field K and a discrete G_K-module A (finite in every use in the paper), Ш^i(K, A) = ker(H^i(G_K, A) → ∏_v H^i(G_{K_v}, A)), where the product runs over all places v of K, archimedean ones included. For a finite Galois extension K′/K such that G_{K′} acts trivially on A, Ш^1(K′/K, A) is the kernel of H^1(Gal(K′/K), A) → ∏_v H^1(Gal(K′_w/K_v), A), where w is a place of K′ above v. The paper uses it for K′ = K(μ_{p^r}) and A = μ_{p^r}.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1, p. 1246 (definition of Ш^i); proof of Lemma 2.2, p. 1247 (the relative group Ш^1(K/F, μ_{p^r}))

items.name: Finite support and local killing of a root obstruction
items.statement: Let M be a number field, m a positive integer and x ∈ H^2(G_M, Z/mZ), with trivial action. Then x is inflated from H^2(Gal(M′/M), Z/mZ) for some finite Galois extension M′/M. Its localization x_v ∈ H^2(G_{M_v}, Z/mZ) vanishes at every finite place v of M unramified in M′: there x_v is inflated from H^2(Gal(M_v^nr/M_v), Z/mZ), which is 0 because Gal(M_v^nr/M_v) ≅ Ẑ has cohomological dimension 1. Hence x_v ≠ 0 for only finitely many places v. Moreover, let v be a finite place and K a finite extension of M_v(ζ_m) with m | [K : M_v(ζ_m)]; then the restriction of x_v to G_K is 0. Indeed, over M_v(ζ_m) one has Z/mZ ≅ μ_m, the local invariant identifies H^2(G_{M_v(ζ_m)}, μ_m) with (1/m)Z/Z, and restriction to G_K multiplies the invariant by [K : M_v(ζ_m)].
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1, first step, p. 1245

uses.how: Input to Roots of finite-field-valued characters with avoidance.

items.proofOutline: Inflate the class from a finite Galois quotient Gal(M′/M). At a finite place unramified in M′, its localization is inflated from Gal(M_v^nr/M_v) ≅ Ẑ, whose second cohomology with finite coefficients vanishes, so only finitely many localizations are nonzero. At each remaining finite place, restrict first to M_v(ζ_m), where Z/mZ ≅ μ_m and the local invariant identifies H^2 with (1/m)Z/Z. Then use that restriction to a finite extension multiplies the invariant by the degree.
items.note: Every class in H² of a profinite group with discrete coefficients is inflated from the quotient by some open normal subgroup; Tau Ceti proves this at the pinned commit (TauCeti.ContCohomology.exists_explicitInfl2_eq). The other inputs are planned. The vanishing of H²(Ẑ, M) for finite M is in Layer 11 of 'Continuous cohomology of profinite groups'. The exact sequence 1 → I_K → G_K → Ẑ → 1 for a local field K is in Layer 4 of 'Local fields and ramification'; it sends the decomposition group at a place unramified in the finite quotient through Gal(K^nr/K) ≅ Ẑ. The isomorphism H²(K, μ_m) ≅ Z/mZ and the square in which restriction multiplies the invariant by the degree are in Layer 5 of 'Class field theory'. Combining them also uses the compatibility of inflation with restriction to decomposition groups. The construction of totally real fields with prescribed local extensions (Clozel–Harris–Taylor, Lemma 4.1.2) is a separate input and is not part of this statement. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, status, planning stages, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Poitou–Tate pairing and transfer adjunction
items.statement: Let K be a number field with no real places and m a positive integer. Then there is a perfect pairing ⟨·,·⟩: Ш^1(K, μ_m) × Ш^2(K, Z/mZ) → Q/Z (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Theorem 8.6.7). Let L/K be a finite extension. Corestriction maps Ш^1(L, μ_m) into Ш^1(K, μ_m), restriction maps Ш^2(K, Z/mZ) into Ш^2(L, Z/mZ), and ⟨x, Res y⟩_L = ⟨Cor x, y⟩_K for all x ∈ Ш^1(L, μ_m) and y ∈ Ш^2(K, Z/mZ). The condition on real places holds for the CM fields to which the proof of Lemma 2.1 applies the duality.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1, p. 1246, citing Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Cohomology of Number Fields, Theorem 8.6.7

items.proofOutline: Over K′ the module μ_{p^r} is trivial, so a class in Ш^1(K′, μ_{p^r}) is a homomorphism G_{K′} → Z/p^rZ that is trivial on every decomposition group. Its fixed field is a cyclic extension of K′ in which every place splits completely, hence trivial by the Chebotarev density theorem. The inflation–restriction sequences for G_{K′} ⊂ G_K and for G_{K′_w} ⊂ G_{K_v} then show, by a diagram chase, that inflation maps Ш^1(K′/K, μ_{p^r}) isomorphically onto Ш^1(K, μ_{p^r}).
items.note: Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Killing the remaining two-primary obstruction
items.statement: Let K be a number field with no real places and m a positive integer, and write m = 2^r m′ with m′ odd. Let L/K be a finite extension of even degree that is linearly disjoint from K(μ_{2^r}) over K. Then corestriction H^1(G_L, μ_m) → H^1(G_K, μ_m) vanishes on Ш^1(L, μ_m). Indeed, the odd-primary part of Ш^1(L, μ_m) is zero, and its 2-primary part is inflated from H^1(Gal(L(μ_{2^r})/L), μ_{2^r}). Restriction identifies H^1(Gal(K(μ_{2^r})/K), μ_{2^r}) with that group, which is killed by 2. Finally, Cor ∘ Res is multiplication by the even integer [L : K]. Consequently, the compatibility ⟨x, Res y⟩ = ⟨Cor x, y⟩ and the perfectness of the Poitou–Tate pairing over L show that restriction Ш^2(K, Z/mZ) → Ш^2(L, Z/mZ) is zero. In Lemma 2.1, K = F_2 and L = F_2L_1. Here L_1 is totally real, Galois over Q and linearly disjoint from F_0F_2(μ_{2^r}) over Q, and its completion at one prime p is prescribed so that 2 | [L : K].
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1: equation (2.1), p. 1247, and the construction of L_1, p. 1248

uses.how: Input to Roots of finite-field-valued characters with avoidance.

items.proofOutline: Since L and K(μ_{2^r}) are linearly disjoint over K, L ∩ K(μ_{2^r}) = K, and restriction identifies Gal(L(μ_{2^r})/L) with Gal(K(μ_{2^r})/K). By Lemma 2.2, the odd-primary part of Ш^1(L, μ_m) vanishes, and its 2-primary part is inflated from H^1(Gal(L(μ_{2^r})/L), μ_{2^r}). It is therefore the restriction of a class inflated from H^1(Gal(K(μ_{2^r})/K), μ_{2^r}). This group is killed by 2 and Cor ∘ Res = [L : K] is even, so Cor = 0 on Ш^1(L, μ_m). Then ⟨x, Res y⟩_L = ⟨Cor x, y⟩_K = 0 for all x ∈ Ш^1(L, μ_m), and perfectness of the pairing over L gives Res y = 0 for every y ∈ Ш^2(K, Z/mZ).
items.note: Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Auxiliary modulus with prescribed order and nonunitary condition
items.statement: Let l be a rational prime, s a positive integer and S a finite set of rational primes. Then there is a positive integer N, divisible neither by l nor by any prime in S, such that the order r of l modulo N (the least r ≥ 1 with N | l^r − 1) is divisible by s, and N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1 when r is even. The proof writes s = 2^{a_0} ∏_{i=1}^{m} p_i^{a_i} and takes N = M_0M_1⋯M_m. The M_i are pairwise coprime, and l has order p_i^{t_i} modulo M_i, with p_0 = 2 and t_i ≥ a_i. The factor M_0 is AB for odd primes A | l^{2^{t_0−2}} + 1 and B | l^{2^{t_0−1}} + 1. This parity step uses that l is odd, the standing convention of §2. When s ≥ 2 one has r ≥ 2 and hence N > 1. Putting every prime below a bound into S therefore forces N above that bound; this gives the condition N > 100n + 100 at the start of §4.
items.locator: Lemma 2.3, p. 1248; proof pp. 1248–1250 (misprint E4 on p. 1250); applied at the start of §4, p. 1268

items.name: Labelled period functors
items.statement: Let K/Q_l be a finite extension with maximal unramified subfield K_0, and let r be a continuous representation of G_K on a finite-dimensional Q̄_l-vector space. For an embedding τ: K_0 → Q̄_l, put D_cris,τ(r) = (r ⊗_{τ,K_0} B_cris)^{G_K} and D_st,τ(r) = (r ⊗_{τ,K_0} B_st)^{G_K}. The Frobenius φ of B_cris and B_st is semilinear with respect to the Frobenius of K_0, so it does not induce an operator on these τ-parts. Its power φ^{[K_0:Q_l]} does, acting Q̄_l-linearly, and the monodromy operator N acts Q̄_l-linearly on D_st,τ(r). The characteristic polynomial of φ^{[K_0:Q_l]} on D_cris,τ(r) does not depend on τ. For an embedding τ: K → Q̄_l, the labelled de Rham module (r ⊗_{τ,K} B_dR)^{G_K} carries the filtration induced from B_dR; its graded pieces gr^i are the ones used in Lemma 2.4.

items.name: Crystalline slope criterion for regular ordinarity
items.statement: Let F be a number field, l a prime, n a positive integer and a = (a_{τ,j}) ∈ (Z^n)^{Hom(F,Q̄_l),+}, so that a_{τ,1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ a_{τ,n} for every embedding τ: F → Q̄_l. Let r: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_l) be a continuous representation that is crystalline at every place v | l; regard v also as the normalized valuation v: F_v^× ↠ Z. Suppose that for every v | l and every τ: F → Q̄_l above v, dim_{Q̄_l} gr^i (r ⊗_{τ,F_v} B_dR)^{G_{F_v}} is 1 if i = a_{τ,j} + n − j for some j ∈ {1, …, n}, and 0 otherwise. For v | l, let F_v^0 be the maximal unramified subextension of F_v. Let α_{v,1}, …, α_{v,n} be the roots of the characteristic polynomial of φ^{[F_v^0:Q_l]} on (r ⊗_{τ,F_v^0} B_cris)^{G_{F_v}} for any τ: F_v^0 → Q̄_l; this polynomial does not depend on τ. Let val_v be the valuation on Q̄_l with val_v(l) = v(l), and order the roots so that val_v(α_{v,1}) ≥ ⋯ ≥ val_v(α_{v,n}). Then r is ordinary of weight a if and only if val_v(α_{v,i}) = Σ_τ (a_{τ,i} + n − i) for every v | l and every i = 1, …, n, where τ runs over the embeddings F → Q̄_l above v.
items.locator: Lemma 2.4, p. 1250, quoted from Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor, Lemma 2.2(1) (author PDF pp. 17–18), which that paper attributes to Geraghty's Lemma 2.7.6

items.name: Enormity of symmetric powers after restriction
items.statement: Let F/Q be a finite extension with normal closure F̃, n a positive integer, l > 2n + 5 a prime, and r̄: G_F → GL_2(F̄_l) a continuous representation with r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊃ SL_2(F_l). If F_1/F is a finite extension linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄} over F, then (Sym^{n−1} r̄)(G_{F_1(ζ_l)}) is enormous. For n ≥ 2 this is ACC+ Lemma 7.1.6(2) with m = n − 1, which needs only l > 2n + 1. For n = 1 the image is the trivial subgroup of GL_1 and the assertion holds trivially.
items.locator: Lemma 2.6(1), p. 1251, proved by citing ACC+ Lemma 7.1.6(2) (published p. 1090)

uses.how: Input to Decomposed genericity of symmetric powers under avoidance.
Input to Automorphy of the auxiliary-prime Dwork realization.

items.proofOutline: For n ≥ 2: linear disjointness from F̄^{ker r̄} gives r̄(G_{F_1}) = r̄(G_F) ⊃ r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊃ SL_2(F_l). Since SL_2(F_l) is perfect and Gal(F_1(ζ_l)/F_1) is abelian, r̄(G_{F_1(ζ_l)}) ⊃ SL_2(F_l). ACC+ Lemma 7.1.4 then shows that (Sym^{n−1} r̄)(G_{F_1(ζ_l)}) is enormous. For n = 1 the image is trivial and ad⁰ = 0.
items.note: Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, proof outline.

items.name: Decomposed genericity of symmetric powers under avoidance
items.statement: Let F/Q be a finite extension with normal closure F̃, n a positive integer, l > 2n + 5 a prime, and r̄: G_F → GL_2(F̄_l) a continuous representation with r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊃ SL_2(F_l). Put H = F̃ · F̄^{ker ad r̄}, and let H′ be the normal closure of H over Q. Let F_1/F be a finite Galois extension that is linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄} over F and linearly disjoint from H′ over F. Then Sym^{n−1} r̄|_{G_{F_1}} is decomposed generic. For n = 1 this is immediate, since Sym^0 r̄ is the trivial character; for n ≥ 2 the proof rests on ACC+ Lemma 7.1.6(3) with m = n − 1.

uses.how: Input to Automorphy of the auxiliary-prime Dwork realization.

items.proofOutline: If a finite extension of F_1 is decomposed generic, so is F_1, so F_1 may be enlarged; replace F by its normal closure. By Dickson's theorem ad r̄(G_F) is PSL_2(k) or PGL_2(k); take E/F of degree at most 2 with ad r̄(G_E) = PSL_2(k). The normal closure Ẽ of E over Q has Gal(Ẽ/E) an elementary abelian 2-group. Hence Ẽ is linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker ad r̄} over E, and ẼF_1 is linearly disjoint from H′ over Ẽ. One may therefore assume that F is Galois over Q and ad r̄(G_F) = PSL_2(k). Take a chain F = F′_0 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ F′_s = F_1 in which each step is Galois with simple group. If H ∩ F̃′_s = F, ACC+ Lemma 7.1.6(3) applies. Otherwise let i be least with H ∩ F̃′_i ≠ F. Then H ⊂ F̃′_i and Gal(F̃′_i/F̃′_{i−1}) ≅ PSL_2(k)^m. Because PSL_2(k) has trivial centre, some σ ∈ G_Q satisfies σH ⊂ F′_iF̃′_{i−1}, and a second use of the trivial centre gives σH ⊂ F′_i ⊂ F_1. This contradicts the linear disjointness of F_1 and H′ over F.
items.note: The paper's proof runs as follows. It suffices to prove decomposed genericity after a finite extension of F_1, and one may assume F is Galois over Q. By Dickson's theorem (Darmon–Diamond–Taylor, Theorem 2.47(b)), ad r̄(G_F) is conjugate to PSL_2(k) or PGL_2(k) for a finite extension k/F_l. Take E/F of degree at most 2 with ad r̄(G_E) = PSL_2(k). The normal closure Ẽ of E over Q is a compositum of extensions of F of degree at most 2, so Gal(Ẽ/E) is an elementary abelian 2-group. Comparing simple factors shows that F̄^{ker ad r̄} and Ẽ are linearly disjoint over E, so ad r̄(G_Ẽ) = PSL_2(k), and ẼF_1 is linearly disjoint from H′ over Ẽ. Replacing F by Ẽ and F_1 by ẼF_1, one may assume F is Galois over Q and ad r̄(G_F) = PSL_2(k). Take a chain F = F′_0 ⊂ … ⊂ F′_s = F_1 in which each F′_i/F′_{i−1} is Galois with simple group Δ_i. If H ∩ F̃′_s = F, ACC+ Lemma 7.1.6(3) applies. Otherwise let i be least with H ∩ F̃′_i ≠ F. Simplicity of PSL_2(k) gives H ⊂ F̃′_i, and Gal(F̃′_i/F̃′_{i−1}) ≅ Δ_i^m with Δ_i ≅ PSL_2(k). Because PSL_2(k) has trivial centre, there is σ ∈ G_Q with σH ⊂ F′_iF̃′_{i−1}, and a second use of the trivial centre gives σH ⊂ F′_i ⊂ F_1. Since σH ⊂ H′ and σH ≠ F, this contradicts the linear disjointness of F_1 and H′ over F. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Goursat's subdirect-product theorem
items.statement: Let G and H be groups and I ⊂ G × H a subgroup whose projections to G and to H are surjective. Put G_0 = {g ∈ G : (g, 1) ∈ I} and H_0 = {h ∈ H : (1, h) ∈ I}. Then G_0 is normal in G, H_0 is normal in H, and there is an isomorphism φ: G/G_0 → H/H_0 such that the image of I in G/G_0 × H/H_0 is the graph of φ. Since I contains G_0 × H_0, I is the full inverse image of this graph.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 2.6(2), p. 1251, and of Proposition 3.8, p. 1261

items.name: Dwork pencil and smooth base
items.statement: Let l be an odd prime, n ≥ 2 an integer, and N an odd integer prime to ln with N > 100n + 100; let F be a CM field containing ζ_N. Let T_0 = P^1 − ({∞} ∪ μ_N) over Z[1/N], with coordinate t, and let Y ⊂ P^{N−1} × T_0 be the projective family X_1^N + X_2^N + ⋯ + X_N^N = N t X_1X_2⋯X_N. items.name: The asymmetric exponent multiset
items.statement: Fix the character χ: H_0 → μ_N, χ(ξ_1, …, ξ_N) = ∏_{i=1}^N ξ_i^{a_i}, where (a_1, …, a_N) = (1, 2, 4, 5, …, (N − n + 2)/2, (N + n − 2)/2, …, N − 5, N − 4, N − 3, 0, …, 0) if n > 2 is odd; (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, …, (N − n + 3)/2, (N + n − 3)/2, (N + n − 1)/2, …, N − 4, 0, …, 0) if n > 2 is even; and (1, 2, …, (N − 3)/2, 0, 0, 0, (N + 3)/2, …, N − 1) if n = 2. Each vector has length N and ∑ a_i ≡ 0 mod N, so χ is well defined on H_0. For n > 2, 0 occurs exactly n + 1 times, every nonzero residue occurs at most once, and the residues 3, N − 2, N − 1 (n odd), resp. 6, N − 3, N − 2, N − 1 (n even), do not occur.

items.name: Complementary character indices
items.statement: Let (a_1, …, a_N) be the exponent vector of item 031 and B = {b ∈ Z/NZ : b + a_j ≢ 0 mod N for every j}. The a_j take exactly N − n distinct values mod N, so B has exactly n elements b_1, …, b_n; only the set B is determined, not an ordering of it. Explicitly, B = {1, 2, N − 3} ∪ {(N + x)/2 : x = −n + 4, −n + 6, …, n − 4} if n > 2 is odd; B = {1, 2, 3, N − 6} ∪ {(N + x)/2 : x = −n + 5, −n + 7, …, n − 5} if n > 2 is even; and B = {(N − 1)/2, (N + 1)/2} if n = 2. For n = 3 and n = 4 the middle ranges are empty, so B = {1, 2, N − 3} and B = {1, 2, 3, N − 6} respectively. In every case 0 ∉ B and ∑_{b∈B} b ≡ 0 mod N.

items.name: Trivial multiplicative stabilizer of the asymmetric indices
items.statement: Let n > 2, let N be odd with N > 100n + 100, and let B ⊂ Z/NZ be the set of item 032. If α ∈ (Z/NZ)^× satisfies αB = B, then α = 1. In particular −B ≠ B. For n = 2, by contrast, B = {(N − 1)/2, (N + 1)/2} satisfies −B = B.

uses.how: Input to Full special-linear monodromy on the punctured line.

items.proofOutline: Since 1 ∈ B, α = α·1 ∈ B. Let n be even. If α ∈ {2, 3, N − 6}, then 2α, 3α or (N − 6)α, that is 4, 9 or 36, would lie in B. But 3 < 4, 9, 36 < (N − n + 5)/2, and none of them is N − 6. This settles n = 4. For n ≥ 6, let α = (N + x)/2 with x odd and |x| ≤ n − 5. Then x ≡ 2α lies in B. Since B meets {1, 3, …, n − 5} ∪ {N − n + 5, N − n + 7, …, N − 1} only in {1, 3}, x ∈ {1, 3}. As (N − x)/2 ∈ B, α(N − x)/2 ≡ −x²/4 lies in B, so N − 1 or N − 9 lies in 4B. As residues in {0, …, N − 1}, 4B ⊂ {2, 6, …, 2n − 10} ∪ {N − (2n − 10), N − (2n − 14), …, N − 2} ∪ {4, 8, 12, N − 24}. But N − 1 and N − 9 exceed 2n − 10 and 12, and they are even while the remaining elements are odd; this is a contradiction. For n odd the same argument uses the elements 2 and N − 3 of B, which exclude α = 2 and α = N − 3 because 4, 9 ∉ B. It uses |x| ≤ n − 4 with x ∈ {1, −3}, and 4B ⊂ {2, 6, …, 2n − 8} ∪ {N − (2n − 8), …, N − 2} ∪ {4, 8, N − 12}.

items.name: Integral and finite étale Dwork eigensheaves
items.statement: Let n > 2. For a prime λ of Z[1/2N, ζ_N] of residue characteristic l, let V_λ = (R^{N−2}π_*Z[ζ_N]_λ)^{χ,H_0}. This is the lisse sheaf on (T_0 × Spec Z[1/2Nl, ζ_N])_et given by the direct summand of R^{N−2}π_*Z[ζ_N]_λ on which H_0 acts through χ. For a nonzero ideal 𝔫 of Z[1/2N, ζ_N] of norm M, let V[𝔫] = (R^{N−2}π_*(Z[ζ_N]/𝔫))^{χ,H_0}, the corresponding lisse sheaf on (T_0 × Spec Z[1/2NM, ζ_N])_et. Both summands are cut out by the idempotent (1/#H_0) ∑_{ξ∈H_0} χ(ξ)^{−1}ξ. It is defined because #H_0 = N^{N−2} is invertible in Z[ζ_N]_λ and in Z[ζ_N]/𝔫.

items.name: Rank-two real forms of the Dwork eigensheaves
items.statement: For n = 2 the exponent vector is that of BLGHT §4 with their n = 2. The same χ-eigensheaf formulas define U_λ and U[𝔫] (λ a prime, 𝔫 a nonzero ideal of Z[1/2N, ζ_N]^+) and U_B, with fibre decompositions U_{λ,0} = ⊕ U_{λ,i} and U[𝔫]_0 = ⊕ U_i[𝔫]. In their place one uses BLGHT's sheaves V_λ, V[𝔫] and V_B. These are cut out by an idempotent in the group algebra over Z[1/2N, ζ_N]^+ of H_0 ⋊ ⟨ς⟩, where ς is the automorphism X_j ↦ X_{N+1−j} of Y. Their coefficients are Z[1/2N, ζ_N]^+_λ, Z[1/2N, ζ_N]^+/𝔫 and Z[1/2N, ζ_N]^+ respectively; the idempotent requires 2N to be invertible. They carry perfect alternating pairings (with a Tate twist for V_λ and V[𝔫]), and V_λ and V[𝔫] are locally free of rank 2 (BLGHT Lemma 4.1(2)). Extension of scalars from Z[1/2N, ζ_N]^+ to Z[1/2N, ζ_N], followed by H_0-equivariant projection, gives isomorphisms onto U_λ, U[𝔫] and U_B ⊗ Z[1/2N] respectively. From then on V_λ, V[𝔫] and V_B denote these objects when n = 2. The residue fields k(λ) are those of the real cyclotomic ring, and their degree over F_l need not be the order of l modulo N.
items.locator: §3, p. 1255 (U_λ, U[𝔫]), p. 1256 (U_B) and the paragraph after Proposition 3.2, p. 1257; BLGHT §4 and Lemma 4.1

items.name: Fermat-fibre character splitting
items.statement: Since H acts on Y_0, the fibres at t = 0 decompose as V_{λ,0} = ⊕_{i∈Z/NZ} V_{λ,i} and V[𝔫]_0 = ⊕_{i∈Z/NZ} V_i[𝔫]. Here V_{λ,i} and V_i[𝔫] are the summands on which H acts through the character χ_i: ξ ↦ ∏_{j=1}^N ξ_j^{a_j+i}, whose restriction to H_0 is χ. The same decomposition holds for V_{B,0} after inverting N, and for the χ-part of H^{N−2}_{dR}(Y_0/K) for any field K of characteristic 0 containing ζ_N. For n = 2 it holds for U_{λ,0} = ⊕ U_{λ,i} and U[𝔫]_0 = ⊕ U_i[𝔫]. The summand of index i is nonzero if and only if i + a_j ≢ 0 mod N for every j, that is, i ∈ B. It then has rank one, and is free over Z[ζ_N]_λ, resp. Z[ζ_N]/𝔫.
items.locator: §3, decomposition of the fibres at t = 0, pp. 1255–1256; nonvanishing and rank of the summands in the proof of Lemma 3.3(1), p. 1257, citing Deligne, Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, Proposition 7.4

items.name: Betti realization and comparison
items.statement: Fix τ: Q(ζ_N) ↪ C with τ(ζ_N) = e^{2πi/N}, and let π̃: Y(C) → T_0(C) be the base change of π along τ, viewed as a map of complex analytic spaces. For n > 2 let V_B = (R^{N−2}π̃_*Z[ζ_N])^{χ,H_0}, a locally constant sheaf of Z[ζ_N]-modules on T_0(C); for n = 2 the same formula defines U_B. Let τ also denote the induced base change (T_0)_C → T_0 × Spec Z[1/2NMl, ζ_N]. Then V_B ⊗_{Z[ζ_N]} Z[ζ_N]_λ corresponds to τ^*V_λ under the equivalence between locally constant analytic Z[ζ_N]_λ-sheaves on T_0(C) and locally constant étale Z[ζ_N]_λ-sheaves on (T_0)_C. In the same way V_B ⊗_{Z[ζ_N]} Z[ζ_N]/𝔫 corresponds to τ^*V[𝔫]. For n = 2 the same relations hold between BLGHT's real forms V_B, V_λ and V[𝔫] of item 035, with coefficients in Z[1/2N, ζ_N]^+ (BLGHT §4).

items.name: The three-punctured-line cover
items.statement: Let n > 2. Let T_0' = P^1 − {0, 1, ∞} with coordinate t', and let Y' ⊂ P^{N−1} × T_0' be the projective family X_1'^N + ⋯ + X_{N−1}'^N + t'^{−1}X_N'^N = N X_1'⋯X_N'. The map t ↦ t' = t^N is an N-fold Galois covering T_0 − {0} → T_0'. Setting X_i' = X_i (i < N) and X_N' = tX_N identifies the pullback of π': Y' → T_0' along this covering with π: Y − Y_0 → T_0 − {0}. Over Z[1/N, ζ_N], H_0 acts on Y' by (ξ_1, …, ξ_N)(X_1', …, X_N', t') = (ξ_1X_1', …, ξ_NX_N', t'), compatibly with its action on Y − Y_0. With π̃': Y'(C) → T_0'(C) the base change along τ, put V_B' = (R^{N−2}π̃'_*Z[ζ_N])^{χ,H_0}. Its pullback along T_0(C) − {0} → T_0'(C) is naturally identified with the restriction of V_B to T_0(C) − {0}. For n = 2 this family is not stable under ς: X_j ↦ X_{N+1−j}. One uses instead BLGHT's family Ỹ ⊂ P^{N−1} × T_0' given by X̃_1^N + ⋯ + X̃_{(N−1)/2}^N + t'^{−1}X̃_{(N+1)/2}^N + X̃_{(N+3)/2}^N + ⋯ + X̃_N^N = N X̃_1⋯X̃_N. Its pullback is identified with Y − Y_0 by X̃_{(N+1)/2} = tX_{(N+1)/2} and X̃_j = X_j (j ≠ (N + 1)/2), and it is stable under ς̃: X̃_j ↦ X̃_{N+1−j}. Its real-coefficient local system Ṽ_B on T_0'(C) pulls back to BLGHT's V_B on T_0(C) − {0} (BLGHT §4).
items.locator: §3, the family Y' over T_0' = P^1 − {0, 1, ∞} and the local system V_B', p. 1256; for n = 2, BLGHT §4 (the family Ỹ and the local system Ṽ_B), used through BLGHT Lemma 4.6 in the proof of Lemma 3.7, p. 1259

items.name: Rank of the étale eigensheaf
items.statement: For n > 2 and every prime λ of Z[1/2N, ζ_N] of residue characteristic l, V_λ is a locally free sheaf of Z[ζ_N]_λ-modules of rank n on T_0 × Spec Z[1/2Nl, ζ_N]. For n = 2, the corresponding statement for BLGHT's V_λ over Z[1/2N, ζ_N]^+_λ is BLGHT Lemma 4.1(2).

items.proofOutline: By smooth and proper base change, R^{N−2}π_*Z[ζ_N]_λ is lisse on the connected base T_0 × Spec Z[1/2Nl, ζ_N], so its stalks at all geometric points are isomorphic. At a complex point s the stalk is H^{N−2}(Y_s(C), Z) ⊗ Z[ζ_N]_λ by Artin's comparison theorem. The integral cohomology of a smooth hypersurface in P^{N−1} is torsion-free (Lefschetz hyperplane theorem and Poincaré duality), so the stalks are free. Since #H_0 = N^{N−2} is invertible in Z[ζ_N]_λ, V_λ is a direct summand and hence locally free. Its rank is constant, and it equals n at t = 0 by the Fermat computation (item 036; Deligne, Hodge cycles, Proposition 7.4).
items.note: The printed proof derives local freeness from smoothness and properness alone. The torsion-freeness of the integral cohomology of the smooth fibres is also needed (E24). The same remark applies to V[𝔫], V_B and V_B'. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, proof outline.

items.name: Rank of the finite-coefficient eigensheaf
items.statement: For n > 2 and every nonzero ideal 𝔫 of Z[1/2N, ζ_N] of norm M, V[𝔫] is a locally free sheaf of Z[ζ_N]/𝔫-modules of rank n on T_0 × Spec Z[1/2NM, ζ_N]. This includes 𝔫 = 𝔓_1𝔓_2 with 𝔓_1, 𝔓_2 of distinct residue characteristics, as used in Proposition 3.8. For n = 2, the corresponding statement over Z[1/2N, ζ_N]^+/𝔫 is BLGHT Lemma 4.1(2).
items.locator: Proposition 3.2, assertion for V[𝔫], p. 1257

uses.how: Input to Fixed-determinant isomorphism torsor.

items.proofOutline: R^{N−2}π_*(Z[ζ_N]/𝔫) is lisse by smooth and proper base change. Write 𝔫 = ∏ λ^{a_λ}, so that Z[ζ_N]/𝔫 = ∏_λ Z[ζ_N]_λ/λ^{a_λ}. The integral cohomology of the fibres is torsion-free in degrees N − 2 and N − 1 (see item 039), so R^{N−2}π_*(Z[ζ_N]_λ/λ^{a_λ}) = R^{N−2}π_*Z[ζ_N]_λ ⊗ Z[ζ_N]_λ/λ^{a_λ}. The χ-summand is cut out by the same idempotent. Hence V[𝔫] ≅ ∏_λ V_λ/λ^{a_λ}, with V_λ defined by the same formula for each prime λ dividing 𝔫, and this is locally free of rank n by item 039.
items.note: Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, proof outline.

items.statement: For n > 2, V_B is a locally free sheaf of Z[ζ_N]-modules of rank n on T_0(C); its stalk V_{B,t} carries the monodromy representation ρ_t. For n = 2, V_B is replaced by BLGHT's real-coefficient local system (item 035).

items.proofOutline: π̃ is a proper submersion, so R^{N−2}π̃_*Z[ζ_N] is locally constant. Its stalks H^{N−2}(Y_s(C), Z) ⊗ Z[ζ_N] are torsion-free (Lefschetz hyperplane theorem and Poincaré duality). The χ-eigenmodule of such a stalk is a finitely generated torsion-free, hence projective, Z[ζ_N]-module. Its rank is constant on the connected space T_0(C) and equals n at t = 0 (item 036). For n = 2 the same argument applies to BLGHT's real form V_B (item 035).

items.name: Monodromy generators with fixed orientation
items.statement: Let n > 2. Fix a base point t ∈ T_0(C) − {0} and let t' = t^N be its image in T_0'(C). Let ρ_t: π_1(T_0(C), t) → GL(V_{B,t}) and ρ_{t'}: π_1(T_0'(C), t') → GL(V'_{B,t'}) be the monodromy representations; V'_{B,t'} = V_{B,t} by item 038. Let γ_0, γ_1, γ_∞ be loops around 0, 1, ∞ that generate π_1(T_0'(C), t') subject only to the relation γ_0γ_1γ_∞ = 1. Orient γ_0 so that its image in the deck group Gal((T_0(C) − {0})/T_0'(C)) is e^{2πi/N} = τ(ζ_N). On the index-N normal subgroup π_1(T_0(C) − {0}, t), ρ_{t'} restricts to ρ_t composed with the surjection π_1(T_0(C) − {0}, t) → π_1(T_0(C), t). For n = 2 the same construction is made with BLGHT's Ṽ_B (item 038).
items.locator: §3: base point and monodromy representations, p. 1256; the loops γ_0, γ_1, γ_∞ and the orientation of γ_0, p. 1257

items.proofOutline: By item 038, the local system V_B' near t' = 0 pulls back to V_B, which extends over t = 0. Hence the action of ρ_{t'}(γ_0) on V'_{B,t'} is equivalent to the action on V_{B,0} of the deck transformation τ(ζ_N), which is induced by the action of H on Y_0. On the χ_i-eigenspace V_{B,i} this is multiplication by ζ_N^i. By item 036 (Deligne, Hodge cycles, Proposition 7.4), V_{B,i} is nonzero exactly for i ∈ B, and then has rank one.

items.proofOutline: Let Z_0 ⊂ P^{N−1} × A^1 be the variety T(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N, with T = 1/t. Base change the H_0-equivariant semistable blowup of item 091 to C along an embedding of W(k)[1/p] into C (with U ↦ 1). This gives a blowup of Z_0 that is an isomorphism outside the fibres over 0 and μ_N and is semistable over A^1 − μ_N with reduced special fibre. The monodromy of a reduced semistable degeneration is unipotent (item 101; Illusie, Théorème 2.1.2, with all multiplicities 1). Hence the monodromy of R^{N−2} of this family around T = 0 is unipotent; this is the local monodromy of V_B around t = ∞. Since t ↦ t' = t^N is totally ramified over ∞, that operator is conjugate to ρ_{t'}(γ_∞)^{±N}, so the eigenvalues of ρ_{t'}(γ_∞) are N-th roots of unity. The printed proof stops here. A further step is needed: ρ_{t'}(γ_∞) = c·u with c a scalar and u unipotent, for instance from Katz's description of the Dwork eigensheaves, as BLGHT use for their Lemma 4.3(3). Then c^N = 1. Moreover c^n = det ρ_{t'}(γ_∞) = 1, because det ρ_{t'}(γ_0) = ζ_N^{∑_{b∈B} b} = 1 (item 043, with ∑_{b∈B} b ≡ 0 mod N) and ρ_{t'}(γ_1) is unipotent (Picard–Lefschetz description at t = 1). Since gcd(n, N) = 1, c = 1.
items.note: The printed proof is incomplete (E27). It takes Z_0: T(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N with T = 1/t, the semistable blowup of arXiv:2103.00106v1, Lemma 2.1 (base changed to C along an isomorphism of the algebraic closure of W(k)[1/p] with C), and Illusie's local monodromy theorem with all multiplicities 1. This shows that the local monodromy of V_B around t = ∞ is unipotent. The cover t ↦ t^N is totally ramified over ∞, so that operator is conjugate to ρ_{t'}(γ_∞)^{±N}, and the argument shows only that the eigenvalues of ρ_{t'}(γ_∞) are N-th roots of unity. The full statement is needed downstream: for Lemma 3.4 and Corollary 3.5, for the residual irreducibility after Definition 3.6, and for the l-power order of ρ̄_{t'}(γ_∞) in the proof of Lemma 3.7. A possible repair follows BLGHT, who prove their Lemma 4.3(3) from Katz's description of the Dwork eigensheaves (Katz, Another look at the Dwork family, Theorem 5.3, with Katz, Exponential sums and differential equations, Theorem 8.4.11). Suppose that description gives ρ_{t'}(γ_∞) = c·u with u unipotent and c a scalar. Then c^N = 1 by the argument above. Also c^n = det ρ_{t'}(γ_∞) = 1, because det ρ_{t'}(γ_0) = ζ_N^{∑_{b∈B} b} = 1 (∑_{b∈B} b ≡ 0 mod N) and ρ_{t'}(γ_1) is unipotent by the Picard–Lefschetz description at t = 1, which does not use this item. Since gcd(n, N) = 1, c = 1. The unipotence of the monodromy of a reduced semistable degeneration is taken from item 101. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Transvection at one
items.statement: For n > 2, ρ_{t'}(γ_1) is a transvection: it is unipotent and ker(ρ_{t'}(γ_1) − 1) has dimension n − 1, so ρ_{t'}(γ_1) − 1 has rank one.

items.proofOutline: By the Picard–Lefschetz description at t = 1, ρ_{t'}(γ_1) is conjugate to the local monodromy T of V_B around t = 1, since t ↦ t^N is étale there. Because N − 2 is odd, the vanishing cycles at the distinct ordinary double points of Y_1 are isotropic and mutually orthogonal, so (T − 1)^2 = 0 on the whole middle cohomology, and ρ_{t'}(γ_1) is unipotent. On the χ-eigenpart the image of T − 1 lies in the span of the single vector ∑_{ξ∈H_0} χ(ξ)^{−1}ξδ_0, so ker(ρ_{t'}(γ_1) − 1) has dimension at least n − 1. Finally ρ_{t'}(γ_1) ≠ 1. Otherwise ρ_{t'}(γ_0) = ρ_{t'}(γ_∞)^{−1} would be unipotent by item 044, whereas its eigenvalues ζ_N^b, b ∈ B, all differ from 1 by item 043, since 0 ∉ B. Hence the kernel has dimension exactly n − 1.
items.note: The proof says only that it is the same as BLGHT Lemma 4.3(2) (E28). That argument gives ker(γ_1 − 1) of rank at least n − 1 on an H_0-eigenpart. It then obtains the characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n from the symplectic pairing, which the non-self-dual χ-eigensheaf here does not carry. Unipotence follows instead because the fibre dimension N − 2 is odd. The vanishing cycles at the distinct double points of Y_1 are isotropic and mutually orthogonal, so the Picard–Lefschetz operator T: x ↦ x ± ∑_{δ∈Δ} ⟨x, δ⟩δ on the whole middle cohomology satisfies (T − 1)^2 = 0. The exact rank n − 1 holds because ρ_{t'}(γ_1) ≠ 1: otherwise ρ_{t'}(γ_0) = ρ_{t'}(γ_∞)^{−1} would have eigenvalue 1, contrary to Lemma 3.3(1)–(2). This last step uses Lemma 3.3(2); see the note on item 044. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Hypergeometric companion representation
items.statement: Write (X − 1)^n = X^n + A_1X^{n−1} + ⋯ + A_n and ∏_{i=1}^n (X − ζ_N^{−b_i}) = X^n + B_1X^{n−1} + ⋯ + B_n, with A_i, B_i ∈ Z[ζ_N]. Let A and B be the companion matrices with ones on the subdiagonal and last columns (−A_n, …, −A_1)^T and (−B_n, …, −B_1)^T; both lie in GL_n(Z[ζ_N]). Let ρ: π_1(T_0'(C), t') → GL_n(Z[ζ_N]) send γ_0 ↦ B^{−1}, γ_∞ ↦ A and γ_1 ↦ BA^{−1}; this respects γ_0γ_1γ_∞ = 1. BA^{−1} agrees with the identity except in its first column, which is (C_n, …, C_1)^T with C_i ∈ Z[ζ_N], so ρ(γ_1) − 1 has rank at most one.
items.locator: Lemma 3.4, p. 1258; shape of ρ(γ_1) = BA^{−1} in its proof, p. 1259

items.proofOutline: Apply Levelt's rigidity theorem over C with h_∞ = ρ_{t'}(γ_∞), h_0 = ρ_{t'}(γ_0), α_j = 1 and β_j = ζ_N^{−b_j}. Its hypotheses hold: h_∞ has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n (item 044); h_0^{−1} has characteristic polynomial ∏_j (X − ζ_N^{−b_j}) (item 043); the two spectra are disjoint because 0 ∉ B; and h_1 = ρ_{t'}(γ_1) = h_0^{−1}h_∞^{−1} is a pseudo-reflection (item 045). The theorem gives g with gh_∞g^{−1} = A and gh_0g^{−1} = B^{−1}. Since γ_0 and γ_∞ generate π_1(T_0'(C), t'), g conjugates ρ_{t'} to ρ.

items.name: Maximal unipotence and maximal nilpotence
items.statement: Let φ be an endomorphism of an n-dimensional vector space V over a field. A unipotent φ is maximally unipotent if its minimal polynomial is (X − 1)^n. A nilpotent φ is maximally nilpotent if its minimal polynomial is X^n. For nilpotent φ the following are equivalent: φ is maximally nilpotent; φ^{n−1} ≠ 0; dim ker φ^j = j for 0 ≤ j ≤ n; φ is conjugate to a single nilpotent Jordan block of size n. A unipotent φ is maximally unipotent if and only if φ − 1 is maximally nilpotent.
items.locator: Definition 3.6, p. 1259

items.name: Maximal monodromy at infinity
items.statement: For n > 2, ρ_{t'}(γ_∞) has minimal polynomial (X − 1)^n: it is conjugate over C to the companion matrix A of Lemma 3.4, a single unipotent Jordan block. The local monodromy of ρ_t around t = ∞ is conjugate to ρ_{t'}(γ_∞)^{±N}, so it also has minimal polynomial (X − 1)^n. Over a field of characteristic 0 a nonzero power of a single unipotent Jordan block is again a single Jordan block, whereas in positive characteristic a power can lower the Jordan size. For n = 2 the corresponding statement is BLGHT Corollary 4.5.
items.locator: Corollary 3.5, p. 1259; for n = 2, BLGHT Corollary 4.5

items.name: Absolute irreducibility of the residual monodromy on the three-punctured line
items.statement: Let n > 2 and let λ be a prime of Z[ζ_N] of residue characteristic l, which is odd and prime to N. Let ρ̄: π_1(T_0'(C), t') → GL_n(Z[ζ_N]/λ) be the reduction of the representation ρ of Lemma 3.4. Then ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible. Suppose ρ̄ had a block-triangular form over an algebraic closure of k(λ). Since ρ̄(γ_1) − 1 has rank at most one, ρ̄(γ_1) acts trivially on one of the two blocks, and there ρ̄(γ_0) = ρ̄(γ_∞)^{−1} has eigenvalue 1. This is impossible, because no b_i is 0 mod N and λ ∤ N. The reduction ρ̄_{t'} of ρ_{t'} on V_{B,t'}'/λ has the same characteristic polynomials as ρ̄ (by Lemma 3.4, both being integral), hence the same semisimplification. Therefore ρ̄_{t'} ≅ ρ̄, and ρ̄_{t'} is absolutely irreducible.
items.locator: §3, paragraph after Definition 3.6, p. 1259, following the argument of Beukers–Heckman, Proposition 3.3

uses.how: Input to Finite-image classification input for transvections.
Input to Full special-linear monodromy on the punctured line.

items.proofOutline: An invariant block would force a common eigenvalue between the disjoint spectra. Transfer equality of characteristic polynomials from the characteristic-zero integral comparison to the geometric residual semisimplification; irreducibility then identifies it.
items.note: The paper says that ρ̄_{t'} and ρ̄ have the same trace. In general equal traces determine the semisimplification only when l > n, but here ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible (proved just before) and both representations have dimension n, so equal traces force ρ̄_{t'} ≅ ρ̄ in every characteristic (Burnside's theorem; the field case of Carayol's theorem). The statement also records the equality of characteristic polynomials, which holds since ρ_{t'} and ρ are conjugate over C and both preserve Z[ζ_N]-lattices. The argument depends on Lemma 3.3(2) through Lemma 3.4 (see the note on item 044). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, name, locator.

items.name: Classification of irreducible groups generated by transvections (Zalesskii–Serezhkin), as used
items.statement: Classification input in the form Qian uses it (n > 2). Let l be an odd prime, n > 2, and k(λ) a finite field of characteristic l. Let G ⊂ GL_n(k(λ)) be an absolutely irreducible subgroup generated by transvections. The residual monodromy image is such a group, by the paragraph after Definition 3.6 and the first step of the proof of Lemma 3.7. Then G is conjugate in GL_n(k(λ)) to SL_n(k), Sp_n(k) or SU(n,k) for some subfield k ⊆ k(λ). Here SU(n,k) = {g ∈ SL_n(k) : σ(g)ᵗg = 1_n} is defined only when [k : F_l] is even, and σ is the element of order 2 of Gal(k/F_l). Qian attributes this to the main theorem of Zalesskii–Serezhkin. The exact hypotheses and exceptional cases of that theorem have not been checked against the original.
items.locator: Lemma 3.7, proof, p. 1260, citing Zalesskii–Serezhkin [18], main theorem

uses.how: Input to Full special-linear monodromy on the punctured line.

items.proofOutline: Read and qualify the original classification theorem; the paper's use is presently a source contract, not a certified all-characteristic classification statement (S3).
items.note: The restriction n > 2 matters. For n = 2 the classification in this form is false. In characteristic 3, SL_2(F_5) embeds in SL_2(F_9) as the preimage of A_5 ⊂ A_6 ≅ PSL_2(F_9). It is absolutely irreducible and is generated by transvections, namely its elements of order 3. It is not conjugate to SL_2(k) = Sp_2(k) or SU(2,k) for any k ⊆ F_9, because these groups have order 24 or 720 and SL_2(F_5) has order 120. Qian applies the classification only for n > 2, and takes the case n = 2 of Lemma 3.7 from Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor (Lemma 4.6 and Corollary 4.7). The proof of that Lemma 4.6 quotes the same classification for n = 2 as well. In Qian's range this does no harm. The monodromy image contains the reduction of ρ(γ0), an element of order N > 300, while every element of SL_2(F_5) has order at most 10. Only this case, in the form Lemma 3.7 uses, is placed with the Dwork family, next to its only consumers (items 052, 053 and 056). The general theorem of Zalesskii–Serezhkin remains a listed prerequisite that no atlas stage plans. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, name, locator, dependencies.

items.name: Full special-linear monodromy on the punctured line
items.statement: Assume the standing hypotheses of §3: l is an odd prime, n > 2, N is odd with N > 100n + 100 and gcd(N, ln) = 1, and the exponents a_j and the index set B = {b_1, …, b_n} are as fixed there. Let λ be a prime of Z[ζ_N] above l, so k(λ) = F_{l^r} with r the order of l modulo N. If r is even, assume N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1. Then for t' ∈ T0'(C), the reduction ρ̄_{t'}: π1(T0'(C), t') → GL(V'_{B,t'}/λ) has image SL(V'_{B,t'}/λ) ≅ SL_n(k(λ)). Proof sketch. The image equals the normal closure of the transvection ρ̄_{t'}(γ1), because its index divides both N and a power of l. By the classification (item 051) it is conjugate to SL_n(k), Sp_n(k) or SU(n,k) for some k ⊆ k(λ). A proper subfield would give l^m B = B with l^m ≢ 1 mod N. Sp_n(k(λ)) would give B = −B. SU(n,k(λ)) would give l^{r/2}B = −B. Lemma 3.1 and the hypothesis on r exclude all three.
items.locator: Lemma 3.7, first assertion, p. 1259, and its proof, pp. 1259–1260

items.name: Full special-linear monodromy on the original base
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of item 052 (n > 2), let t ∈ T0(C) be a nonzero base point with image t' = t^N ∈ T0'(C). Then the reduction ρ̄_t: π1(T0(C), t) → GL(V_{B,t}/λ) has image SL(V_{B,t}/λ) ≅ SL_n(k(λ)). Proof sketch. π1(T0(C) − {0}, t) surjects onto π1(T0(C), t), and it is normal in π1(T0'(C), t') with cyclic quotient of order N. So its image is a normal subgroup of SL_n(k(λ)) with cyclic quotient of order dividing N. For n > 2 the cyclic composition factors of SL_n(k(λ)) have order dividing n, and gcd(N, n) = 1, so the quotient is trivial.
items.locator: Lemma 3.7, second assertion, p. 1259, and the last paragraph of its proof, p. 1260

items.name: Constancy of the determinant local system
items.statement: For every admitted ideal a, the geometric monodromy of wedge^n V[a] is trivial because each generating local monodromy has determinant one. Therefore wedge^n V[a] over (T0)_F is the pullback of a one-dimensional G_F-representation, identifiable at t=0. This is descent of the determinant, not triviality of its arithmetic Galois character.
items.locator: §3, paragraph following the proof of Lemma 3.7, p. 1260

items.name: Fixed-determinant isomorphism torsor
items.statement: Let 𝔫 be a nonzero ideal of Z[1/2N, ζ_N] (of Z[1/2N, ζ_N]⁺ when n = 2), let R = Z[ζ_N]/𝔫 (resp. Z[ζ_N]⁺/𝔫), and let W be a finite free R-module of rank n with a continuous G_F-action, viewed as a lisse sheaf on Spec F. Suppose given an isomorphism of lisse sheaves φ: ∧ⁿW_{(T0)_F} → ∧ⁿV[𝔫] over (T0)_F that comes from an isomorphism of G_F-characters, so the determinants must be matched first. Define T_W on schemes S over (T0)_F by T_W(S) = {ψ ∈ Isom_S(W_S, V[𝔫]_S) : ∧ⁿψ = φ_S}. The paper asserts that T_W is representable by a scheme smooth over (T0)_F. In fact T_W is finite étale over (T0)_F. Étale locally both sheaves are constant and φ is multiplication by a unit u of R. T_W is then the set of matrices of determinant u, a coset of SL_n(R) in GL_n(R), and the finite étale group scheme SL(W) acts on it simply transitively.
items.locator: §3, construction of T_W preceding Proposition 3.8, pp. 1260–1261

items.name: Two-prime product monodromy
items.statement: Assume the standing hypotheses of §3: n ≥ 2, N is odd, N > 100n + 100 and gcd(N, n) = 1, F is a CM field containing ζ_N, and the exponents a_j and the set B are as fixed there. Let 𝔫 = 𝔓1𝔓2, where 𝔓1 and 𝔓2 are prime ideals of Z[ζ_N] (of Z[ζ_N]⁺ when n = 2) whose residue characteristics l1 ≠ l2 are prime to 2N, and suppose max{l1, l2} > 10. If n > 2, suppose also, for i = 1, 2, that N ∤ l_i^{r_i/2} + 1 whenever the order r_i of l_i modulo N is even. Then for every t ∈ T0(C) the monodromy map π1(T0(C), t) → SL(V_{B,t}/𝔫) = SL(V_{B,t}/𝔓1) × SL(V_{B,t}/𝔓2) ≅ SL_n(k(𝔓1)) × SL_n(k(𝔓2)) is surjective. Proof sketch. Each projection is surjective by Lemma 3.7 (item 053 for n > 2, item 108 for n = 2). By Goursat's lemma the image is the preimage of the graph of an isomorphism SL_n(k(𝔓1))/H1 ≅ SL_n(k(𝔓2))/H2 for normal subgroups H1 and H2. Say l1 > 10. If H1 were proper, SL_n(k(𝔓1))/H1 would have PSL_n(k(𝔓1)) as a composition factor, by the theorem on normal subgroups of SL_n over a finite field. By Artin's theorem, no composition factor of SL_n(k(𝔓2)) is isomorphic to PSL_n(k(𝔓1)). Hence H1 and H2 are the whole groups, and the image is the full product.
items.locator: Proposition 3.8, first two paragraphs of the proof, p. 1261, citing Lemma 3.7, Goursat's lemma and Artin [2], Theorem 2

uses.how: Input to Geometric connectedness of the determinant torsor.

items.proofOutline: Each projection is surjective (items 053 and 108). Goursat's lemma (item 028) reduces surjectivity to the absence of a common nontrivial quotient. For l1 > 10, a nontrivial quotient of SL_n(k(𝔓1)) has PSL_n(k(𝔓1)) as a composition factor (normal subgroups of SL_n). By Artin's theorem, PSL_n(k(𝔓1)) is not a composition factor of SL_n(k(𝔓2)).
items.note: The exceptional cases of the two group-theoretic inputs do not occur here. Both l_i are odd. For n = 2, a residue field k(𝔓_i) = F_3 of Z[ζ_N]⁺ would require 3 ≡ ±1 mod N, that is N | 2 or N | 4, which is impossible because N > 300 is odd. For n = 2 the ideal 𝔫 lies in Z[1/2N, ζ_N]⁺ (p. 1260), so 𝔓1 and 𝔓2 are primes of Z[ζ_N]⁺ and V_B is the local system with real cyclotomic coefficients. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Geometric connectedness of the determinant torsor
items.statement: Under the two-prime hypotheses of Proposition 3.8 (item 056) and a given identification φ: ∧^n W ≅ ∧^n V[𝔫], the torsor T_W is geometrically connected. On each geometric fibre its points form one orbit under the full product monodromy. Over a field of characteristic zero, T_W is smooth, so connectedness gives geometric irreducibility, as Moret–Bailly's theorem needs.
items.locator: Proposition 3.8 and the last paragraph of its proof, p. 1261

items.statement: Let F_q be a finite field with N | q − 1, t: μ_N(F_q) → μ_N(Q̄_l) a chosen identification, ψ a nontrivial additive character of F_q and a ∈ Z/NZ. For such i it is one-dimensional, and its only nonzero Hodge graded piece has degree M(a) + #{b ∈ B : ⟨ab⟩ < ⟨ai⟩}; equivalently, this degree is (∑_j ⟨a(a_j + i)⟩)/N − 1.

For an embedding σ: F_v → Q̄_l with σ^{−1}(ζ_N) = ζ_N^a on the cyclotomic subfield, its σ-labelled Hodge–Tate weights, in the paper's cohomological convention, are M(a), …, M(a) + n − 1. The comparison identifies D_{dR,σ} with the correspondingly twisted de Rham eigenspace, not the untwisted one.

items.name: Ordinarity near the Fermat fibre
items.statement: Let λ be a prime of Z[ζ_N] above l and v a place of F above l, and suppose l ≡ 1 mod N, so that Q(ζ_N)_λ = Q_l. If t ∈ m_{F_v}, then V_{λ,t}, as a representation of G_{F_v}, is ordinary of weight μ in the sense of Definition 1.2. Here μ_{τ,i} = M(a_τ) for every i = 1, …, n and every embedding τ: F_v → Q̄_l, and a_τ ∈ (Z/NZ)^× is defined by τ^{-1}(ζ_N) = ζ_N^{a_τ}. The paper writes this weight as (λ_{τ,i}); a different letter is used here because λ denotes the prime. Proof sketch. D_cris(V_{λ,t}) and D_cris(V_{λ,0}) are both the χ-eigenspace of the crystalline cohomology of the common special fibre, the reduction of Y_0, so they agree as φ-modules. Their labelled Hodge–Tate weights agree by Lemma 3.11(1). As a representation of inertia, V_{λ,0} ⊗ Q̄_l ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} Q̄_l(−M(a_τ) − i). Lemma 2.4 (item 025) then gives the claim.
items.locator: Lemma 3.11(3) and its proof, pp. 1266–1267 (using Lemma 2.4)

items.proofOutline: Compare the crystalline Frobenius at t with the common special fibre at0. Since l splits cyclotomically, its Fermat lines have the required individual slopes; item025 supplies ordinarity.

items.name: Maximal away-from-coefficient-prime monodromy near infinity
items.statement: Let v be a place of F above l and t ∈ F_v with v(t) < 0 (E1), and let λ′ be a prime of odd residue characteristic l′ ≠ l with l′ ∤ N. Then the monodromy operator N of the Weil–Deligne representation of V_{λ′,t}|G_{F_v} has minimal polynomial X^n. Inertia acts unipotently, through exp(t_{l′}(σ)N), and the logarithm of the monodromy at infinity is maximally nilpotent. The hypothesis v(t) < 0 is necessary: when t ∈ O_{F_v} and t^N − 1 is a unit, V_{λ′,t} is unramified at v and N = 0.
items.locator: Lemma 3.12 and its proof, pp. 1267–1268, with correction E1 (v(t) < 0); Harris–Shepherd-Barron–Taylor [10], Lemma 1.15(2)

items.name: Ordinary automorphy lifting theorem over CM and totally real fields (ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2)
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM or totally real field, p a prime, and ρ: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) a continuous representation such that: (1) ρ is unramified almost everywhere; (2) for each place v | p, ρ|G_{F_v} is potentially semistable and ordinary with regular Hodge–Tate weights. That is, there is a weight λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,Q̄_p)} such that for each v | p, ρ|G_{F_v} is conjugate to an upper-triangular representation with diagonal characters ψ_{v,1}, …, ψ_{v,n}: G_{F_v} → Q̄_p^×, where ψ_{v,i} agrees on an open subgroup of I_{F_v} with σ ↦ ∏_{τ ∈ Hom(F_v,Q̄_p)} τ(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))^{−(λ_{τ,n−i+1}+i−1)}; (3) ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic, and ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is enormous; (4) there is σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar, and p > n; (5) there are a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(A_F) and an isomorphism ι: Q̄_p → C such that π is ι-ordinary and r̄_ι(π) ≅ ρ̄. Then ρ is ordinarily automorphic of weight ιλ: there is an ι-ordinary cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_n(A_F) of weight ιλ with ρ ≅ r_ι(Π). Moreover, if v ∤ p is a finite place of F at which both ρ and π are unramified, then Π_v is unramified. The bound p > n belongs to hypothesis (4). Qian's Theorem 1.4 does not impose it (E2).
items.locator: ACC+ (Allen et al., Ann. of Math. 197 (2023)), Theorem 6.1.2, pp. 1029–1030; applied in the proofs of Theorem 1.1 (pp. 1272–1273) and Theorem 1.4 (p. 1274)

items.proofOutline: Cited from ACC+, where it is proved by the patching argument of ACC+ §6; Qian does not reprove it. Every hypothesis is used exactly as stated, including the bound p > n and the scalar element outside G_{F(ζ_p)} in (4).
items.note: The status stays missing: no atlas stage states an automorphy lifting theorem. ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 is the output of the patching layers of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure and belongs at PA.4, with PA.2 (ι-ordinarity, ACC+ Theorem 5.5.1) and PA.5 (the base-change checklist) as further inputs. Qian applies it at p = l′ in the proof of Theorem 1.1 (p. 1272), where p > n holds because l′ > 2ln + 5, and at p = l in the proof of Theorem 1.4 (p. 1274), where p > n is not among the hypotheses (E2). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, name, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Auxiliary data and initial avoidance field
items.statement: Fix a non-CM elliptic curve E/Q, written E_0 here to avoid a clash with the CM field E constructed later. For a prime l′, let r̄_{E_0,l′} be the G_Q-representation H^1_et(E_0, F_{l′}). Let F, F^av, n, l, s and r̄: G_F → GL_n(F_{l^s}) be as in Theorem 1.1, and write n = l^a m with l ∤ m. Let k′ (written F′ in the paper) be the finite field generated by the m-th roots of all elements of F_{l^s}. By Lemma 2.3 there is a positive integer N such that: (i) N is odd, and N is divisible by no prime factor of ln, by no prime ramified in F^av or in F̄^{ker r̄}, and by no prime of bad reduction of E_0; (ii) N > 100n + 100; (iii) F_{l^2}k′ ⊂ F_l(ζ_N); when n = 2, moreover F_l(ζ_N) = F_{l^r} with r even, and F_{l^2}k′ is contained in the residue field of Q(ζ_N)^+ at a prime above l (written F_l(ζ_N)^+); (iv) writing F_l(ζ_N) = F_{l^r}, if r is even then N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1. Let F^avoid be the normal closure over Q of F^av F̄^{ker r̄}(ζ_l). Then Q(ζ_N) and F^avoid are linearly disjoint over Q. Indeed, a prime ramified in their intersection would divide N and ramify in F^avoid, so the intersection is unramified over Q and hence equals Q. Consequently F^avoid and F(ζ_N) are linearly disjoint over F.
items.locator: §4, opening paragraphs (choice of E, N and F^avoid), p. 1268

items.name: Selection of a large ordinary auxiliary prime
items.statement: In the situation of the opening of §4 there is a rational prime l′ such that: l′ ≡ 1 mod N; l′ > 2ln + 5 and l′ is unramified in F; r̄_{E_0,l′}(G_{F̃}) = GL_2(F_{l′}), where F̃ is the normal closure of F over Q; there is σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_{l′})} with r̄_{E_0,l′}(σ) scalar; and E_0 has good ordinary reduction at l′. Proof: the congruence condition holds on a set of primes of positive Dirichlet density. The second, third and fifth conditions each exclude a set of density 0: the third by Serre's open image theorem, and the fifth because the supersingular primes of a non-CM curve have density 0 (Serre). The fourth condition follows from the second and third: take u ∈ F_{l′}^× with u^2 ≠ 1 and σ ∈ G_{F̃} with r̄_{E_0,l′}(σ) = u. The same argument allows two further conditions that the later argument needs and Proposition 4.1 does not list. First, l′ ≡ 1 mod n, so that k(λ′) = F_{l′} contains the n-th roots of unity that Lemma 2.1 requires (correction E7). Second, l′ is unramified in F^avoid; the first paragraph of the proof of ACC+ Corollary 7.2.4 requires this of its prime.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1 (first list) and the first paragraph of its proof, p. 1269; correction E7

uses.how: Input to An automorphic elliptic symmetric-power seed with avoidance.
Input to Determinant matching at the auxiliary prime.

items.proofOutline: The primes l′ ≡ 1 mod Nn have Dirichlet density 1/φ(Nn) > 0. Remove the density-zero set of primes of supersingular reduction of E_0 (Serre, 1981, Theorem 20). Remove the finitely many primes l′ with r̄_{E_0,l′}(G_{F̃}) ≠ GL_2(F_{l′}) (Serre's open image theorem over F̃). Remove the finitely many primes that are at most 2ln + 5, ramified in F or in F^avoid, or of bad reduction for E_0. For the scalar element take u ∈ F_{l′}^× with u^2 ≠ 1 and σ ∈ G_{F̃} with r̄_{E_0,l′}(σ) = u. Since det r̄_{E_0,l′} = ε̄_{l′}^{−1}, we get ε̄_{l′}(σ) = u^{−2} ≠ 1, so σ ∉ G_{F(ζ_{l′})}.
items.note: The proof of Proposition 4.1 (p. 1269) says that the listed properties of l′ give everything the first paragraph of the proof of ACC+ Corollary 7.2.4 needs of its prime. They do not: that paragraph also requires the prime to be unramified in F^avoid, which is what makes Q̄^{ker r̄_{E_0,l′}} linearly disjoint from F^avoid (ACC+ Lemma 7.1.8(2), p. 1100). Without this condition the second list can fail. Suppose F^av contains the quadratic subfield Q(√((−1)^{(l′−1)/2} l′)) of Q(ζ_{l′}), which lies in Q̄^{ker r̄_{E_0,l′}}. Then no F_2^avoid can both contain Q̄^{ker r̄_{E_0,l′}} and meet F^avoid only in Q. The condition excludes only finitely many primes, so l′ can be chosen to satisfy it, and the existence statement of Proposition 4.1 stands. The same holds for the congruence l′ ≡ 1 mod n: since gcd(N, n) = 1, the primes l′ ≡ 1 mod Nn have positive density. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: An automorphic elliptic symmetric-power seed with avoidance
items.statement: Let N and F^avoid be as at the opening of §4, and let l′ be as in Proposition 4.1 and also unramified in F^avoid. Let 𝓛 be the set of prime divisors of N. There are a finite Galois extension F_2^avoid/Q and a finite totally real Galois extension F^suff/Q, unramified above 𝓛, such that: F_2^avoid ∩ F^avoid = Q; F^suff ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid = Q; Q̄^{ker r̄_{E_0,l′}} ⊂ F_2^avoid; and F^avoid and F_2^avoid are unramified above 𝓛. Moreover, for every finite totally real extension F′/F^suff with F′ ∩ F_2^avoid = Q, the l′-adic representation Sym^{n−1} r_{E_0,l′}|G_{F′} is automorphic, where r_{E_0,l′} = H^1_et(E_0, Q̄_{l′}). Proof: run the proof of ACC+ Corollary 7.2.4 with its F^avoid equal to F^avoid, its elliptic curve equal to E_0, M = {n−1}, its set of primes equal to 𝓛 (primes of good reduction of E_0), and its prime l equal to l′. ACC+ state the conclusion for the dual Sym^m r_{E,l}^∨. The dual of r_{l,ι}(π) is r_{l,ι}(π^∨) up to a power of the cyclotomic character, which corresponds to twisting π^∨ by a power of |det|. So a representation is automorphic if and only if its dual is. The third and fourth properties are not in the statement of ACC+ Corollary 7.2.4. The third comes from its proof, where F_2^avoid = F_1^avoid L_3 and L_3 = L_2 Q̄^{ker r̄_{E_0,l′}}. For the fourth, F^avoid is unramified above 𝓛 by the choice of N. L_3 is unramified above 𝓛, because E_0 has good reduction there, l′ ∉ 𝓛, and the imaginary quadratic field and the characters ψ_m of that proof are unramified above 𝓛. F_1^avoid is unramified above 𝓛, because the proof of ACC+ Proposition 7.2.3 cuts it out by auxiliary residual representations unramified above 𝓛 and the roots of unity of an auxiliary prime outside 𝓛.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1 (second list and final assertion) and its proof, pp. 1269–1270; ACC+ Corollary 7.2.4, p. 1100 (proof pp. 1100–1103), and Proposition 7.2.3, p. 1099
