items.proofOutline: Rerun the proof of ACC+ Corollary 7.2.4 (pp. 1100–1103) with its avoidance field equal to F^avoid, its elliptic curve equal to E_0, M = {n − 1}, its set of primes equal to the prime divisors of N, and l′ in place of its prime l. The prime l′ meets that proof's requirements, including l′ ≥ 2(n + 1) and l′ unramified in F^avoid. The containment Q̄^{ker r̄_{E_0,l′}} ⊂ F_2^avoid and the unramifiedness of F_2^avoid above the prime divisors of N are read off from that proof. Pass from the dual Sym^{n−1} r_{E_0,l′}^∨ to Sym^{n−1} r_{E_0,l′}: the dual of an automorphic representation r_{l,ι}(π) is r_{l,ι}(π^∨) up to a power of the cyclotomic character.
items.note: Qian applies this to (F′)^+, which contains F^+ ⊂ F^avoid. He therefore needs ACC+ Corollary 7.2.4 in its printed form, which asks only for disjointness from F_2^avoid. That proof applies the printed Proposition 7.2.3 with F^avoid L_3 as its avoidance field, and the proposition asks for disjointness from F^avoid L_3 F_1^avoid. The Allen et al. extraction records this as a gap, with a repair: weaken Proposition 7.2.3 to disjointness from F_1^avoid. That repair is exactly what this use needs, since F_1^avoid ⊂ F_2^avoid. Qian's page references in the proof are to arXiv v1 of ACC+ (1812.09999v1), the version he cites. There pp. 180–183 match, but L_3 is defined on p. 182 and F_2^avoid on p. 183, not on pp. 206 and 208 as printed. In the published paper the passages are on pp. 1099–1102. In item 2 of that proof, 'ζ_{l′}' and 'l′ ∉ L' refer to the auxiliary prime of the proof of ACC+ Proposition 7.2.3, not to Qian's l′. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, proof outline.

items.name: Determinant matching at the original coefficient prime
items.statement: Let l be an odd prime, n ≥ 2 an integer written n = l^a m with l ∤ m, s ≥ 1, and N an odd integer prime to ln with N > 100n + 100. Let F be a CM field, M = F(ζ_N), and r̄: G_F → GL_n(F_{l^s}) a continuous representation. Let λ be a prime of Z[ζ_N] above l (of Z[ζ_N]^+ when n = 2), with residue field k(λ). Assume that k(λ) contains F_{l^2} and an m-th root of every element of F_{l^s}, inside a fixed algebraic closure F̄_l. Then: (i) det r̄ takes values in (k(λ)^×)^n. Indeed, if x ∈ F_{l^s}^× and y ∈ k(λ) with y^m = x, then y = z^{l^a} for some z ∈ k(λ)^×, because the l^a-th power map is bijective on k(λ)^×, and so x = z^n. (ii) The determinant det V[λ] of the Dwork eigensheaf, a character of G_M, takes values in (F_{l^2}^× k(λ)^×)^n = (k(λ)^×)^n, by Lemma 3.9 applied over M. (iii) Hence the character det V[λ] ⊗ (det r̄|_{G_M})^∨ of G_M takes values in (k(λ)^×)^n. (iv) k(λ) contains the m-th roots of 1 ∈ F_{l^s}, and these are all the n-th roots of unity in F̄_l. So m | #k(λ)^×, and Lemma 2.1 applies to the character in (iii) with k = k(λ). The paper asks for n | #k(λ)^× instead, which fails when l | n (correction E5). In §4 the hypothesis on k(λ) holds by condition (iii) on N at the opening of §4, which puts F_{l^2}k′ inside k(λ); here k′ is the finite field generated by the m-th roots of all elements of F_{l^s}.
items.locator: §4, paragraph beginning 'On the side of characteristic l', p. 1270; Lemma 3.9, p. 1262; correction E5

uses.how: Input to Simultaneous determinant twists and CRT representation.

items.proofOutline: (i) is finite-field arithmetic: the l^a-th power map is an automorphism of k(λ)^×. (ii) is Lemma 3.9 over M = F(ζ_N) together with F_{l^2} ⊂ k(λ). (iii) follows from (i) and (ii). (iv) holds because μ_m(F̄_l) consists of the m-th roots of 1 ∈ F_{l^s}, and x^n = 1 if and only if x^m = 1 in characteristic l.
items.note: Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Determinant matching at the auxiliary prime
items.statement: Let n ≥ 2, let N be an odd integer prime to n with N > 100n + 100, let F be a CM field and M = F(ζ_N), and let B = {b_1, …, b_n} be the index set of §3. Let l′ be an odd prime with l′ ≡ 1 mod N (so l′ ∤ N), and let λ′ be a prime of Z[ζ_N] above l′ (of Z[ζ_N]^+ when n = 2). Then Q(ζ_N)_{λ′} = Q_{l′} and k(λ′) = F_{l′}. For a place v of M of residue characteristic p ∤ 2Nl′, write q = #k(v), Frob_v for a geometric Frobenius element at v, and g(v,b) for the Gauss sums of Lemma 3.9 with values in Q̄_{l′}. View det V_{λ′} as a character of G_M through the fibre at t = 0. Then: (i) det(Frob_v | V_{λ′,0}) · q^{−n(n−1)/2} = (q^{(N−2n−1)/2} ∏_{b∈B} g(v,b))^n. The exponent (N − 2n − 1)/2 is an integer because N is odd, and q^{(N−2n−1)/2} ∏_{b∈B} g(v,b) lies in Z_{l′}^×. Equivalently, since ε_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2}(Frob_v) = q^{n(n−1)/2} for the l′-adic cyclotomic character ε_{l′}, the character det V_{λ′} ⊗ ε_{l′}^{n(n−1)/2} takes the value (q^{(N−2n−1)/2} ∏_{b∈B} g(v,b))^n at Frob_v. (ii) Consequently, for every continuous representation r̄′: G_F → GL_n(F_{l′}) with det r̄′ = ε̄_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2}, the character (det r̄′|_{G_M})^∨ ⊗ det V[λ′] of G_M takes values in (F_{l′}^×)^n. (iii) If moreover l′ ≡ 1 mod n, then F_{l′} contains the n-th roots of unity, and Lemma 2.1 applies to this character with k = F_{l′} (correction E7). Lemma 3.9 by itself gives values only in (F_{l′^2}^×)^n here; the cancellation in (i) supplies the missing step (correction E6).
items.locator: §4, paragraph beginning 'On the other side of characteristic l′', p. 1270; Lemma 3.9 and equation (3.1), pp. 1262–1263; corrections E6, E7 and E9

uses.how: Input to Simultaneous determinant twists and CRT representation.

items.proofOutline: By the constancy of the determinant local system, det V_{λ′} is determined by its fibre at t = 0. Equation (3.1) gives det(Frob_v | V_{λ′,0}) = q^{n(N−n−2)/2}(∏_{b∈B} g(v,b))^n; divide by q^{n(n−1)/2}. By (3.2) the product of Gauss sums lies in Q_{l′}(ζ_N) = Q_{l′}. It is an l′-adic unit, because g(v,b)g(v,−b) = q and p ≠ l′. Reduce modulo λ′; det r̄′(Frob_v) is q^{n(n−1)/2} mod l′. By Chebotarev density every element of the finite image of the quotient character is the value at some such Frob_v.
items.note: Frob_v is geometric Frobenius, the convention in which the eigenvalues q^{−1}∏_j g(v, a_j + i) of Lemma 3.9 have absolute value q^{(N−2)/2}. In §4 the seed is r̄′ = Sym^{n−1} r̄_{E_0,l′}|_{G_F}. Since H^1_et(E_0, F_{l′}) is dual to the Tate module, its determinant is ε̄_{l′}^{−1}, so det r̄′ = ε̄_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2}, whose value at geometric Frobenius is q^{n(n−1)/2}. The paper prints the exponent +n(n−1)/2 (E9). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Simultaneous determinant twists, the module W and the torsor T_W
items.statement: Hypotheses. Let l be an odd prime, n ≥ 2 an integer written n = l^a m with l ∤ m, s ≥ 1, and N an odd integer prime to ln with N > 100n + 100. Let r be the order of l modulo N, and assume N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1 if r is even. Let F be a CM field, M = F(ζ_N), and r̄: G_F → GL_n(F_{l^s}) continuous. Let λ be a prime of Z[ζ_N] above l (of Z[ζ_N]^+ when n = 2) whose residue field k(λ) contains F_{l^2} and an m-th root of every element of F_{l^s}. Let l′ > 2ln + 5 be a prime unramified in F with l′ ≡ 1 mod N and l′ ≡ 1 mod n (the second congruence is correction E7). Let λ′ be a prime of Z[ζ_N] above l′ (of Z[ζ_N]^+ when n = 2), so k(λ′) = F_{l′}, and let r̄′: G_F → GL_n(F_{l′}) be continuous with det r̄′ = ε̄_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2}. Let F^avoid/Q be a finite Galois extension containing F, F_2^avoid/Q a finite Galois extension, and F^suff/Q a finite totally real Galois extension. Assume F^avoid, F_2^avoid and F^suff are unramified above every prime divisor of N, F_2^avoid ∩ F^avoid = Q, and F^suff ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid = Q. Put F_0 = F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff(ζ_N), a finite Galois extension of Q containing M. Construction. Apply Lemma 2.1 to the (k(λ)^×)^n-valued character det V[λ] ⊗ (det r̄|_{G_M})^∨ of G_M with avoidance field F_0, obtaining L_1. Then apply it over L_1M to the (F_{l′}^×)^n-valued character (det r̄′)^∨ ⊗ det V[λ′], with avoidance field F_0L_1, obtaining L_2. Put L = L_1L_2 and E = LM. This gives: (a) a finite totally real Galois extension L/Q, linearly disjoint from F_0 over Q, and the CM field E = LM, finite and Galois over F; (b) characters χ̄_1: G_E → k(λ)^× and χ̄_2: G_E → F_{l′}^× with χ̄_1^n = det V[λ] ⊗ (det r̄)^∨ and χ̄_2^n = det V[λ′] ⊗ (det r̄′)^∨ on G_E; (c) the finite free module W of rank n over Z[ζ_N]/λλ′ ≅ k(λ) × F_{l′} (over Z[ζ_N]^+/λλ′ when n = 2), on which G_E acts by (χ̄_1 ⊗ r̄) × (χ̄_2 ⊗ r̄′). Then det W ≅ det V[λλ′] as characters of G_E. This gives an isomorphism φ: ∧^n W_{(T_0)_E} ≅ ∧^n V[λλ′] of lisse sheaves on (T_0)_E, so the torsor T_W over (T_0)_E is defined. (d) T_W is geometrically connected, by Proposition 3.8. Its hypotheses hold: l and l′ are distinct odd primes prime to N, max(l, l′) > 10, the order of l′ modulo N is 1, and N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1 when r is even. (e) E ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff = F, so E and F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff are linearly disjoint over F. Indeed, L and F_0 are linearly disjoint over Q and M ⊂ F_0, so E ∩ F_0 = M. Moreover F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff is Galois over Q and unramified above the prime divisors of N, so it meets Q(ζ_N) only in Q; as it contains F, M ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff = F. In §4 the hypotheses are met as follows: N and F^avoid (the normal closure over Q of F^av F̄^{ker r̄}(ζ_l)) come from the opening of §4; l′, F_2^avoid and F^suff come from Proposition 4.1; and r̄′ = Sym^{n−1} r̄_{E_0,l′}|_{G_F}, whose determinant is ε̄_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2} (correction E9).

items.name: Moret–Bailly with three kinds of local conditions
items.statement: Let K be a number field and S = S_1 ⊔ S_2 ⊔ S_3 a finite set of places of K, every place in S_2 being non-archimedean. Let T/K be a smooth, geometrically connected variety. Suppose given: for v ∈ S_1, a nonempty open subset Ω_v ⊂ T(K_v) for the v-adic topology; for v ∈ S_2, a nonempty open Gal(K_v^{nr}/K_v)-invariant subset Ω_v ⊂ T(K_v^{nr}); for v ∈ S_3, a nonempty open Gal(K̄_v/K_v)-invariant subset Ω_v ⊂ T(K̄_v). Let H/K be a finite Galois extension. Then there are a finite Galois extension K′/K and a point P ∈ T(K′) such that: K′/K is linearly disjoint from H/K; every v ∈ S_1 splits completely in K′, and P ∈ Ω_v ⊂ T(K′_w) for every place w | v of K′; every v ∈ S_2 is unramified in K′, and P ∈ Ω_v ∩ T(K′_w) for every place w | v of K′; and P ∈ Ω_v ∩ T(K′_w) for every place w of K′ above some v ∈ S_3. The paper writes F and F′ for K and K′. This is an existence theorem for points over a controlled extension, not weak approximation in a fixed field.

items.name: Weil restriction and simultaneous local valuation opens
items.statement: Let E, F^suff and the torsor T_W over (T_0)_E be as in the construction of W and φ (§4, pp. 1270–1271), with T_W smooth and geometrically connected. Let T = Res_{EF^suff/Q}(T_W ×_E EF^suff), where T_W is viewed as a variety over E. Then T is a smooth, geometrically connected variety over Q, since Weil restriction along the finite separable extension EF^suff/Q preserves both properties. Its real points form the product of T_W(C) over the complex places of EF^suff, which is nonempty because EF^suff is CM and has no real places; take Ω_∞ = T(R). The projection T_W → (T_0)_E induces a morphism p: T → Res_{EF^suff/Q} T_0. Put Ω_{l,0} = {(t_τ) ∈ ∏_{τ: EF^suff → Q̄_l} T_0(Q̄_l) : v_l(t_τ) < 0 for all τ} and Ω_{l′,0} = {(t_τ) ∈ ∏_{τ: EF^suff → Q̄_{l′}} T_0(Q̄_{l′}) : v_{l′}(t_τ) > 0 for all τ}. Put Ω_l = p^{−1}(Ω_{l,0}) and Ω_{l′} = p^{−1}(Ω_{l′,0}). These sets are open, nonempty, and invariant under Gal(Q̄_l/Q_l), respectively Gal(Q̄_{l′}/Q_{l′}). Indeed, Ω_{l,0} and Ω_{l′,0} are open, Galois-stable and nonempty, since a t with v_l(t) < 0, respectively v_{l′}(t) > 0, avoids μ_N and ∞. Moreover p is finite étale and surjective on Q̄_l- and Q̄_{l′}-points.

items.name: The Dwork switching point and controlled CM extension
items.statement: Keep the hypotheses and notation of the construction of E, χ̄_1, χ̄_2, W, φ and T_W (§4, pp. 1270–1271): l, l′, n, N, F, M = F(ζ_N), r̄, r̄′, λ, λ′, F^avoid, F_2^avoid, F^suff, F_0 = F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff(ζ_N), L and E = LM. Apply Proposition 4.2 over Q to T = Res_{EF^suff/Q} T_W with H = F_0L = F_0E, S_1 = {∞}, S_2 = ∅ and S_3 = {l, l′}. Take Ω_∞ = T(R), and let Ω_l, Ω_{l′} be the sets of points whose image t = (t_τ) in Res_{EF^suff/Q} T_0 satisfies v_l(t_τ) < 0 for every τ: EF^suff → Q̄_l, respectively v_{l′}(t_τ) > 0 for every τ: EF^suff → Q̄_{l′}. This gives a finite totally real Galois extension L′/Q, linearly disjoint from F_0L over Q. With F′ = L′EF^suff, it also gives a point t ∈ T_0(F′) together with a G_{F′}-equivariant isomorphism W ≅ V[λλ′]_t whose top exterior power is φ_t. These satisfy: (i) L′ and EF^suff are linearly disjoint over Q; F′ ⊃ EF^suff is a CM field, finite and Galois over F, with maximal totally real subfield (F′)^+ = L′E^+F^suff; (ii) χ̄_1^{−1}V[λ]_t ≅ r̄|_{G_{F′}} and χ̄_2^{−1}V[λ′]_t ≅ r̄′|_{G_{F′}}; (iii) v(t) < 0 for every place v | l of F′, and v(t) > 0 for every place v | l′ of F′; (iv) F′ ∩ F_2^avoid = Q and F′ ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid = F. In particular F′ is linearly disjoint over F from every extension of F contained in F^avoid F_2^avoid; in §4 these include F^av and F̄^{ker r̄}. (v) K = L′LF^suff(ζ_N) is a finite Galois extension of Q with FK = F′ and K ∩ F^avoid = Q. This is the field that the proof of Theorem 1.4 needs to be linearly disjoint from F^avoid; the paper states the disjointness for F′, which contains F (correction E3).

items.proofOutline: Apply Proposition 4.2 to T with the local sets of the Weil-restriction step. A point of T(L′) is a point of T_W over L′ ⊗ EF^suff = F′, that is, t ∈ T_0(F′) with a G_{F′}-isomorphism W ≅ V[λλ′]_t; its two components give (ii), and the choice of Ω_l and Ω_{l′} gives (iii). For (iv) and (v), compute the intersections step by step. Use that L′ is linearly disjoint from F_0L, that L is linearly disjoint from F_0, that F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff is linearly disjoint from Q(ζ_N), that F^suff ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid = Q and that F^avoid ∩ F_2^avoid = Q. Each time pass to the relevant base field by base change of linear disjointness.

items.name: Automorphy of the auxiliary-prime Dwork realization
items.statement: Let E_0/Q be the non-CM elliptic curve fixed at the opening of §4. Let l′, F_2^avoid and F^suff be as in Proposition 4.1, with l′ moreover ≡ 1 mod n and unramified in F^avoid. Put r̄′ = Sym^{n−1} r̄_{E_0,l′}|_{G_F}. Since det H^1_et(E_0, F_{l′}) = ε̄_{l′}^{−1}, det r̄′ = ε̄_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2} (correction E9). So the construction of W, φ and T_W and the choice of a point by Proposition 4.2 (pp. 1270–1272) apply; let t ∈ T_0(F′) be the resulting point and F′ = L′EF^suff the resulting CM field. Then V_{λ′,t} is automorphic as a representation of G_{F′}. The argument is as follows. (a) F′ ∩ F_2^avoid = Q and Q̄^{ker r̄_{E_0,l′}} ⊂ F_2^avoid, so F′ and Q̄^{ker r̄_{E_0,l′}} are linearly disjoint over Q. Hence r̄_{E_0,l′}(G_{F′}) = r̄_{E_0,l′}(G_Q) = GL_2(F_{l′}), and some σ ∈ G_{F′} − G_{F′(ζ_{l′})} has r̄_{E_0,l′}(σ) scalar. (b) The totally real field (F′)^+ = L′E^+F^suff contains F^suff and meets F_2^avoid in Q, so Sym^{n−1} r_{E_0,l′}|_{G_{(F′)^+}} is automorphic by Proposition 4.1. Its restriction to G_{F′} is irreducible by (c), so base change to the CM quadratic extension F′/(F′)^+ shows that Sym^{n−1} r_{E_0,l′}|_{G_{F′}} is automorphic. (c) Since r̄_{E_0,l′}(G_{F′}) ⊃ SL_2(F_{l′}) and l′ > n, Sym^{n−1} r̄_{E_0,l′}|_{G_{F′}} is absolutely irreducible. The element σ of (a) has scalar image under Sym^{n−1}, which is condition (4) of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2. The image of G_{F′(ζ_{l′})} under Sym^{n−1} r̄_{E_0,l′} is enormous by Lemma 2.6(1). Sym^{n−1} r̄_{E_0,l′}|_{G_{F′}} is decomposed generic by Lemma 2.6(2): F′/F is Galois and F′ ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid = F, while F̃ ⊂ F^avoid and Q̄^{ker r̄_{E_0,l′}} ⊂ F_2^avoid, so the normal closure over Q of F̃ F̄^{ker ad r̄_{E_0,l′}} lies in F^avoid F_2^avoid. (d) Because E_0 has good ordinary reduction at l′, Sym^{n−1} r_{E_0,l′}|_{G_{F′}} is ordinary at every l′-adic place of F′. It is polarizable, so it is ι′-ordinarily automorphic by Geraghty's Lemma 5.9. (e) Let χ_2 be the Teichmüller lift of χ̄_2, with values in Q(ζ_N)_{λ′}^× = Q_{l′}^× (the paper writes Q(ζ_N)^×), and put ρ = V_{λ′,t} ⊗ χ_2^{−1}. Then ρ̄ ≅ Sym^{n−1} r̄_{E_0,l′}|_{G_{F′}}. At every l′-adic place v′ of F′ we have v′(t) > 0, so t is integral and t^N − 1 is a unit. Hence V_{λ′,t} is crystalline at v′ by Lemma 3.11(2), and ordinary with regular Hodge–Tate weights by Lemma 3.11(3), since l′ ≡ 1 mod N. So the twist ρ by a finite-order character is potentially crystalline and ordinary with the same regular weights. (f) ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 applies with p = l′ > 2ln + 5 > n, to ρ and the ι′-ordinary automorphic representation of (d), whose residual representation is ρ̄. It shows that ρ, and hence V_{λ′,t} = ρ ⊗ χ_2, is automorphic.

items.name: Transport of Dwork automorphy between coefficient primes
items.statement: The fibre Y_t and the fixed eigenprojector give realizations V_{λ,t} and V_{λ′,t}. At the good places of F′, their Frobenius characteristic polynomials have coefficients in Q(ζ_N) (in Q(ζ_N)^+ when n = 2) and agree once the coefficient embeddings are matched. Suppose V_{λ′,t} ≅ r_{l′,ι′}(π) for a regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_n(A_{F′}). Then, for a compatible choice of ι, r_{l,ι}(π) has the same Frobenius characteristic polynomials as V_{λ,t} at almost all places, so r_{l,ι}(π) ≅ V_{λ,t}^{ss} by Chebotarev density and Brauer–Nesbitt. This is all that Theorem 1.1 needs. V_{λ,t} is irreducible, so that V_{λ,t} ≅ r_{l,ι}(π), when its residual representation χ̄_1 ⊗ r̄|G_{F′} is absolutely irreducible, as under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.4. For the semisimple r̄ of Theorem 1.1, semisimplicity of V_{λ,t} is not known. The argument gives no information about monodromy at bad places.
items.locator: §4, proof of Theorem 1.1, p. 1273 ('Hence V_{λ,t} is automorphic as a G_{F′} representation'); the same comparison is used in the proof of Lemma 4.3, p. 1273

Input to Ordinarity of the automorphic Dwork realization at the original prime.

items.proofOutline: The Frobenius characteristic polynomials on the χ-eigenspace of H^{N−2} of the smooth proper fibre Y_t have coefficients in Q(ζ_N) (in Q(ζ_N)^+ when n = 2) that do not depend on the coefficient prime. This follows from the Lefschetz trace formula for the maps h ∘ Frob^m with h in the symmetry group. Transfer the good-place characteristic polynomials of r_{l′,ι′}(π) to r_{l,ι}(π) by the compatibility of the system attached to π. Chebotarev density and Brauer–Nesbitt then give r_{l,ι}(π) ≅ V_{λ,t}^{ss}. Nothing follows about bad places or about semisimplicity of V_{λ,t}.

items.name: Order on Weil–Deligne monodromy types
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_q for a prime q ≠ p. Let 𝒲 be the set of classes of irreducible representations of the Weil group W_K over Q̄_p with open kernel, where s and s′ are equivalent if s′ ≅ s ⊗ (χ ∘ det) for an unramified character χ. A Weil–Deligne representation (σ, N) decomposes as ⊕_{ω∈𝒲} (σ[ω], N[ω]), where every irreducible subquotient of σ[ω] lies in ω. For each ω there are unique integers m_{1,ω}(σ,N) ≥ m_{2,ω}(σ,N) ≥ … ≥ 0 and s_1, s_2, … ∈ ω with σ[ω]^{Frob-ss} ≅ ⊕_i s_i ⊗ Sp(m_{i,ω}(σ,N)). Here Sp(m) is the indecomposable Weil–Deligne representation of dimension m whose monodromy is nilpotent of degree exactly m. The m_{i,ω}(σ,N) form a partition of dim σ[ω]/dim s for any s ∈ ω. Define (σ,N) ≺ (σ′,N′) if m_{1,ω}(σ,N) + ⋯ + m_{i,ω}(σ,N) ≤ m_{1,ω}(σ′,N′) + ⋯ + m_{i,ω}(σ′,N′) for every ω ∈ 𝒲 and every i ≥ 1. The relation is not strict. Suppose (σ,N) ≺ (σ′,N′), dim σ[ω] = dim σ′[ω], and σ[ω]^{Frob-ss} ≅ s ⊗ Sp(d) is a single block. Then σ′[ω]^{Frob-ss} ≅ s′ ⊗ Sp(d) for some s′ ∈ ω.
items.locator: Varma, arXiv:1411.2520v1, §9, Definition 1, p. 20; used in the proof of Lemma 4.3, p. 1273

items.name: Varma's away-from-p comparison with a monodromy bound
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM or totally real field, π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F), p a prime and ι: Q̄_p ≅ C. Let r_{p,ι}(π) be the continuous semisimple representation constructed by Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne and Scholze. Then for every finite place v ∤ p of F, WD(r_{p,ι}(π)|G_{F_v})^{Frob-ss} ≺ ι^{−1} rec_{F_v}(π_v |det|_v^{(1−n)/2}), where rec_{F_v} is normalized as in Harris–Taylor and ≺ is the order of Varma's Definition 1. The monodromy on the Galois side is bounded by that of rec_{F_v}, not asserted equal to it.

items.name: Steinberg local component from maximal monodromy
items.statement: Let t ∈ F′ with v(t) < 0 at an l-adic place v of F′. Suppose V_{λ,t} (or its semisimplification) is isomorphic to r_{l,ι}(π) for a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(A_{F′}). Let l′ be the auxiliary prime (odd, l′ ≠ l, l′ ∤ N) and λ′ | l′, and suppose V_{λ′,t} is semisimple. This holds for the point t of the proof of Theorem 1.1: there χ̄_2^{−1}V[λ′]_t ≅ Sym^{n−1} r̄_{E_0,l′}|G_{F′} is absolutely irreducible, so V_{λ′,t} is irreducible. Then V_{λ′,t} ≅ r_{l′,ι′}(π) for a compatible ι′: Q̄_{l′} ≅ C. By Lemma 3.12 (which needs v(t) < 0, correction E1), inertia at v acts unipotently on V_{λ′,t}, and its Weil–Deligne monodromy is a single Jordan block of size n. In particular a semisimple V_{λ′,t} is irreducible, since a nontrivial decomposition would split the block. By Varma's Theorem (1), this Frobenius-semisimplified Weil–Deligne representation is ≺ ι′^{−1}rec_{F′_v}(π_v|det|_v^{(1−n)/2}). Its partition (n), in the class of unramified characters, is maximal, so ι′^{−1}rec_{F′_v}(π_v|det|_v^{(1−n)/2}) is also an unramified character times a single Jordan block of size n. Hence π_v ≅ Sp_n(ψ_v|·|_v^{(1−n)/2}) for an unramified character ψ_v of F′_v^×. Without semisimplicity of V_{λ′,t}, compatibility gives only V_{λ′,t}^{ss} ≅ r_{l′,ι′}(π), and semisimplification can split the Jordan block.
items.locator: Lemma 4.3, first paragraph of the proof, p. 1273; Lemma 3.12 with correction E1

Input to Central-character slope identity for the Steinberg argument.

items.proofOutline: Lemma 3.12 gives a single Jordan block of size n for V_{λ′,t}|_{G_{F′_v}}, with unipotent inertia. Semisimplicity of V_{λ′,t} and the transport between coefficient primes give V_{λ′,t} ≅ r_{l′,ι′}(π). The Galois side is an unramified character times Sp(n), and the partition (n) is maximal. So Varma's bound forces ι′^{−1}rec_{F′_v}(π_v|det|_v^{(1−n)/2}) to be an unramified character times Sp(n), and local Langlands gives π_v ≅ Sp_n(ψ_v|·|_v^{(1−n)/2}) with ψ_v unramified.

items.name: Ordinarity of the automorphic Dwork realization at the original prime
items.statement: Let t ∈ F′ satisfy v(t) < 0 for every l-adic place v of F′. Suppose V_{λ,t} (or its semisimplification) is isomorphic to r_{l,ι}(π) with π regular algebraic cuspidal, and suppose V_{λ′,t} is semisimple (here equivalent to irreducible). The printed Lemma 4.3 omits this last hypothesis, which its proof uses. It holds for the t constructed in the proof of Theorem 1.1. Then π is ι-ordinary at every l-adic place, so V_{λ,t} (respectively V_{λ,t}^{ss}) is ι-ordinarily automorphic. Proof: π_v ≅ Sp_n(ψ_v|·|_v^{(1−n)/2}) with ψ_v unramified (Steinberg step). By Lemma 3.11, the Hodge–Tate weights of V_{λ,t} with respect to τ are λ_τ, λ_τ + 1, …, λ_τ + n − 1, so in Geraghty's notation the weight of π has λ_{τ,i} = −λ_τ for all i. By Geraghty's Lemma 5.2 it suffices to show that val_l(ι^{−1}ψ_v(det α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v})) = val_l(∏_τ τ(ϖ_v)^{−jλ_τ}) for j ∈ [0, n], and this follows from the central-character slope identity. This removes the weight-0 hypothesis of Geraghty's Lemma 5.6.
items.locator: Lemma 4.3 and its proof, p. 1273

items.proofOutline: By the Steinberg step, π_v ≅ Sp_n(ψ_v|·|_v^{(1−n)/2}) with ψ_v unramified. By Lemma 3.11 the labelled Hodge–Tate weights are λ_τ, …, λ_τ + n − 1, so π has parallel weight λ_{τ,i} = −λ_τ. The central-character identity gives val_l(ι^{−1}ψ_v(ϖ_v^j)) = val_l(∏_τ τ(ϖ_v)^{−jλ_τ}) for all j. The ordinarity criterion for a twisted Steinberg component (Geraghty, Lemmas 5.2 and 5.6) then gives ι-ordinarity at every v | l.
items.note: In the proof of Theorem 1.1 (p. 1273) the lemma is applied to the point t constructed in §4, and the conclusion is passed to V_{λ,t} ⊗ χ_1^{−1}. The paper uses χ_1 without defining it: it is the Teichmüller lift of χ̄_1, with values in W(k(λ))[1/l]^×, the coefficient field of V_{λ,t}. This step uses, without comment in the paper, that twisting by a finite-order character preserves ι-ordinary automorphy. The residual representation of V_{λ,t} ⊗ χ_1^{−1} is χ̄_1^{−1} ⊗ V[λ]_t ≅ r̄|_{G_{F′}}. Since r̄|_{G_{F′}} is semisimple (F′/F is Galois), it is the semisimplified reduction of V_{λ,t}^{ss} ⊗ χ_1^{−1}, which gives the conclusion of Theorem 1.1. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Central-character slope identity for the Steinberg argument
items.statement: Let v be an l-adic place of F′ with uniformizer ϖ_v. Let π be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_{F′}) such that, for each embedding τ: F′ → Q̄_l, the τ-labelled Hodge–Tate weights of r_{l,ι}(π) are λ_τ, λ_τ + 1, …, λ_τ + n − 1 for an integer λ_τ. This holds when r_{l,ι}(π) ≅ V_{λ,t}^{ss}, by Lemma 3.11, with λ_τ = M(a_τ); the integer λ_τ is unrelated to the prime λ. Let φ_π be the central character of π and r_{l,ι}(φ_π) the l-adic character attached to it. Then r_{l,ι}(φ_π) = det r_{l,ι}(π) · χ_cyc^{n(n−1)/2}, so r_{l,ι}(φ_π) has τ-labelled Hodge–Tate weight nλ_τ. Since r_{l,ι}(φ_π) takes values in l-adic units, val_l(ι^{−1}φ_{π,v}(ϖ_v)) = val_l(∏_{τ: F′_v → Q̄_l} τ(ϖ_v)^{−nλ_τ}). Suppose π_v ≅ Sp_n(ψ_v|·|_v^{(1−n)/2}), in the convention of Harris–Taylor and Geraghty, where the central character of this representation is ψ_v^n. Then for every j ∈ [0, n], val_l(ι^{−1}ψ_v(det α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v})) = (j/n)·val_l(ι^{−1}φ_{π,v}(ϖ_v)) = val_l(∏_τ τ(ϖ_v)^{−jλ_τ}), where α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v} = diag(ϖ_v, …, ϖ_v, 1, …, 1) with j entries ϖ_v.
items.locator: Lemma 4.3, last paragraph of the proof, p. 1273

uses.how: Input to Ordinarity of the automorphic Dwork realization at the original prime.

items.proofOutline: Compare the l-adic character of the central character with det r_{l,ι}(π) · χ_cyc^{n(n−1)/2}. Its labelled Hodge–Tate weights are nλ_τ. Evaluate at Art_{F′_v}(ϖ_v), where the Galois side is an l-adic unit, to get the valuation of ι^{−1}φ_{π,v}(ϖ_v). Use φ_{π,v} = ψ_v^n and det α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v} = ϖ_v^j, then divide by n and multiply by j.
items.note: Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, proof outline.

items.name: Preservation of decomposed genericity in the final base change
items.statement: Let F be a number field and r̄: G_F → GL_n(F̄_l) continuous, absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic. Let K/Q be a Galois extension linearly disjoint over Q from the Galois closure over Q of F̄^{ker r̄}(ζ_l). Then r̄|G_{FK} is absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic. In the proof of Theorem 1.4 this is applied with K = L′LF^suff(ζ_N), which is Galois over Q with K ∩ F^avoid = Q, and FK = F′. The paper asserts the disjointness for F′ itself, which is impossible because both fields contain F (correction E3).
items.locator: ACC+ (Allen et al., Ann. of Math. 197 (2023)), Lemma 7.1.7, p. 1091; applied in the proof of Theorem 1.4 (last paragraph of §4), p. 1274, with correction E3

uses.how: Input to Potential automorphy of a supplied ordinary lift: supported range.

items.proofOutline: Cited from ACC+ Lemma 7.1.7 (p. 1091). Let H be the Galois closure over Q of F̄^{ker r̄}(ζ_l). A Frobenius class in Gal(H/Q) that witnesses decomposed genericity lifts to (σ, 1) in Gal(HK/Q) = Gal(H/Q) × Gal(K/Q), and its primes witness decomposed genericity of r̄|_{G_{FK}}. In the proof of Theorem 1.4 it is applied with K = L′LF^suff(ζ_N) and FK = F′.

items.name: Galois ordinarity recovered from automorphic ordinarity
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field, ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F), regular algebraic of weight ιλ. Suppose that π is ι-ordinary at every l-adic place and that r̄_ι(π) is irreducible and decomposed generic. Then for every v | l, r_ι(π)|G_{F_v} is ordinary of weight λ, and its diagonal characters are given by the ordinary Hecke eigenvalues (ACC+ Corollary 5.5.2, deduced from Theorem 5.5.1). Remark 4.4 applies this, after Lemma 4.3, to V_{λ,t} ≅ r_{l,ι}(π) over F′ to recover ordinarity of V_{λ,t} at the l-adic places. That application needs the residual representation χ̄_1 ⊗ r̄|G_{F′} to be irreducible and decomposed generic. This holds under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.4, but not for an arbitrary semisimple r̄ as in Theorem 1.1. The converse, that automorphic and Galois-ordinary implies ι-ordinary, is not asserted without polarizability.
items.locator: Remark 4.4, p. 1274; ACC+ Theorem 5.5.1 (p. 991, restated p. 1026) and Corollary 5.5.2 (p. 1028)
items.proofOutline: Cited from ACC+ Corollary 5.5.2 (p. 1028). Its proof makes a solvable CM base change disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄_ι(π)}, which preserves ι-ordinarity by Geraghty's Lemma 5.7, and then applies ACC+ Theorem 5.5.1 and Lemma 6.2.11. Remark 4.4 applies it after Lemma 4.3, where the residual hypotheses must be checked separately.
items.note: The status stays missing. ACC+ Theorem 5.5.1, for the Hecke-algebra-valued representation, is planned in PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.2, but no stage plans the single-representation Corollary 5.5.2; the Allen et al. extraction also lists it as missing. That extraction records a gap in the proof of Corollary 5.5.2: the base change it uses must be chosen so that it preserves decomposed genericity, as Lemma 7.1.7 allows. Remark 4.4 also has misprints: 'Theorem 5.5.1 or [1]' should read 'of [1]', 'l-adic places v of F' should read F′, and 'ordinary as l′-adic representation' should read l-adic. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Dwork semistable blowup at reciprocal parameter
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k), and N > 1 with p ∤ N. Let Spec W[T,U^{±1}]' be the open subscheme of Spec W[T,U^{±1}] where (TU)^N ≠ 1, and let Y_N ⊂ P^{N−1} × Spec W[T,U^{±1}]' be the hypersurface UT(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N, with divisors D_i = {X_i = 0} and D = {X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N = 0}. Blow up Y_N along D ∩ D_N; then, for j = N−1, …, 1 in turn, blow up along the intersection of the strict transforms of D and of D_j. The result 𝕏 = Y_0 satisfies: (a) every centre is stable under H_0 = {(ξ_i) ∈ μ_N^N : ∏ξ_i = 1}/μ_N, so H_0 acts on 𝕏 and the blowdown 𝕏 → Y_N is H_0-equivariant; (b) the blowdown is an isomorphism over T ≠ 0; (c) locally on 𝕏 there is an étale map over W[T,U^{±1}]' to W[T,U^{±1}]'[Z_1,…,Z_r,Z_{r+1}^{±1},…,Z_m^{±1}]/(TU − Z_1⋯Z_r), and these charts can be chosen H_0-equivariant, with H_0 acting on the target coordinates through characters (Remark 2.2). Consequently, for a finite extension F/Q_p with residue field k, uniformiser π and u ∈ O_F^×, the base change along T ↦ π, U ↦ u is a semistable model with H_0-action of uπ(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N (the case d = 1 of item 092). The paper uses only the base change to C along U ↦ 1 and an isomorphism between an algebraic closure of W(k)[1/p] and C (Lemma 3.3(2), p. 1257): a blowup of T(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N over A^1 − μ_N which is an isomorphism away from T = 0 and whose fibre over T = 0 is a reduced normal-crossings divisor without self-crossings.
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, Lemma 2.1, Remark 2.2 and the paragraph after it, pp. 4–8; used in Lemma 3.3(2), p. 1257

items.name: Equivariant semistable model after ramified extension
items.statement: Let F be a finite extension of Q_p containing ζ_N, with p ∤ N and N > 1; let π be a uniformiser of O_F, k its residue field, W = W(k), and t = uπ^d ∈ F with u ∈ O_F^× and d = v(t) > 0. Then there are e ≥ 1 and, for F' = F(π^{1/e}) (totally ramified of degree e over F, with uniformiser π^{1/e}), a semistable model 𝒴 over O_{F'}, in the sense of Definition 1.3, of the fibre Z_{t^{-1}}: t(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N, with compatible H_0-action (Theorem 1.4 = Theorem 2.3). More precisely (Proposition 1.5), let Spec W[S,U^{±1}]' be the open subscheme of Spec W[S,U^{±1}] where (S^{de}U)^N ≠ 1. There is a scheme Z over W[S,U^{±1}]' with H_0-action which is an H_0-equivariant blowup of US^{de}(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N (the base change of UT(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N along T ↦ S^{de}), is an isomorphism outside S = 0, and locally admits an étale map over W[S,U^{±1}]' to W[U^{±1},S,Z_1,…,Z_r,Z_{r+1}^{±1},…,Z_m^{±1}]/(US − Z_1⋯Z_r); 𝒴 is the base change of Z along S ↦ π^{1/e}, U ↦ u. The scheme Z is obtained from the model of item 091, base changed along T ↦ S^{de}, by the blowup attached to a subdivision of the slice S = 1 of its conical complex into unimodular lattice simplices (lattice polytopes of lattice volume 1/d_α!, where d_α is the dimension). Being a blowup of a projective scheme, Z is projective, and so is 𝒴. Only semistability over F' is asserted, not over F.
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, Theorem 1.4 and Proposition 1.5, p. 3; restated as Theorem 2.3, p. 9; proof pp. 8–13 (the case d = 1 on p. 8)

items.proofOutline: Apply the equivariant toroidal semistable reduction theorem to 𝕏_d over W. By pp. 10–11 this is a toroidal embedding with open part R ≠ 0, whose cones have the product form ℝ_{≥0} × σ'. Take f = R and H = H_0; by Remark 2.2, H_0 fixes every boundary Cartier divisor. This gives e, a unimodular subdivision and an H_0-equivariant modification Z → 𝕏_{de}, with Z smooth over W and S = v·T_1⋯T_m in local charts. Since U is a primitive character of the local torus, a change of coordinates (p. 12) brings the charts to the form (1.1) over W[S,U^{±1}]'. Base change along S ↦ π^{1/e}, U ↦ u gives 𝒴, which is semistable over O_{F'}. Its generic fibre is the fibre of 𝕏_{de} over S = π^{1/e}, that is Z_{t^{-1}} ⊗ F' (p. 13).
items.note: Moved to the Dwork switching-motives Part II (PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII). It applies the equivariant toroidal semistable reduction theorem to 𝕏_d, the model of item 091 base changed along T ↦ R^d. SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.4 owns that theorem, and the Part II imports it. The item is not on the path to Theorems 1.1 and 1.4. The published paper uses the companion in four places. Lemma 2.1 (item 091) is used in the proof of Lemma 3.3(2), p. 1257, and that use is on the path. The companion's main result is mentioned on p. 1241 and in Remarks 3.13 and 4.4 (pp. 1268 and 1274), but the proof of Theorem 1.4 on p. 1274 does not use it. Condition (5) of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 asks only that the automorphic representation be ι-ordinary, and Lemma 4.3 (p. 1273) supplies this. Remark 3.13 states that 'The full strength of the main result of [14] is not needed in this paper'. Items 092–105 therefore support only Remarks 3.13 and 4.4 and the companion's main theorem. Of the material under gate S7, only the verification of the hand computation behind item 091 lies on the path to items 009 and 010. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Standard semistable logarithmic structures
items.statement: A scheme X over a discrete valuation ring A with uniformiser π has semistable reduction if, étale locally on X, there is a smooth morphism X → Spec A[T_1,…,T_r]/(T_1⋯T_r − π) for some r ≥ 0 (Definition 1.3, following Hyodo–Kato). Such an X carries the canonical log structure N of the Cartier divisor (π). With it, X is a log scheme over (Spec A, ℕ, 1 ↦ π), and its special fibre with the pullback log structure is a log scheme over the log point (k, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0). Remark 2.4 puts this log structure on the model 𝒴 over O_{F'} (divisor (π^{1/e})), and the analogous log structure M of the divisor (S) on Z over W[S,U^{±1}]'. The later comparisons use this log special fibre, not only its underlying singular scheme.
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, Definition 1.3, p. 3, and Remark 2.4, p. 13

items.name: Identification of the logarithmic special fibre with a Witt lift
items.statement: Let Z over W[S,U^{±1}]' be the H_0-equivariant scheme of Proposition 1.5 (item 092), with the log structure M of the divisor (S). Let 𝒴 = Z ⊗ O_{F'} (base change along S ↦ π^{1/e}, U ↦ u) carry the log structure 𝒩 of the Cartier divisor (π^{1/e}), and let (𝒴̄, 𝒩̄) be its special fibre with the pullback log structure, a log scheme over (k, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0). Choose u' ∈ W^× with the same image as u in k^×, and let Spec W[T]' be the open subscheme of Spec W[T] where (T^{de}u')^N ≠ 1. Let (Y, N) be the base change of (Z, M) along W[S,U^{±1}]' → W[T]', S ↦ T, U ↦ u', with the pullback log structure, and let (Ȳ_1, N̄_1) be its further base change along T ↦ 0 to k. Then: (a) (𝒴̄, 𝒩̄) ≅ (Ȳ_1, N̄_1) as log schemes over k with H_0-action, since both are the base change of (Z, M) along S ↦ 0, U ↦ ū; (b) Y is an H_0-equivariant blowup of the projective scheme u'T^{de}(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N over Spec W[T]', and hence is projective over Spec W[T]'; (c) by the charts (1.1) with U ↦ u', étale locally Y is étale over W[T]'[Z_1, …, Z_r, Z_{r+1}^{±1}, …, Z_m^{±1}]/(u'T − Z_1⋯Z_r), so (Y, N) is log smooth over (W[T]', ℕ, 1 ↦ T) and the comparison of items 098 and 099 applies to it.

items.name: Log-crystalline cohomology in the lifted semistable case
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W_n = W_n(k), and let (X, M) be a fine log scheme over the log point (Spec k, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0). In the application (X, M) is proper, log smooth and of Cartier type, for instance the log special fibre of a proper scheme with semistable reduction (item 093) or the fibre (Ȳ_1, N̄_1) of item 098. Give the ideal (p) ⊂ W_n its usual divided powers, which extend to every W_n-scheme. The i-th Hyodo–Kato (log-crystalline) cohomology is H^i_HK(X, M) = (lim_n H^i(((X, M)/(W_n, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0))_crys, O_{X/W_n}))[1/p], the limit taken along the maps induced by W_{n+1} → W_n. The finite-level groups and their transition maps are part of the datum. When (X, M) is proper, log smooth and of Cartier type, H^i_HK is a finite-dimensional W(k)[1/p]-vector space. Hyodo and Kato equip it with a Frobenius-semilinear bijection φ and a nilpotent linear monodromy operator N such that Nφ = pφN.

items.name: Base change of logarithmic differentials
items.statement: Let (X',M') → (X,M) over (Y',N') → (Y,N) be a cartesian square of log schemes, with g: X' → X. Then the natural map g^*ω^1_{(X,M)/(Y,N)} → ω^1_{(X',M')/(Y',N')} is an isomorphism (Lemma 3.1, quoting Ogus, Lectures on logarithmic algebraic geometry, Proposition IV.1.3.1), and hence so is g^*ω^i → ω^i for every i. The lemma is used in the proof of Theorem 3.2 (steps (i) and (ii)) and in (4.1), as follows: when the ω^i_{(X,M)/(Y,N)} are locally free (for instance when (X,M) is log smooth over (Y,N)), the termwise pullback of the log de Rham complex is the log de Rham complex of the base change.
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, Lemma 3.1, p. 13 (quoting Ogus, Lectures on logarithmic algebraic geometry, Proposition IV.1.3.1)

items.name: The logarithmic monodromy triangle
items.statement: Let A be a ring and let (X, M) be a fine log scheme, log smooth over the standard log point (Spec A, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0). In the applications A is W, W_n or C, and the same construction is made over the analytic log point (pt, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0). Identify ω^1_{(A,ℕ,1↦0)/(A,(0))} with A by dlog 1 ↦ 1. Then the sequence 0 → O_X → ω^1_{X/(A,(0))} → ω^1_{X/(A,ℕ,1↦0)} → 0, whose first map is multiplication by dlog 1, is a locally split exact sequence of locally free O_X-modules of finite rank (Ogus, Lectures on logarithmic algebraic geometry, Theorem IV.3.2.3). Taking exterior powers gives, for every i ≥ 1, locally split exact sequences 0 → ω^{i−1}_{X/(A,ℕ,1↦0)} → ω^i_{X/(A,(0))} → ω^i_{X/(A,ℕ,1↦0)} → 0, with first map η ↦ dlog 1 ∧ η̃ for any lift η̃ of η (Remark 1.7). These sequences are compatible with the log de Rham differentials and form an exact triangle dR_{X/(A,ℕ,1↦0)}[−1] → dR_{X/(A,(0))} → dR_{X/(A,ℕ,1↦0)} →. The monodromy operator N on H^i(dR_{X/(A,ℕ,1↦0)}) is by definition the degree-i connecting homomorphism of this triangle. The construction is natural in (X, M), so N commutes with automorphisms of (X, M) over the log point and, by item 096, with base change in A.

items.name: Lifted log-crystalline/de Rham comparison with monodromy
items.statement: Let Spec W[T]' ⊂ Spec W[T] be an affine open subscheme containing the closed subscheme T = 0. Let (Y, N) be a fine log scheme, log smooth over (W[T]', ℕ, 1 ↦ T), with Y proper over Spec W[T]'. Let (Ȳ, N̄) be its base change along (W, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0) → (W[T]', ℕ, 1 ↦ T), T ↦ 0, and let (Ȳ_n, N̄_n) be its base change to (W_n, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0); in particular (Ȳ_1, N̄_1) is log smooth over (k, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0). (a) For every n ≥ 1 there is an isomorphism H^i(((Ȳ_1, N̄_1)/(W_n, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0))_crys, O_{Ȳ_1/W_n}) ≅ H^i(dR_{Ȳ_n/(W_n,ℕ,1↦0)}). It carries the Hyodo–Kato monodromy operator to the degree-i connecting homomorphism of the dlog 1 triangle of item 097 over W_n, and the transition maps to the pullback maps from level n+1 to level n. (b) Consequently (lim_n H^i(((Ȳ_1, N̄_1)/(W_n, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0))_crys, O_{Ȳ_1/W_n}))[1/p] ≅ H^i(dR_{Ȳ/(W,ℕ,1↦0)})[1/p]. Under this isomorphism the Hyodo–Kato monodromy operator N on the left corresponds to the degree-i connecting homomorphism of the triangle dR_{Ȳ/(W,ℕ,1↦0)}[−1] → dR_{Ȳ/(W,(0))} → dR_{Ȳ/(W,ℕ,1↦0)} → of item 097. These isomorphisms are natural in (Y, N), so they commute with automorphisms of (Y, N) over (W[T]', ℕ, 1 ↦ T).
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, Theorem 1.6, p. 4, restated as Theorem 3.2, p. 14, proof pp. 14–18

uses.how: Input to Negative-valuation Dwork local ordinary conclusion in the selected family.

items.proofOutline: Step (i). Apply the embedding description of log-crystalline cohomology to the exact closed immersion Ȳ_1 ↪ Ȳ_n over (W_n, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0). Its ideal is generated by p, so the log PD envelope is Ȳ_n itself, and the finite-level isomorphism follows. For N-equivariance, take Hyodo–Kato's triangle for Ȳ_1 ↪ Y_n over (W_n[T]', ℕ, 1 ↦ T), realised by the chain maps (3.3), tensor it down to W_n, and compare it with the dlog 1 triangle through the diagram on p. 17. Its outer columns are isomorphisms by local freeness and item 096. Steps (ii) and (iii). Item 099 gives the N-equivariant identification lim_n H^i(dR_{Ȳ_n/(W_n,ℕ,1↦0)}) ≅ H^i(dR_{Ȳ/(W,ℕ,1↦0)}); then invert p.
items.note: Properness of Y is not in the printed Theorems 1.6 and 3.2, but step (iii) of the proof uses that each H^j(dR_{Ȳ/(W,ℕ,1↦0)}) is finitely generated over W, and that requires properness (E12). The statement is general. The Dwork identification of item 094 is combined with it only in item 105 and in the companion's main theorem. The item is missing: CR.6 plans the comparison of Hyodo–Kato cohomology with the de Rham cohomology of the generic fibre, not this N-equivariant comparison with the log de Rham cohomology of a Witt lift over the log point. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Finite-level torsion exact sequence and its limit
items.statement: Let (Y, N) be log smooth over (W[T]', ℕ, 1 ↦ T), with Y proper over an affine open subscheme Spec W[T]' of Spec W[T] containing T = 0. Let (Ȳ, N̄) and (Ȳ_n, N̄_n) be its base changes to (W, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0) and to (W_n, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0), and write H^j = H^j(dR_{Ȳ/(W,ℕ,1↦0)}); these are finitely generated W-modules because Ȳ is proper over W. Then for all i and all n ≥ 1 there is a short exact sequence 0 → H^i/p^n → H^i(dR_{Ȳ_n/(W_n,ℕ,1↦0)}) → H^{i+1}[p^n] → 0 (3.5). The sequences for n+1 and n form a commutative diagram (3.6) whose vertical maps are reduction on the left, pullback in the middle and multiplication by p on the right. The first map of (3.5) commutes with the operators N of item 097 over W and over W_n. Consequently lim_n H^{i+1}[p^n] = 0 for the transition maps given by multiplication by p, and the natural map H^i → lim_n H^i(dR_{Ȳ_n/(W_n,ℕ,1↦0)}) is an N-equivariant isomorphism.
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, proof of Theorem 3.2, steps (ii)–(iii), displays (3.2), (3.5) and (3.6), pp. 15 and 17–18

uses.how: Input to Lifted log-crystalline/de Rham comparison with monodromy.

items.proofOutline: Ȳ is log smooth over (W, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0), hence flat over W, and the terms of its log de Rham complexes are locally free. So item 096 gives Li_n^* dR_Ȳ = dR_{Ȳ_n}, and base change for the derived pushforward gives Rπ_* dR_Ȳ ⊗^L_W W_n ≅ Rπ_{n,*} dR_{Ȳ_n}, compatibly with the dlog 1 triangles. Applying this to the triangle W → W → W_n, whose first map is multiplication by p^n, gives (3.5); the morphism of these triangles from p^{n+1} to p^n gives (3.6). Finite generation, which comes from properness, makes H^i p-adically complete and bounds the p-power torsion of H^{i+1}. Hence a composite of finitely many transition maps of the torsion system is zero, and its inverse limit vanishes.
items.note: Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Proper logarithmic GAGA with monodromy
items.statement: Let (X, M) be a fine log scheme, log smooth over the log point (Spec C, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0), with X proper over C, and let (X^an, M^an) be its analytification, log smooth over the analytic log point (pt, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0). For every log scheme (X, M) over a log scheme (Z, L) locally of finite type over C, the pullback of ω^i_{(X,M)/(Z,L)} along the analytification morphism X^an → X is ω^i_{(X^an,M^an)/(Z^an,L^an)}. So the analytic log de Rham complexes are the termwise analytifications of the algebraic ones, compatibly with the dlog 1 triangles of item 097. Consequently, for every i, analytification gives an isomorphism H^i(dR_{X/(C,ℕ,1↦0)}) ≅ H^i(dR_{X^an/(pt,ℕ,1↦0)}) that commutes with the operators N, defined on both sides as the degree-i connecting homomorphisms of the dlog 1 triangles. The isomorphism is natural in (X, M), so it commutes with automorphisms of (X, M) over the log point.
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, Theorem 1.8, p. 4, proved as Proposition 3.6, pp. 18–19

uses.how: Input to Residue of Gauss–Manin and analytic monodromy.

items.proofOutline: Apply coherent proper GAGA to each logarithmic differential bundle and to the dlog exact triangle; compare hypercohomology and connecting N.

items.name: Residue of the Gauss–Manin connection and monodromy for a log smooth degeneration over a disc
items.statement: Let S ⊂ C be an open disc around 0 with coordinate T and the log structure ℕ → O_S, 1 ↦ T. Let π: (Y, M) → (S, ℕ, 1 ↦ T) be a proper, log smooth morphism of fine analytic log spaces which is smooth with trivial log structure over S − {0}. The case needed is the analytification of a scheme with semistable reduction over an open subset of A^1_C containing 0, with M the log structure of the divisor T = 0. Let (Y_0, M_0) be the fibre over 0, log smooth over the analytic log point (pt, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0). Then the following hold. (a) For every i, R^iπ_* dR_{Y/(S,ℕ,1↦T)} is a locally free O_S-module of finite rank, and base change gives an isomorphism R^iπ_* dR_{Y/(S,ℕ,1↦T)} ⊗_{O_S} O_S/(T) ≅ H^i(dR_{Y_0/(pt,ℕ,1↦0)}). (b) Identify ω^1_{(S,ℕ,1↦T)/C} with O_S by dlog T ↦ 1. The Gauss–Manin connection on R^iπ_* dR_{Y/(S,ℕ,1↦T)} is then the degree-i connecting homomorphism obtained by applying Rπ_* to the exact triangle dR_{Y/(S,ℕ,1↦T)}[−1] → dR_{Y/(pt,(0))} → dR_{Y/(S,ℕ,1↦T)} →, whose first map is wedge product with dlog T. The isomorphism of (a) carries its residue at 0 to the operator N on H^i(dR_{Y_0/(pt,ℕ,1↦0)}) defined by the dlog 1 triangle. (c) For s ∈ S − {0}, the monodromy T_s around 0 of the local system R^iπ_*C on S − {0}, acting on its fibre at s, is conjugate to exp(−2πiN) acting on H^i(dR_{Y_0/(pt,ℕ,1↦0)}), in Illusie's convention. (d) All of this is natural in (Y, M). It therefore commutes with any finite group H acting on (Y, M) over (S, ℕ, 1 ↦ T), and it restricts to the χ-eigenparts for every character χ: H → C^×. (e) Suppose that over S − {0} the family is the pullback, along T ↦ T^e, of a family over a punctured disc whose local system R^i has monodromy T' around 0. Then T_s is conjugate to T'^e. Consequently, on every H-eigenpart on which T' is maximally unipotent, T_s is maximally unipotent, because a positive power of a maximally unipotent operator in characteristic 0 is maximally unipotent, and N is maximally nilpotent.
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, §4, display (4.1), Lemma 4.3 and the final paragraph, pp. 21–23; Illusie, Autour du théorème de monodromie locale (Astérisque 223), 2.2.1.2–2.2.1.3, 2.2.2 and Corollary 2.2.3

uses.how: Input to Negative-valuation Dwork local ordinary conclusion in the selected family.

items.proofOutline: (a) and (c): Illusie 2.2.2 and Corollary 2.2.3. Illusie's derived fibre of dR_{Y/S} at 0 is identified with dR_{Y_0/(pt,ℕ,1↦0)} by local freeness and item 096. (b): proper base change for Rπ_* along 0 → S, with the morphism of triangles on pp. 22–23. (d): naturality. (e): pulling a local system back along the e-fold cover of the punctured disc raises its monodromy to the e-th power. Then N = −(2πi)^{-1} log T_s, and the linear algebra of item 048 gives maximal nilpotence.
items.note: Routed to the proposed Part II of the Tau Ceti Hodge structures roadmap, 'Hodge structures (pure, mixed, and polarized), Part II: variations, period maps and non-abelian Hodge theory' (HodgeStructuresPartII). That Part II plans the Deligne canonical extension and its logarithmic de Rham comparison; this item computes the residue of that extension for a log smooth degeneration. The result is Steenbrink's theorem in the logarithmic form of Illusie, Autour du théorème de monodromie locale (Astérisque 223, Exposé I), 2.2.2 and Corollary 2.2.3. The comparison of residues in (b) is the companion's Lemma 4.3 (pp. 22–23). Illusie was not read at source level; the hypotheses are those under which the companion applies 2.2.2. In the application (p. 23) the disc must be small enough to lie in the image of Spec W[T]'. The family is Y over C, whose restriction to the punctured disc is the pullback along T ↦ T^{de} of u'T(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N, so T_s is identified with ρ_s(γ_∞)^{de}. Imports: the canonical extension (HodgeStructuresPartII); the Gauss–Manin connection and coherent GAGA (ComplexComparisonPartII C2, C3, C5); log differentials (CrystallineCohomology CR.5:log-algebra, CR.5); the finite logarithm and maximal nilpotence (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.1, item 048). Searched: the pinned libraries have no Gauss–Manin connections and no log structures. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, name, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Equivariant semistable comparison on character eigenparts (Tsuji)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with residue field k and maximal unramified subfield K_0 = W(k)[1/p], and fix a uniformiser ϖ of O_K. Let 𝒳 be a proper O_K-scheme with semistable reduction (item 093), with generic fibre X_K and log special fibre (𝒳̄, 𝒩̄) over (k, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0). Let H^i_HK be the Hyodo–Kato cohomology of (𝒳̄, 𝒩̄) (item 095), a (φ, N)-module over K_0. Let a finite group H act on 𝒳 by O_K-automorphisms, let E be an algebraic extension of Q_p containing a copy of K_0, let χ: H → E^× be a character, and let V^χ be the χ-eigenpart of H acting on H^i_ét(X_{K̄}, Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} E. Then V^χ is semistable, and Tsuji's semistable comparison isomorphism for 𝒳 is H-equivariant. For every embedding τ: K_0 ↪ E it induces an isomorphism D_st,τ(V^χ) = (V^χ ⊗_{τ,K_0} B_st)^{G_K} ≅ (H^i_HK ⊗_{K_0,τ} E)^{H=χ} compatible with N. When χ takes values in τ(K_0), the right side equals (H^i_HK)^{H=τ^{-1}∘χ} ⊗_{K_0,τ} E. Summed over τ, these give an isomorphism of filtered (φ, N)-modules (V^χ ⊗_{Q_p} B_st)^{G_K} ≅ (H^i_HK ⊗_{Q_p} E)^{H=χ}. On it φ carries the τ-component to the τ∘Frob^{-1}-component, where Frob is the absolute Frobenius of K_0. After extending scalars from K_0 to K, the filtration is the one induced on (H^i_dR(X_K) ⊗_{Q_p} E)^{H=χ} by the Hodge filtration, transported by the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism H^i_HK ⊗_{K_0} K ≅ H^i_dR(X_K) attached to ϖ.
items.locator: Tsuji, p-adic étale cohomology and crystalline cohomology in the semi-stable reduction case, Invent. Math. 137 (1999), no. 2, 233–411, main comparison theorem; applied in eigenpart form in arXiv:2103.00106v1, §4, p. 21, with the definition of D_st,σ at the foot of p. 20

uses.how: Input to Negative-valuation Dwork local ordinary conclusion in the selected family.

items.proofOutline: Apply Tsuji's C_st to 𝒳. Naturality for the automorphisms h ∈ H of the log scheme 𝒳 over O_K makes the comparison H-equivariant. Take χ-eigenparts; the eigenprojectors exist because #H is invertible in E. Then decompose K_0 ⊗_{Q_p} E ≅ ∏_τ E.
items.note: Planned at CohomologyComparisons CP.4. CP.4 plans 'the B_st comparison for proper flat semistable O_K-formal models' with 'compatibility with G_K, Frobenius, monodromy and filtration', followed by 'Transport to the admitted algebraic models by formal comparison'. Equivariance and the passage to eigenparts follow from the naturality of the comparison for automorphisms of the model. Extending coefficients along τ replaces χ by τ^{-1}∘χ on the K_0-structure. Tsuji's theorem, the source the companion cites, is an admissible source beside Česnavičius–Koshikawa, the atlas's source. The Dwork case (arXiv:2103.00106v1, p. 21) is a separate new item in the Dwork switching-motives Part II. Searched: Mathlib has B_dR^+ and B_dR, but no B_st, no period functors and no Hyodo–Kato cohomology. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, name, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Semistable maximal-monodromy ordinarity with Hodge bounds
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with maximal unramified subfield K_0, and let r: G_K → GL_n(Q̄_p) be semistable. Suppose that for every embedding τ: K ↪ Q̄_p, dim gr^i (r ⊗_{τ,K} B_dR)^{G_K} = 1 for i = 0, 1, …, n−1 and 0 for all other i. Suppose also that for some (equivalently every) embedding τ: K_0 ↪ Q̄_p and each j = 1, …, n−1, the kernel of N^j on D_st,τ(r) = (r ⊗_{τ,K_0} B_st)^{G_K} has dimension j. Then r is ordinary of regular weight λ = 0 in the sense of Definition 1.2 (item 002). That is, there is a G_K-stable full flag 0 = V_0 ⊂ V_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ V_n = Q̄_p^n such that G_K acts on each V_i/V_{i−1} by a character ψ_i with ψ_i(σ) = ∏_{τ: K ↪ Q̄_p} τ(Art_K^{-1}(σ))^{−(i−1)} for all σ in an open subgroup of the inertia group I_K, where Art_K sends uniformisers to geometric Frobenius elements. More generally, suppose that for each τ: K ↪ Q̄_p the labelled Hodge–Tate weights of r (the i with gr^i (r ⊗_{τ,K} B_dR)^{G_K} ≠ 0) are c_τ, c_τ + 1, …, c_τ + n − 1, each with multiplicity one, and that the kernel condition on N holds. Then r is ordinary of regular weight λ with λ_{τ,i} = c_τ for all i. To see this, apply the first assertion to r ⊗ ψ, where ψ is a crystalline character with labelled Hodge–Tate weights −c_τ; twisting by ψ does not change the kernels of N^j.
items.locator: Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor, A family of Calabi–Yau varieties and potential automorphy II (Publ. RIMS 47 (2011) 29–98), Lemma 2.2(2), author's preprint p. 18, with the definition of 'ordinary of weight a' on p. 17; corrects arXiv:2103.00106v1, Lemma 4.2, p. 20 (E11)

uses.how: Input to Negative-valuation Dwork local ordinary conclusion in the selected family.

items.proofOutline: With labelled weights 0, …, n−1, the kernels of N^j form a (φ, N)-stable flag in D_st. The Hodge bounds force each step to be a weakly admissible sub-object, and admissibility turns the flag into the ordinary flag with the stated inertia characters (BLGHT Lemma 2.2(2), proved like Geraghty's Lemma 2.7.6). For the shifted form, twist by a crystalline character ψ with labelled weights −c_τ (a product of Lubin–Tate characters). This leaves the N^j unchanged. Then multiply the graded characters by ψ^{-1}, which on inertia is ∏_τ τ(Art_K^{-1}(·))^{−c_τ}. Without the weight hypothesis the conclusion fails (E11).
items.note: BLGHT state Lemma 2.2(2) for a global representation, at every place above l; the assertion is local. 'Ordinary' here is the notion of Definition 1.2 (item 002), which is word for word condition (2) of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2. BLGHT's 'ordinary of weight a' is the same notion with λ = a, with the same normalisation of Art_K. The consecutive-weight hypothesis cannot be dropped: maximal nilpotence of N alone does not imply ordinarity (E11). This corrects arXiv:2103.00106v1, Lemma 4.2 (p. 20). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, proof outline.

items.name: Descent of regular ordinarity
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p and r: G_K → GL_n(Q̄_p) a continuous representation. Suppose that for some finite extension L/K the restriction r|G_L is de Rham and ordinary of some regular weight λ' in the sense of Definition 1.2 (item 002). Then r is de Rham, and λ'_{τ',i} depends only on the restriction of τ': L ↪ Q̄_p to K. Moreover r is ordinary of regular weight λ, where λ_{τ,i} = λ'_{τ',i} for any τ' extending τ: K ↪ Q̄_p. Every G_L-stable flag as in Definition 1.2 is G_K-stable.

uses.how: Input to Negative-valuation Dwork local ordinary conclusion in the selected family.

items.proofOutline: Pass to a Galois finite extension. Strictly ordered labelled ordinary character weights imply uniqueness of the first stable line, hence invariance under the whole group; repeat on the quotient.
items.note: Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator.

items.name: Negative-valuation Dwork local ordinary conclusion in the selected family
items.statement: Let λ be a prime of Z[ζ_N] (of Z[ζ_N]^+ when n = 2, as in §3) whose residue characteristic l is odd and prime to N. Let F_v be a finite extension of Q_l containing ζ_N, and let χ be the character of H_0 fixed in §3, whose exponent vector (p. 1253) contains 0. Let t ∈ F_v with v(t) < 0, and regard V_{λ,t} as a representation of G_{F_v}. (1) There is a finite totally ramified extension F'_v/F_v such that V_{λ,t}|G_{F'_v} is semistable. For every embedding σ of the maximal unramified subfield of F'_v into an algebraic closure of Q(ζ_N)_λ, the monodromy operator N on D_st,σ(V_{λ,t}|G_{F'_v}) is maximally nilpotent. (2) V_{λ,t} is ordinary of regular weight μ in the sense of Definition 1.2 (item 002), where μ_{σ,i} = M(a_σ) for every embedding σ: F_v ↪ \overline{Q(ζ_N)_λ} and every i. Here σ^{-1}(ζ_N) = ζ_N^{a_σ}, and M(a) is the integer of Lemma 3.10 (item 066).
items.locator: Remark 3.13, p. 1268, with Lemma 3.11(1), pp. 1266–1267; arXiv:2103.00106v1, Theorem 1.1, p. 2, proved in §4, pp. 19–23
items.proofOutline: Put s = t^{-1}, so that v(s) > 0. Item 092 gives e, F'_v and the semistable model 𝒴 of the fibre. The Dwork case of the semistable comparison identifies D_st,σ with the σ^{-1}χ-eigenpart of H^{N−2}_HK of the log special fibre of 𝒴, and item 094 identifies that special fibre with the one of the Witt lift Y. Item 098 identifies this Hyodo–Kato cohomology, with its N, with the log de Rham cohomology of Ȳ over (W, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0) and its dlog 1 operator. After base change along an embedding W → C, items 100 and 101 identify N on the conjugate eigenpart with the residue at 0 of the Gauss–Manin connection. By item 101, exp(−2πiN) is conjugate to the monodromy ρ_s(γ_∞)^{de}, which is maximally unipotent by item 049. Hence N is maximally nilpotent. For (2), the labelled Hodge–Tate weights at every embedding are M(a_σ), …, M(a_σ) + n − 1 (item 068). The twisted form of item 103 then gives ordinarity of regular weight μ over F'_v, and item 104 descends it to F_v.
items.note: Not on the path to Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 in the published version. Assertion (1) is what Remark 3.13 (p. 1268) records as a consequence of the proof of the companion's main theorem. The remark says 'semistable', but the companion proves semistability only over the totally ramified extension F'_v (its Theorem 1.4, p. 3). The paper says 'The full strength of the main result of [14] is not needed in this paper'. The proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 need only that the automorphic representation π with r_{l,ι}(π) ≅ V_{λ,t} is ι-ordinary at the places above l, and Lemma 4.3 (p. 1273) proves this by a Steinberg argument. For the point t constructed there, Remark 4.4 (p. 1274) recovers ordinarity of V_{λ,t} from ACC+ Theorem 5.5.1. In arXiv v1 the corresponding statement was Lemma 3.10(4): stated on p. 20, proved on p. 21 ('This is the main theorem of [Qia21]') and used in the proof of Theorem 1.1 on p. 24. The journal version replaced it by Lemma 4.3. Assertion (2) does not follow from maximal nilpotence alone (E11); it uses the consecutive labelled weights of Lemma 3.11(1). The proof also needs maximal unipotence at ∞ for the Galois-conjugate characters that appear after coefficients are extended along the chosen embeddings. This follows from Corollary 3.5 (item 049), because the coefficient automorphism carries the χ-eigenpart to its conjugates compatibly with monodromy. The companion's Remark 1.2 also gives it, since 0 occurs among the a_i. Gate S8 therefore does not block items 009 and 010, and of gate S7 only the verification of the hand computation behind item 091 lies on their path. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Size of the Kummer local-global kernel
items.statement: Let K be a number field, p a prime and r ≥ 1. Then Ш^1(K, μ_{p^r}) is either 0 or cyclic of order 2, and it can be nonzero only when p = 2.
items.locator: Lemma 2.2, first assertion, p. 1246; proof p. 1247, citing Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Cohomology of Number Fields, Proposition 9.1.6 (the paper calls the lemma essentially their Theorem 9.1.9)

uses.how: Input to Roots of finite-field-valued characters with avoidance.
Input to Killing the remaining two-primary obstruction.

items.proofOutline: By the inflation identification, Ш^1(K, μ_{p^r}) is isomorphic to the subgroup Ш^1(K(μ_{p^r})/K, μ_{p^r}) of H^1(Gal(K(μ_{p^r})/K), μ_{p^r}). By Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Proposition 9.1.6, that group is 0 or Z/2Z, and it is nonzero only for p = 2.
items.note: The proof gives more. Ш^1(K, μ_{p^r}) vanishes unless p = 2, r ≥ 2 and −1 lies in the image of the cyclotomic character Gal(K(μ_{2^r})/K) → (Z/2^rZ)^×. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Rank of the three-punctured Betti local system
items.statement: For n > 2, V_B' is a locally free sheaf of Z[ζ_N]-modules of rank n on T_0'(C); its stalk V'_{B,t'} carries the monodromy representation ρ_{t'}.
items.locator: Proposition 3.2, assertion for V_B', p. 1257

uses.how: Input to Monodromy generators with fixed orientation.

items.proofOutline: Pull back V_B' through the surjective finite étale cover to the known rank-n V_B; rank is locally constant and descends.
items.note: The printed proof of Proposition 3.2 checks the rank at the fibre over 0, which does not lie over T_0'. For V_B' the rank therefore follows only after pulling back along t ↦ t^N to V_B on T_0(C) − {0} (item 038). For n = 2 the analogous object is BLGHT's Ṽ_B, since the family Y' is not stable under ς (item 038). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator.

items.name: Rank-two full monodromy over the real coefficient field
items.statement: Let n = 2, t ∈ T_0(C), and λ a nonzero prime of Z[1/2N, ζ_N]^+ with residue field k(λ). Then the residual monodromy π_1(T_0(C), t) → GL(V_{B,t}/λ) has image Sp(V_{B,t}/λ) = SL(V_{B,t}/λ) ≅ SL_2(k(λ)) (BLGHT Corollary 4.7). Here V_B is BLGHT's real-coefficient local system, and k(λ) is a residue field of the real cyclotomic ring, whose degree over F_l need not be the order of l modulo N.
items.locator: §3, paragraph after Proposition 3.2, p. 1257, citing BLGHT Corollary 4.7; for the three-punctured line, the proof of Lemma 3.7, p. 1259, cites BLGHT Lemma 4.6

uses.how: Input to Two-prime product monodromy.

items.proofOutline: Use BLGHT's rank-two real-coefficient monodromy result and identify Sp2 with SL2. The remaining full corollary proof is S2.
items.note: Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator.

items.name: Varma's semisimplified local–global compatibility
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM or totally real field, π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F), p a prime and ι: Q̄_p ≅ C. Let r_{p,ι}(π) be the continuous semisimple representation constructed by Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne and Scholze. Then for every finite place v ∤ p of F, WD(r_{p,ι}(π)|G_{F_v})^{ss} ≅ ι^{−1} rec_{F_v}(π_v ⊗ |det|_v^{(1−n)/2})^{ss}, with rec_{F_v} normalized as in Harris–Taylor. This forgets the monodromy operator and is weaker than full Weil–Deligne compatibility.
items.locator: Varma, arXiv:1411.2520v1, Theorem (1^ss), p. 1; input to the proof of Lemma 4.3, p. 1273

uses.how: Input to Varma's away-from-p comparison with a monodromy bound.

items.proofOutline: Cited, not proved in the paper: Varma, arXiv:1411.2520v1, Theorem (1^ss), valid at every finite place v ∤ p. It is separate from the monodromy bound of Theorem (1).
items.note: Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, planning stages, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Real-coefficient descent of the rank-two Gauss product
items.statement: Let n = 2, so that B = {(N−1)/2, (N+1)/2} = −B, and let v be a place of F whose residue characteristic p divides neither N nor l. Then g(v,b_1)g(v,b_2) lies in Q_l(ζ_N)⁺ = Q_l(ζ_N + ζ_N^{-1}) ⊂ Q̄_l. Proof sketch. An automorphism σ of Q̄_l fixing Q_l(ζ_N)⁺ acts on N-th roots of unity by ζ ↦ ζ^{±1} and on p-th roots of unity by ζ_p ↦ ζ_p^a for some a ∈ F_p^×. The substitutions of (3.2) and (3.3) together give σ(g(v,b)) = t(a^{(q−1)/N})^{±b} g(v,±b). Hence σ(g(v,b_1)g(v,b_2)) = t(a^{(q−1)/N})^{±(b_1+b_2)} g(v,±b_1)g(v,±b_2) = g(v,b_1)g(v,b_2), because b_1 + b_2 ≡ 0 mod N and B = −B.
items.locator: Lemma 3.9, proof, case n = 2, equation (3.3), pp. 1263–1264

uses.how: Input to Determinant image is an n-th power after a quadratic coefficient extension.

items.proofOutline: Let σ ∈ G_{Q_l(ζ_N)⁺}. It sends ζ_N to ζ_N^ε with ε = ±1, and ζ_p to ζ_p^a with a ∈ F_p^×. The change of additive character (item 060) gives σ(g(v,b)) = t(a^{(q−1)/N})^{εb} g(v,εb). Multiply over B = {b_1, b_2}. The root-of-unity factors cancel because b_1 + b_2 ≡ 0 mod N, and εB = B. So the product is fixed by G_{Q_l(ζ_N)⁺} and lies in Q_l(ζ_N)⁺.
items.note: The printed proof (pp. 1263–1264) uses one σ ∈ G_{Q_l(ζ_N)⁺} with σ(ζ_N) = ζ_N^{-1} and σ(ζ_p) = ζ_p, where p is the residue characteristic of v. Such a σ need not exist. Take n = 2, l = 3, N = 301 = 7·43 (odd, greater than 300 and prime to 6) and p = 5. The extension Q_3(ζ_301, ζ_5)/Q_3 is unramified, and its Galois group is cyclic, generated by Frobenius, which raises roots of unity of order prime to 3 to the third power. Frob^k inverts ζ_301 only when 3^k ≡ −1 mod 301, that is k ≡ 21 mod 42, so k is odd. Frob^k fixes ζ_5 only when 4 | k. The argument in the statement treats every σ fixing Q_l(ζ_N)⁺ and needs no such choice, so the conclusion of Lemma 3.9 is unaffected. Section 4 never needs this case. There −1 is not a power of l modulo N, because for n = 2 the order r of l modulo N is even and N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1 (p. 1268). Hence Q_l(ζ_N)⁺ = Q_l(ζ_N), and at the auxiliary prime l′ ≡ 1 mod N one has Q_{l′}(ζ_N) = Q_{l′}. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23: statement, locator, dependencies, proof outline.

items.name: Residually automorphic representation
items.statement: Let E be a CM or totally real field and ι: Q̄_l ≅ C the fixed isomorphism. A continuous representation r̄: G_E → GL_n(F̄_l) is automorphic if it has a lift r: G_E → GL_n(Q̄_l) that is automorphic (Definition 1.3). Under the convention of ACC+ §1.2, the residual representation of r is the semisimplification of its reduction. So this means r̄ is isomorphic to the residual representation of r_{l,ι}(π) for some regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(A_E). In particular such an r̄ is semisimple, as it is in every application (Theorem 1.1 assumes semisimplicity). The witness keeps E, l, ι and π.
items.locator: Definition 1.3, p. 1241 (second sentence)

items.name: Continuous second cohomology carrier
items.statement: Let G be a topological group acting continuously on a topological abelian group M. The continuous 2-cocycles are the continuous maps f: G × G → M with g·f(h, k) − f(gh, k) + f(g, hk) − f(g, h) = 0 for all g, h, k ∈ G. The 2-coboundaries are the maps (g, h) ↦ g·c(h) − c(gh) + c(g) for continuous c: G → M, and H^2(G, M) = Z^2/B^2 is the quotient group. In the paper G is a Galois group with its Krull topology and M is a finite discrete module; only the group structure of H^2 is used.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1, pp. 1245–1248 (the obstruction group H^2(G_M, Z/mZ), its localizations and its restrictions to G_{F_2} and G_{F_1})
