items.name: Regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation
items.statement: Let E be a number field and ξ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(E,C)}, where Z^n_+ = {(a_1,…,a_n) ∈ Z^n : a_1 ≥ … ≥ a_n}. An irreducible admissible representation π of GL_n(A_E) is regular algebraic of weight ξ if the infinitesimal character of π_∞ equals that of V_ξ^∨. Here V_ξ is the irreducible algebraic representation of Res_{E/Q} GL_n with highest weight ξ. π is regular algebraic if it is regular algebraic of some weight. π is a cuspidal automorphic representation if it is isomorphic to a subquotient of the space of cusp forms on GL_n(E)\GL_n(A_E), the automorphic forms whose constant terms along every proper parabolic subgroup defined over E vanish. Section 1 applies these notions with E CM or totally real. The regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n(A_E) are the π to which r_{l,ι}(π) is attached, and they are the witnesses in Definition 1.3.
items.locator: ACC+ §1.2 (Notation), p. 908; used without definition in §1, pp. 1240–1241
items.note: AG2.0 plans the weight condition: 'Define regular algebraic, conjugate self-dual, essentially conjugate self-dual and polarized cases separately'. The stage decomposition of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII records the same infinitesimal-character condition, taken from Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne, Theorem A. Cuspidality is planned in AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.3, which defines cuspidality by the vanishing of every proper-parabolic constant term. The pinned libraries have no declaration for automorphic representations of GL_n(A_E). Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Local Langlands correspondence for GL_n
items.statement: For a finite extension K of Q_p, rec_K is the local Langlands correspondence of Harris–Taylor. It is a bijection from isomorphism classes of irreducible admissible complex representations π of GL_n(K) to isomorphism classes of n-dimensional Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations rec_K(π) of W_K. Local class field theory is normalized so that Art_K sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius elements (ACC+ §1.2). For n = 1, rec_K(χ) = χ ∘ Art_K^{-1}. Section 1 uses rec in the normalization ι^{-1} rec_{E_v}(π_v ⊗ |det|_v^{(1−n)/2}) that characterizes r_{l,ι}(π). Lemma 4.3 uses it, through Varma's theorem, to show that π_v is a twist of the Steinberg representation because the monodromy operator is a single Jordan block.
items.locator: §1, p. 1240 ('rec_{E_v} denotes the local Langlands correspondance for E_v'); Lemma 4.3 and its proof, p. 1273; convention of ACC+ §1.2, p. 906
items.note: ET.6 says: 'Construct the characteristic-zero local correspondence for GL_m(E), E a finite extension of Q_p, with full Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameters and monodromy, not only semisimplified Weil parameters'. It also covers Steinberg twists and reconstructs the single-Jordan-block monodromy of each segment. The pinned libraries have no local Langlands declaration. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Linearly disjoint restriction preserves the residual image and the lifting hypotheses
items.statement: Let F be a number field, l a prime, r: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_l) continuous with residual representation r̄, and M = F^{ker r̄}(ζ_l). Let F'/F be a finite extension linearly disjoint from M over F. Then G_{F'} surjects onto Gal(M/F), so r̄(G_{F'}) = r̄(G_F) and r̄(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) = r̄(G_{F(ζ_l)}). Consequently: r̄|G_{F'} is absolutely irreducible if r̄ is; r̄(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) is enormous if r̄(G_{F(ζ_l)}) is; and if σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_l)} has r̄(σ) scalar, then some σ' ∈ G_{F'} − G_{F'(ζ_l)} has r̄(σ') = r̄(σ). If r is unramified almost everywhere, so is r|G_{F'}. Suppose r|G_{F_v} is potentially semistable and ordinary of weight λ_v (Definition 1.2). Then for each place w | v of F', r|G_{F'_w} is potentially semistable and ordinary of weight (λ_{v,τ'|F_v})_{τ'}, by the compatibility Art_{F_v} ∘ N_{F'_w/F_v} = (restriction) ∘ Art_{F'_w}. Decomposed genericity is not covered here; it needs ACC+ Lemma 7.1.7.
items.locator: Remark after Definition 1.3, p. 1241; proof of Theorem 1.4, p. 1274 ('all conditions except decomposed genericity follows from the corresponding conditions of r̄')
items.note: PA.5 says: 'Supply a reusable checklist theorem which records that the input package for a chosen lifting argument survives a specified base change'. At finite level, the Galois-theoretic core is Mathlib's IntermediateField.restrictRestrictAlgEquivMapHom_surjective: for K/F normal and finite-dimensional, E/L finite Galois and K ⊓ L = ⊥, restriction Gal(E/L) → Gal(K/F) is surjective. Apply it with E the compositum. The passage from linear disjointness to K ⊓ L = ⊥ is IntermediateField.LinearDisjoint.inf_eq_bot. The pinned libraries have no carrier for Galois representations. Absolute irreducibility is also a conclusion of ACC+ Lemma 7.1.7 (item 089), which in addition gives decomposed genericity. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Soluble Galois extensions with prescribed local completions and avoidance (Clozel–Harris–Taylor, Lemma 4.1.2)
items.statement: Let F be a number field, D/F a finite Galois extension and S a finite set of places of F, archimedean places allowed. For each v ∈ S let E′_v/F_v be a finite Galois extension. Then there is a finite soluble Galois extension E/F, linearly disjoint from D over F, such that for every v ∈ S and every place w of E above v, E_w/F_v is isomorphic to E′_v/F_v. In particular, for F = Q with ∞ ∈ S and E′_∞ = R, the field E is totally real, and E is linearly disjoint over F from every subfield of D.
items.locator: Clozel–Harris–Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois representations, Publ. Math. IHÉS 108 (2008), Lemma 4.1.2, pp. 117–118; used in the proof of Lemma 2.1, pp. 1245–1246 and p. 1248
items.note: The paper applies it twice, both times with F = Q and the trivial extension R/R prescribed at ∞. First, with D = F_0 and local fields E_q ⊃ M_q(ζ_m) of degree divisible by m over M_q(ζ_m), producing L_2. Second, with D the Galois closure of F_0F_2(μ_{2^r}), which need not be Galois over Q, one prime p and E_p of even degree over the composite of the completions of F_2, producing L_1. The proof proceeds in three steps. Induction on the degrees reduces to cyclic E′_v/F_v. These are realized by global class field theory, after extending a finite-order character of ∏_{v∈S} F_v^× to the idèle class group (Clozel–Harris–Taylor, Lemma 4.1.1). Disjointness from D is forced by adding to S, for each Galois subextension of D/F with simple group, a place that does not split completely in it, with trivial prescribed extension. Neither pinned library states it. PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1 plans Moret–Bailly's theorem and the field selection it needs, but does not state this lemma. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: First cohomology of the cyclotomic Galois group with coefficients μ_{p^r}
items.statement: Let K be a number field, p a prime, r ≥ 1 and K′ = K(μ_{p^r}). Then H^1(Gal(K′/K), μ_{p^r}) = 0, except when p = 2, r ≥ 2 and −1 lies in the image of the cyclotomic character Gal(K′/K) → (Z/2^rZ)^×; in that case H^1(Gal(K′/K), μ_{2^r}) ≅ Z/2Z. In particular the group is always killed by 2.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.2, p. 1247, citing Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Cohomology of Number Fields, Proposition 9.1.6; used again in the last step of (2.1), p. 1247
items.note: The group depends only on the image G ⊂ (Z/p^rZ)^× of the cyclotomic character, acting on Z/p^rZ by multiplication. For odd p the vanishing is elementary. If G contains an element of order prime to p, that element acts by a scalar c with c − 1 a unit and kills the cohomology. Otherwise G is generated by some a = 1 + p^s u with u a unit; the norm Σ a^i has p-adic valuation r − s, so its kernel equals (a − 1)(Z/p^rZ). The case p = 2 is where Z/2Z can occur. The fact that the group is killed by 2 is why (2.1) ends in 0, since [F_1 : F_2] is even. Neither pinned library nor any atlas stage provides it; ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2 needs it for Lemma 2.2. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Connecting homomorphisms and the low-degree long exact sequence for discrete modules
items.statement: Let G be a topological group and 0 → A → B → C → 0 a short exact sequence of discrete G-modules. Continuous cohomology then has connecting homomorphisms δ^0: H^0(G, C) → H^1(G, A) and δ^1: H^1(G, C) → H^2(G, A). The sequence 0 → H^0(G, A) → H^0(G, B) → H^0(G, C) → H^1(G, A) → H^1(G, B) → H^1(G, C) → H^2(G, A) → H^2(G, B) is exact, and δ^1 commutes with restriction to subgroups. In particular, a class in H^1(G, C) lifts to H^1(G, B) if and only if δ^1 kills it.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1, pp. 1244–1245 (the long exact sequence of the power-map sequence and the obstruction χ̃ = δ(χ))
items.note: In the pinned Tau Ceti library, DiscreteShortExact records the inclusion, the projection, their equivariance and exactness, for discrete A, B and C. The exactness statements at the nodes involving H^2 assume continuous multiplication on G. explicitDelta1_res gives Res ∘ δ^1 = δ^1 ∘ Res. The character-root obstruction of Lemma 2.1 is this construction applied to 0 → μ_m(k) → k^× → (k^×)^n → 0, with second map x ↦ x^n. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Restriction, inflation and corestriction in low degrees
items.statement: Let G be a topological group and M a discrete G-module. Restriction to a subgroup, and inflation from G/N for a normal subgroup N with coefficients M^N, are defined on continuous H^1 and H^2. In degree 1, inflation is injective and its image is the kernel of restriction to N. If G is profinite, every class in H^2(G, M) is inflated from H^2(G/U, M^U) for some open normal subgroup U. For an open subgroup U of finite index, corestriction H^i(U, M) → H^i(G, M) is defined for i = 1, 2, and Cor ∘ Res is multiplication by the index (G : U).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1, p. 1245 (every element of H^2(G_M, Z/mZ) is inflated from a finite quotient) and pp. 1246–1248 (Res and Cor in the Poitou–Tate compatibility, and 'Recall the relation Cor ∘ Res = [F_1 : F_2]' before (2.1), p. 1247); proof of Lemma 2.2, p. 1247 (the inflation–restriction columns of the diagram)
items.note: In the pinned Tau Ceti library, corestriction assumes U open of finite index. Degree one needs continuous multiplication and inversion on G, and degree two a topological group. Inflation needs a continuous action of G/N on M^N, which is automatic for discrete M. exists_explicitInfl2_eq assumes G compact and totally disconnected and M discrete. All of these hold for Galois groups of number fields and local fields with finite discrete coefficients. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Finite subgroups of PGL_2(F̄_l) containing PSL_2(F_l) (Dickson)
items.statement: Let l ≥ 5 be a prime and G a finite subgroup of PGL_2(F̄_l) containing the image of SL_2(F_l). Then G is conjugate in PGL_2(F̄_l) to PSL_2(k) or PGL_2(k) for some finite extension k/F_l.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.6(2), p. 1251, citing Darmon–Diamond–Taylor, Theorem 2.47(b)
items.note: R01.4 says: 'Prove the finite-subgroup facts of GL₂/PGL₂ used in the source arguments, including dihedral and exceptional images, normal subgroups'. For l ≥ 5, PSL_2(F_l) is simple and not solvable, so the Borel, dihedral, A_4 and S_4 cases of Dickson's classification are excluded. For l = 5, an A_5 containing PSL_2(F_5) is PSL_2(F_5) itself. The paper applies the theorem to ad r̄(G_F) with l > 2n + 5. ACC+ Lemmas 7.1.4 and 7.1.6 rest on the same input. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Decomposed genericity of Sym^m r̄ when the adjoint image over the Galois closure is large (ACC+ Lemma 7.1.6(3))
items.statement: Let F/Q be finite with normal closure F̃, m a positive integer, l > 2m + 3 a prime, and r̄: G_F → GL_2(F̄_l) continuous with r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊃ SL_2(F_l). Let F′/F be a finite extension linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄} over F, with normal closure F̃′ over Q. If ad r̄(G_{F̃′}) ⊃ PSL_2(F_l), then Sym^m r̄|_{G_{F′}} is decomposed generic.
items.locator: Allen–Calegari–Caraiani–Gee–Helm–Le Hung–Newton–Scholze–Taylor–Thorne, Potential automorphy over CM fields, Ann. of Math. 197 (2023), Lemma 7.1.6(3), pp. 1090–1091; used in the proof of Lemma 2.6(2), p. 1251
items.note: The paper applies it with F′ = F_1 and m = n − 1, after reducing to F Galois over Q with ad r̄(G_F) = PSL_2(k). In the case H ∩ F̃′_s = F the hypothesis holds, because then ad r̄(G_{F̃_1}) = PSL_2(k). The ACC+ proof uses Dickson's theorem, Goursat's lemma, the automorphism group of PSL_2(k)^n and the Chebotarev density theorem. No atlas stage plans it: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 plans the enormity definition and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.7 the genericity definitions, not this criterion. It belongs with the decomposed-genericity lemmas of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5, downstream of AG2.7. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Composita of Galois extensions with a common simple group
items.statement: Let k be a field, Δ a finite simple group, and K_1, …, K_s finite Galois extensions of k inside a common field, each equal to k or with Galois group isomorphic to Δ. Then there is a subset J ⊂ {1, …, s} such that the compositum K = K_1⋯K_s is the compositum of the K_j with j ∈ J, and restriction identifies Gal(K/k) with ∏_{j∈J} Gal(K_j/k) ≅ Δ^{|J|}. In particular, for disjoint subsets I, I′ of J, the composita of the K_j over j ∈ I and over j ∈ I′ are linearly disjoint over k.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.6(2), pp. 1251–1252 (the claims 'Gal(Ẽ/E) = (Z/2Z)^r' and 'Gal(F̃′_i/F̃′_{i−1}) … is of form Δ_i^m', both attributed to Goursat's lemma)
items.note: Proof: adjoin the K_j one at a time. Each K_j meets the compositum so far in a Galois extension of k whose group is a quotient of Δ, hence in k or in K_j; in the first case the Galois group of the new compositum is the product. The paper applies it twice. The first use is to the conjugates σE, with Δ = Z/2Z over F. The second is to the fields σ_jF′_iF̃′_{i−1} over F̃′_{i−1}, each Galois over F̃′_{i−1} with group Δ_i or trivial. The pinned Goursat lemma concerns subgroups of a product of two groups and does not give this. Neither pinned library nor any atlas stage description states it. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Levelt's rigidity theorem for hypergeometric monodromy
items.statement: Let α_1, …, α_n, β_1, …, β_n ∈ C^× with α_j ≠ β_k for all j, k. Write ∏_j (X − α_j) = X^n + A_1X^{n−1} + ⋯ + A_n and ∏_j (X − β_j) = X^n + B_1X^{n−1} + ⋯ + B_n. Let A and B be the companion matrices with ones on the subdiagonal and last columns (−A_n, …, −A_1)^T and (−B_n, …, −B_1)^T. Suppose h_0, h_∞ ∈ GL_n(C) satisfy three conditions: h_∞ has characteristic polynomial ∏_j (X − α_j); h_0^{−1} has characteristic polynomial ∏_j (X − β_j); and h_1 = h_0^{−1}h_∞^{−1} is a pseudo-reflection, i.e. h_1 − 1 has rank one. Then some g ∈ GL_n(C) satisfies gh_∞g^{−1} = A and gh_0g^{−1} = B^{−1}, so that gh_1g^{−1} = BA^{−1}. Conversely, (h_0, h_∞) = (B^{−1}, A) satisfies these conditions. The relation is written in the order h_0h_1h_∞ = 1 of Lemma 3.4. The pseudo-reflection condition does not depend on the order, since h_0^{−1}h_∞^{−1} and h_∞^{−1}h_0^{−1} are conjugate. Lemma 3.4 applies this with α_j = 1 and β_j = ζ_N^{−b_j}.
items.locator: Beukers–Heckman, Monodromy for the hypergeometric function nF_{n−1}, Invent. Math. 95 (1989), Theorem 3.5 (Levelt); invoked in the proof of Lemma 3.4, p. 1259
items.note: Stated in the form Lemma 3.4 uses, with the relation written as h_0h_1h_∞ = 1. Beukers–Heckman's own normalisation of h_0, h_1, h_∞ should be matched to it when their paper is read (open gate S2). The proof is linear algebra. X = h_∞ and Y = h_0^{−1} differ by a matrix of rank one, so W = ker(X − Y) is a hyperplane, and some nonzero e satisfies X^je ∈ W for 0 ≤ j ≤ n − 2. If the X-cyclic span of e were proper, it would be invariant under X and Y, X and Y would agree on it, and they would have a common eigenvalue. So e, Xe, …, X^{n−1}e is a basis, and in it X and Y are the companion matrices A and B. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has n × n companion matrices or hypergeometric groups (Tau Ceti has only the 2 × 2 companion element TauCeti.companionGL), and no atlas stage plans this theorem. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Picard–Lefschetz description of the Dwork monodromy at t = 1
items.statement: Let T be a generator of the local monodromy of the local system R^{N−2}π̃_*Z on T_0(C) around the puncture t = 1, acting on H^{N−2}(Y_t(C), Z) for t ∈ T_0(C) close to 1. The fibre Y_1 is singular exactly at the N^{N−2} points of the H_0-orbit of (1 : ⋯ : 1), on which H_0 acts freely, and these are ordinary double points. By Picard–Lefschetz theory there is a set Δ ⊂ H^{N−2}(Y_t(C), Z) of vanishing cycles, one for each singular point of Y_1 and permuted by H_0 up to sign, with two properties. First, the sequence 0 → H^{N−2}(Y_1(C), Z) → H^{N−2}(Y_t(C), Z) → Z^Δ, x ↦ (⟨x, δ⟩)_{δ∈Δ}, is exact. Second, T(x) = x + ε ∑_{δ∈Δ} ⟨x, δ⟩δ for all x, where ⟨ , ⟩ is the cup-product pairing and ε ∈ {±1} depends only on N. Consequently: (i) since N − 2 is odd, ⟨ , ⟩ is alternating and vanishing cycles at distinct singular points are orthogonal, so ⟨δ, δ'⟩ = 0 for all δ, δ' ∈ Δ and (T − 1)^2 = 0; (ii) fixing δ_0 ∈ Δ, every x in the χ-eigenpart of H^{N−2}(Y_t(C), Z[ζ_N]) satisfies T(x) − x = ε⟨x, δ_0⟩ ∑_{ξ∈H_0} χ(ξ)^{−1}ξδ_0. Hence on the χ-eigenpart T is unipotent and ker(T − 1) has rank at least n − 1. For n > 2 the map t ↦ t^N is étale near t = 1, so ρ_{t'}(γ_1) is conjugate to the restriction of T to V_{B,t}.
items.locator: BLGHT, proof of Lemma 4.3(2) (citing SGA 7); invoked in the proof of Lemma 3.3(3), p. 1258
items.note: LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.2 plans the ℓ-adic Picard–Lefschetz formula for a single ordinary quadratic singularity ('ρ(σ)x = x + ε_n t_ℓ(σ)⟨x, δ⟩δ'), and a formalisation should import it. The use here also needs the topological version over C, several ordinary double points in one fibre forming a free H_0-orbit, and the restriction to an H_0-eigenpart; these are not planned. The singular points were found by solving X_i^N = ∏_j X_j for all i, and the Hessian at (1 : ⋯ : 1) is N(N·I − J), which is nondegenerate. BLGHT write H^{n−1} where the middle degree N − 2 is meant. BLGHT's last step, from the symplectic pairing to the characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n, does not apply to the χ-eigenpart, which is not self-dual; conclusion (i) replaces it. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Normal subgroups of SL_n over a finite field; simplicity of PSL_n
items.statement: Let k be a finite field with q elements and n ≥ 2, with (n, q) ≠ (2, 2), (2, 3). Then SL_n(k) is perfect, and its centre is the group μ_n(k) of scalar matrices. The quotient PSL_n(k) = SL_n(k)/μ_n(k) is a non-abelian simple group, and every proper normal subgroup of SL_n(k) is central. Consequently SL_n(k) has no nontrivial abelian quotient, every nontrivial quotient of SL_n(k) has PSL_n(k) as a composition factor, and the cyclic composition factors of SL_n(k) have prime order dividing gcd(n, q − 1).
items.locator: Used without citation in the last paragraph of the proof of Lemma 3.7, p. 1260, and in the proof of Proposition 3.8, p. 1261 (classical; Jordan and Dickson)
items.note: Pinned Mathlib has Iwasawa's criterion (MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup). It has the rank-two case: Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.rank_two_simple (PSL_2(F) is simple for a field with at least four elements) and Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top. It also has the centre of SL_n (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.center_equiv_rootsOfUnity). Simplicity of PSL_n for n ≥ 3 and the description of the normal subgroups of SL_n are absent from both pinned libraries, and no atlas stage plans them. The theorem is therefore placed with the Dwork family, whose Lemma 3.7 and Proposition 3.8 use it. In those uses the excluded cases never arise: Lemma 3.7 has n > 2, and Proposition 3.8 applies the theorem over a field of characteristic l1 > 10. Lemma 5.2.3 of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne (The Ramanujan and Sato–Tate conjectures for Bianchi modular forms) is a longer statement that also covers PSU_n. It is marked missing in that paper's blueprint as well, and the two should be planned once. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Non-isomorphism of PSL_n in different characteristics (Artin)
items.statement: Let n ≥ 2, let l1 ≠ l2 be odd primes with l1 > 10, and let r, s ≥ 1. Then PSL_n(F_{l1^r}) is not isomorphic to PSL_n(F_{l2^s}). Consequently PSL_n(F_{l1^r}) is not a composition factor of SL_n(F_{l2^s}).
items.locator: Proposition 3.8, proof, p. 1261, citing Artin [2] (The orders of the classical simple groups, 1955), Theorem 2
items.note: Qian deduces this from Artin's comparison of the orders of the classical simple groups (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 8 (1955)). The exact statement of Artin's Theorem 2 has not been checked. The well-known coincidence PSL_2(F_4) ≅ PSL_2(F_5) involves characteristic 2 and lies outside this range. The 'consequently' clause uses the theorem on normal subgroups of SL_n: the composition factors of SL_n(F_{l2^s}) are PSL_n(F_{l2^s}) and cyclic groups, and only cyclic groups when (n, l2^s) = (2, 3). Neither pinned library has the statement and no atlas stage plans it, so it is placed with the Dwork family, whose Proposition 3.8 uses it. Lemma 5.2.3 of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne states a longer list of non-isomorphisms that includes this case. It is marked missing there too, and the two should be planned once. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Finite special unitary group SU(n,k)
items.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic l with [k : F_l] even, and let σ be the unique element of order 2 of Gal(k/F_l). Then SU(n,k) = {g ∈ SL_n(k) : σ(g)ᵗg = 1_n}, where σ(g) means σ applied to the entries of g.
items.locator: Lemma 3.7, proof, displayed definition, p. 1260
items.note: Matrix.specialUnitaryGroup n α consists of the matrices A with star A * A = 1, A * star A = 1 and det A = 1, where star A is the conjugate transpose for a StarRing structure on α. By Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff', membership in the unitary group is star A * A = 1, so taking α = k with star = σ recovers SU(n,k). Mathlib has no such star-ring instance on k, so it must be supplied as a small wrapper. This is easy because k is commutative and σ is an involution. The docstring's proviso that 2 be invertible holds in odd characteristic. The other two families in the classification are Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup and Matrix.symplecticGroup. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: p-adic de Rham comparison for smooth proper varieties
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_l and X a smooth proper variety over K. For every i, the G_K-representation H^i_et(X_{K̄}, Q_l) is de Rham. There is a natural isomorphism of filtered K-vector spaces (H^i_et(X_{K̄}, Q_l) ⊗_{Q_l} B_dR)^{G_K} ≅ H^i_dR(X/K), functorial in X. In particular it is compatible with a finite group of automorphisms of X and with its eigenspace projectors after extending coefficients.
items.locator: §3, étale comparison displayed before Lemma 3.10, p. 1265; used in Lemma 3.11(1), p. 1267
items.note: CP.3 plans this: 'When X descends to a proper smooth X_0/K, compare that deformation with H_dR(X_0/K) tensor_K B_dR^+' and 'the comparison after B_dR-inversion with p-adic étale cohomology', with filtration strictness. Qian applies it with coefficients Z[ζ_N]_λ and an embedding σ of F_v, which is a formal consequence. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Crystalline comparison for smooth proper schemes over a p-adic ring of integers
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_l with ring of integers O_K, residue field k and maximal unramified subfield K_0 = W(k)[1/l]. Let X be a smooth proper scheme over O_K. Then H^i_et(X_{K̄}, Q_l) is crystalline, and D_cris(H^i_et(X_{K̄}, Q_l)) ≅ H^i_cris(X_k/W(k))[1/l] as φ-modules over K_0. The isomorphism is compatible with the de Rham comparison after ⊗_{K_0}K and functorial in X. In particular, two such schemes with the same special fibre have isomorphic D_cris as φ-modules, compatibly with automorphisms acting on both.
items.locator: Lemma 3.11(2) and (3) and their proofs, pp. 1266–1267
items.note: CP.2 plans 'RΓ_et(X_C,Q_p) tensor B_cris ≃ RΓ_crys(X_k/W(k))[1/p] tensor_(W(k)[1/p]) B_cris' for a smooth proper formal O_K-model, together with 'G_K/Frobenius compatibility' and the identification of D_cris with crystalline cohomology. Qian applies it to Y_t over O_{F_v} when t ∈ O_{F_v} and t^N − 1 is a unit, and, for t ∈ m_{F_v}, to Y_t and Y_0, which have the same special fibre. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Local freeness of the relative Hodge filtration in characteristic zero
items.statement: Let S be a smooth connected scheme over a field K of characteristic zero and f: X → S a smooth projective morphism. Then H^i_dR(X/S) is locally free of finite rank, and its Hodge filtration F^j is by local direct summands. Each graded piece gr^j ≅ R^{i−j}f_*Ω^j_{X/S} is locally free. All of these commute with arbitrary base change, so the Hodge numbers of the fibres are constant. The same holds for the direct summand cut out by an idempotent e ∈ K[G], where G is a finite group acting on X over S.
items.locator: §3, before Lemma 3.10, p. 1264 (H_dR is locally free with Hodge filtration by local direct summands), and proof of Lemma 3.10(2), p. 1266 ('Since gr^j V_{dR,σ} is locally free')
items.note: This is Deligne's theorem (Théorème de Lefschetz et critères de dégénérescence de suites spectrales, 1968): the relative Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence degenerates in characteristic zero, and its terms commute with base change. In Qian's application S = T0 × Q(ζ_N), K = Q(ζ_N), and e is the idempotent of the H0-character χ. No atlas stage plans the relative statement. CohomologyComparisons:CP.3 plans degeneration for a single proper smooth variety over a p-adic field. ComplexComparisonPartII:C5 plans the algebraic de Rham–Betti comparison and 'relative Gauss–Manin compatibility for proper smooth families', but not local freeness of the Hodge pieces. The item is placed at C5. That stage must add the degeneration for smooth projective complex varieties (from Hodge theory, through GAGA). It must also add the semicontinuity and base-change argument that turns constant Hodge numbers into local freeness. The pinned libraries do not have it. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Chebotarev density theorem
items.statement: Let L/K be a finite Galois extension of number fields with group G. For every conjugacy class C of G, the finite places v of K unramified in L with Frob_v ∈ C form a set of Dirichlet density #C/#G. In particular every element of G is Frob_v for infinitely many v, and these v can be chosen outside any prescribed finite set of places (for instance, of odd residue characteristic prime to Nl).
items.locator: Implicit in the last step of the proof of Lemma 3.9, p. 1264, where the image of the determinant character is read off from its values at Frobenius elements
items.note: That Tau Ceti layer plans 'the named theorem hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet with value #C/#G over every number field K' and to 'derive ... infinitude of every Frobenius class'. The pinned Tau Ceti tree has Frobenius prime sets but not the density theorem. The target (F_{l²}^× k(λ)^×)^n in Lemma 3.9 is a subgroup, so the weaker statement that Frobenius elements outside a finite set generate the Galois group would suffice there. The theorem is also invoked in the proofs recorded in items 021, 077 and 083. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Weil–Deligne representation attached to an l′-adic representation (l′ ≠ p)
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p, let l′ ≠ p be a prime, and let r: G_K → GL_n(Q̄_{l′}) be continuous. By Grothendieck's monodromy theorem there are an open subgroup I′ of the inertia group I_K and a unique nilpotent N ∈ M_n(Q̄_{l′}) such that r(σ) = exp(t_{l′}(σ)N) for all σ ∈ I′. Here t_{l′}: I_K → Z_{l′} is the l′-adic tame character, defined after choosing a compatible system of l′-power roots of unity. Fix a Frobenius lift φ ∈ G_K and set r_1(φ^m σ) = r(φ^m σ)·exp(−t_{l′}(σ)N) for σ ∈ I_K and m ∈ Z. This defines a representation r_1 of the Weil group W_K that is trivial on an open subgroup of I_K. The pair WD(r) = (r_1, N) is the Weil–Deligne representation attached to r. Up to isomorphism it does not depend on the choice of φ or of t_{l′}.
items.locator: Lemma 3.12, p. 1267 (WD(V_{λ′,t}) = (r_1, N)), and its proof, pp. 1267–1268
items.note: R01.2 plans: 'For ℓ different from the residue characteristic, prove quasi-unipotence and construct the monodromy operator and Weil–Deligne representation, including independence of the tame character.' LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.1 supplies the geometric form exp(t_ℓ(σ)N) = ρ(σ) used in the proof of Lemma 3.12. Item 084 orders Weil–Deligne types, but no item defines WD(r) itself. Lemma 3.12 (item 071) and the first step of the proof of Lemma 4.3 (item 086) are statements about this object. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Ordinarity of a polarizable automorphic representation with ordinary Galois representation (Geraghty, Lemma 5.9)
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field, l a prime, ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, and π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) such that r = r_{l,ι}(π) is polarizable. If r|_{G_{F_v}} is ordinary (Definition 1.2) at every place v | l of F, then π is ι-ordinary at every v | l, so r is ι-ordinarily automorphic. This is the form in which Qian uses the lemma, with F = F′, l = l′ and r = Sym^{n−1} r_{E_0,l′}|_{G_{F′}}. Geraghty states it for polarized (essentially conjugate self-dual) automorphic representations, and its precise hypotheses are those of his Lemma 5.9.
items.locator: Geraghty, Modularity lifting theorems for ordinary Galois representations, Math. Ann. 373 (2019), Lemma 5.9 (reference [8]); applied in the proof of Theorem 1.1, p. 1273, to Sym^{n−1} r_{E_0,l′}|G_{F′}; its polarizability hypothesis is the point of Remark 4.4, p. 1274
items.note: Geraghty's paper is not among the sources read, so the exact hypotheses must be taken from his Lemma 5.9 before use. No atlas stage plans it. This direction of local–global compatibility, from Galois ordinarity to ι-ordinarity, is available only for polarizable representations, as Remark 4.4 (p. 1274) explains; the non-polarized theory of ACC+ does not supply it. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: ι-ordinary automorphic representation (Geraghty, Definition 5.3)
items.statement: Let F be a CM or totally real field, π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) of weight λ, ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, and v | l a place of F with uniformizer ϖ_v. For integers c ≥ b ≥ 0, let Iw_v(b,c) ⊂ GL_n(O_{F_v}) be the subgroup of matrices that are upper triangular modulo ϖ_v^c and unipotent upper triangular modulo ϖ_v^b. π is ι-ordinary at v if, for some integers c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1, the Iw_v(b,c)-invariants of ι^{−1}π_v contain a nonzero vector with the following property: for each j = 1, …, n, it is an eigenvector of the weight-normalized Hecke operator U^{(j)}_{λ,ϖ_v} attached to α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v} = diag(ϖ_v, …, ϖ_v, 1, …, 1) (with j entries ϖ_v), with an l-adic unit eigenvalue. π is ι-ordinary if this holds at every v | l.
items.locator: Geraghty, Math. Ann. 373 (2019), Definition 5.3 (reference [8]); cited in Definition 1.3, p. 1241; used in Lemma 4.3, p. 1273, and in ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2(5) (p. 1030) and Corollary 5.5.2 (p. 1028); the groups Iw_v(b,c) as recalled in ACC+, p. 922
items.note: The normalizing factor of U^{(j)}_{λ,ϖ_v} must be copied from Geraghty, which is not among the sources read; ACC+ recall the groups Iw_v(b,c) (p. 922) and use the definition without restating it. No atlas stage names ι-ordinary automorphic representations. PA.2 plans the normalized positive Hecke operators and ordinary parts in which the definition is phrased. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Ordinarity criterion for a twisted Steinberg component (Geraghty, Lemmas 5.2 and 5.6, as used in Lemma 4.3)
items.statement: Let F be a CM field, l a prime, ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, and v | l a place of F with uniformizer ϖ_v. Let π be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) whose weight, in Geraghty's notation, satisfies λ_{τ,i} = −λ_τ for all i = 1, …, n and all τ: F_v → Q̄_l. Suppose π_v ≅ Sp_n(ψ_v|·|_v^{(1−n)/2}) with ψ_v an unramified character of F_v^×. Suppose also that val_l(ι^{−1}ψ_v(det α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v})) = val_l(∏_{τ: F_v → Q̄_l} τ(ϖ_v)^{−jλ_τ}) for every j ∈ [0, n], where α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v} = diag(ϖ_v, …, ϖ_v, 1, …, 1) with j entries ϖ_v. Then π is ι-ordinary at v. Since det α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v} = ϖ_v^j, the condition for j = n implies it for every j. Geraghty's Lemma 5.6 shows that an unramified twist of the Steinberg representation is ι-ordinary in weight 0. Qian removes the weight hypothesis by checking this valuation condition, which comes from Geraghty's Lemma 5.2. In the proof of Lemma 4.3 it is applied with F = F′.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 4.3, second paragraph, p. 1273, citing Lemmas 5.2 and 5.6 of Geraghty [8]
items.note: This is recorded in the form stated in the proof of Lemma 4.3. Geraghty's Lemmas 5.2 and 5.6 are not among the sources read and must be checked, including whether ψ_v must be unramified; in Qian's application ψ_v is unramified by the Steinberg step. No atlas stage names the criterion. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Base change of automorphy to the CM quadratic extension
items.statement: Let K be a CM field with maximal totally real subfield K^+, l a prime, ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, and π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_{K^+}) such that r_{l,ι}(π)|_{G_K} is irreducible. Then the Arthur–Clozel base change π_K of π to K is a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_K), and r_{l,ι}(π_K) ≅ r_{l,ι}(π)|_{G_K}. In particular r_{l,ι}(π)|_{G_K} is automorphic. π_K is cuspidal because π ≇ π ⊗ η_{K/K^+}: otherwise r_{l,ι}(π) ≅ r_{l,ι}(π) ⊗ η_{K/K^+}, and then r_{l,ι}(π)|_{G_K} would have a non-scalar endomorphism and so would be reducible.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.1, p. 1272 ('Symm^{n−1} r_{E,l′}|G_{(F′)^+} and hence Symm^{n−1} r_{E,l′}|G_{F′} is automorphic'), used without citation; Arthur–Clozel, Simple algebras, base change, and the advanced theory of the trace formula (1989)
items.note: ET.7a plans the 'cyclic automorphic-induction/base-change steps from the Arthur–Clozel and Moeglin–Waldspurger proofs, with central characters and cuspidality hypotheses'. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.5 also registers cyclic base change. But ML.5 requires ML.3 and hence ML.2, and the statement is used in ML.2 (proof of Theorem 1.1), so ML.5 cannot supply it. In Qian's application r_{l′,ι′}(π)|_{G_{F′}} is irreducible, because the residual image contains Sym^{n−1} of SL_2(F_{l′}) and l′ > n. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Serre's open image theorem for non-CM elliptic curves
items.statement: Let K be a number field and E/K an elliptic curve without complex multiplication over K̄. Then for all but finitely many primes l, the mod-l representation r̄_{E,l}: G_K → GL_2(F_l) is surjective. Qian applies this with K = F̃, the normal closure of F over Q, and E = E_0 ⊗ F̃.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.1, p. 1269, citing Serre, Propriétés galoisiennes des points d'ordre fini des courbes elliptiques, Invent. Math. 15 (1972) (reference [16])
items.note: No atlas stage plans it. The Faltings finiteness roadmap says explicitly that it avoids needing the full Serre open image theorem. It is used to choose l′ with r̄_{E_0,l′}(G_{F̃}) = GL_2(F_{l′}); this surjectivity yields the scalar element, the enormous image and the decomposed genericity that ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 needs at l′. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Supersingular primes of a non-CM elliptic curve over Q have density zero (Serre)
items.statement: Let E/Q be an elliptic curve without complex multiplication. Then the set of primes p at which E has good supersingular reduction has density 0.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.1, p. 1269, citing Serre, Quelques applications du théorème de densité de Chebotarev, Publ. Math. IHÉS 54 (1981), Theorem 20 (reference [15]); also used in the proof of ACC+ Corollary 7.2.4, p. 1100
items.note: No atlas stage plans it. It ensures that the primes l′ ≡ 1 mod Nn at which E_0 has good ordinary reduction still have positive density. Ordinarity of E_0 at l′ is what makes Sym^{n−1} r_{E_0,l′} ordinary at l′, as the proof of Theorem 1.1 requires. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Regular ordinarity of Dwork motives near infinity (companion main theorem)
items.statement: Let F be a finite extension of Q_p containing ζ_N, with p odd and p ∤ N. Let T_0 = P^1 − ({∞} ∪ μ_N) over Z[1/N], let π: Z → T_0 be the family X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N = N t X_1⋯X_N, and let H_0 = {(ξ_i) ∈ μ_N^N : ∏ ξ_i = 1}/μ_N act by X_i ↦ ξ_i X_i. Let χ(ξ) = ∏ ξ_i^{a_i} with Σ a_i ≡ 0 mod N. For a prime λ of Z[1/2N, ζ_N] above p put V_λ = (R^{N−2}π_* Z[ζ_N]_λ)^{χ,H_0}, locally free of some rank n. Let V_B be the corresponding Betti local system on T_0(C) (via τ(ζ_N) = e^{2πi/N}), with monodromy representation ρ_s and loop γ_∞ around ∞. Assume that, for every σ ∈ Gal(Q(μ_N)/Q), ρ_s(γ_∞) has minimal polynomial (X − 1)^n on the local system attached to σχ; by Remark 1.2 this holds when 0 ∈ {a_1, …, a_N}. Then, for every finite extension F_0/F and every t ∈ F_0 with v(t) > 0, the G_{F_0}-representation V_{λ,t^{-1}} is ordinary of some regular weight in the sense of Definition 1.2 (item 002). The companion's proof (§4) applies its Lemma 4.2, which omits the Hodge–Tate hypothesis of BLGHT Lemma 2.2(2) (E11). A complete proof must also show that at every embedding the labelled Hodge–Tate weights of V_{λ,t^{-1}} are n consecutive integers, each of multiplicity one, and the companion does not do this. For the character fixed in the published §3 this input is Lemma 3.11(1) (item 068), and item 105 records that case.
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.2, p. 2, proved in §4, pp. 19–23; cited as 'the main result of [14]' on p. 1241 and in Remarks 3.13 and 4.4, pp. 1268 and 1274
items.note: The printed proof (§4, pp. 19–23) combines items 092, 094, 098, 100 and 101, the Dwork case of the semistable comparison, and item 104 with the companion's Lemma 4.2, which is false as stated (E11). BLGHT Lemma 2.2(2) needs consecutive labelled Hodge–Tate weights, and the companion does not establish them for a general χ. A possible repair, not in the source and still to be checked: maximal unipotence at ∞ forces n distinct consecutive Hodge numbers on each eigen-variation, via the limiting mixed Hodge structure (N^{n−1} ≠ 0 and N of type (−1, −1)). The de Rham comparison would then give consecutive labelled Hodge–Tate weights, and the twisted form of item 103 would apply. The hypothesis for every σ follows from the case σ = 1, because the automorphism σ of the coefficients Z[ζ_N] carries the χ-eigenpart of R^{N−2}π_*Z[ζ_N] onto the σχ-eigenpart compatibly with monodromy. The item is routed to the Dwork switching-motives Part II next to item 105 and carries gates S7 and S8. The published proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 do not use it (Remark 3.13, p. 1268). items.name: Toroidal embeddings over a discrete valuation ring and subdivision blowups
items.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π and generic point η; in the application R = W(k) and π = p. A torus embedding over R is an irreducible normal R-scheme of finite type containing a split torus T_η as a dense open subscheme, with a T-action extending translation. The affine torus embeddings are X_σ = Spec R[π^k 𝔛^α : (k,α) ∈ Z × M(T), ⟨(k,α), v⟩ ≥ 0 for all v ∈ σ], for rational polyhedral cones σ ⊂ ℝ_{≥0} × N_ℝ(T) containing no line of N_ℝ(T). A toroidal embedding is a pair U ⊂ X, with X irreducible, normal and of finite type over R and U ⊂ X_η open, which Zariski locally admits étale maps of pairs to torus embeddings. Its boundary X − U is a union of normal irreducible divisors E_i without self-intersection. The strata are the connected components of ∩_{i∈J} E_i − ∪_{i∉J} E_i. To a stratum Y one attaches the lattice of Cartier divisors on Star(Y) supported on Star(Y) − U, and the cone dual to its effective elements; these cones glue to a conical complex with integral structure. Every finite rational subdivision of this complex determines a toroidal embedding U ⊂ X' with the subdivided complex, together with a proper map X' → X that is the identity on U; X' is unique up to unique isomorphism over X. When the subdivision is cut out by a convex piecewise-linear order function, X' → X is the normalised blowup of a coherent ideal sheaf that is locally a sum of sheaves O_X(−D), for boundary Cartier divisors D determined by that function. The companion cites part (e) on p. 198 of Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat when it calls this map a blowup. A finite group that acts on X, preserves U and fixes every boundary Cartier divisor acts trivially on the complex, and therefore acts compatibly on X'.
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, proof of Theorem 2.3, pp. 9–12, recalling Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat, Toroidal embeddings I (Lecture Notes in Math. 339), chapter 'Further applications', pp. 191–198 (parts (d) and (e) on pp. 197–198), and chapter 'Semi-stable reduction', p. 59, for the case over a field
items.note: Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat was not available at source level; the page references are those of the companion. Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.4 together with the equivariant toroidal semistable reduction theorem, which uses it. Searched: the pinned libraries have no declarations for toroidal embeddings or log structures. The atlas plans toric varieties over a field, with cones, fans and subdivisions (Tau Ceti Analytic toric geometry, Layer 0), and toroidal compactifications of Shimura varieties (ShimuraCompactifications C0–C3), but nothing over a discrete valuation ring. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Unimodular subdivision after scaling (Knudsen–Mumford)
items.statement: Let P be a compact rational polyhedral complex with integral structure. Then there are an integer e ≥ 1 and a projective subdivision of eP into lattice polytopes σ_α whose volume, measured by the integral structure, is 1/(d_α)!, where d_α = dim σ_α; equivalently, each σ_α is a unimodular lattice simplex. Here 'projective' means that the subdivision is induced by a continuous piecewise-linear function that is convex on each polytope of eP and whose maximal domains of linearity are the σ_α. Now let Δ be a conical complex with integral structure and l an integral linear function on Δ that is positive on Δ − {0}, and suppose {σ_α} is a subdivision of the compact slice {l = 1} into unimodular lattice simplices. Then the vertices of each σ_α form a basis of the lattice in the linear span of the cone over σ_α, and extend to a basis of the lattice of any cone of Δ containing it. So the cones over the σ_α are regular and form a subdivision of Δ.
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, proof of Theorem 2.3, pp. 11–12, citing Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat, Toroidal embeddings I (Lecture Notes in Math. 339), chapter 'Semi-stable reduction', pp. 95 and 105–108 (Lemma 4 on p. 96), and Knudsen, Construction of nice polyhedral subdivisions, same volume, pp. 109–164
items.note: Not read at source level, because Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat was not available. The projectivity clause is the form needed to present the resulting modification as a blowup in the equivariant toroidal semistable reduction theorem; it must be checked against the source. In the companion's application (pp. 11–12), P is the slice R = 1 of the conical complex of 𝕏_d, the model of item 091 base changed along T ↦ R^d. The further base change R ↦ S^e gives 𝕏_{de}, whose slice S = 1 is eP. The regular cones over the σ_α give the charts W[S, U^{±1}, T_1, …, T_{d_α+1}, T_{d_α+2}^{±1}, …]/(SU − T_1⋯T_{d_α+1}) of item 092. Searched: no library declarations on unimodular triangulations of lattice polytopes. Tau Ceti Analytic toric geometry, Layer 0, plans regular cones, finite fans and subdivisions, which this item should reuse. No atlas stage plans the toroidal semistable-reduction theorem; SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.4 plans 'semistable reduction and alterations' in general. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Equivariant toroidal semistable reduction over a discrete valuation ring
items.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π and fraction field K (in the application R = W(k) and π = p). Let U ⊂ X be a toroidal embedding over R in the sense of the item on toroidal embeddings over a discrete valuation ring, with conical complex Δ̃. Assume that the special fibre is a boundary divisor and that every cone of Δ̃ has the form ℝ_{≥0} × σ', with the first factor dual to the Cartier divisor (π). Then Δ̃ = ℝ_{≥0} ⊕ Δ, where Δ is the conical complex of the toroidal embedding U ⊂ X_K over K. Let f ∈ Γ(X, O_X) be invertible on U and vanish on every irreducible component of X_K − U. Then f defines an integral linear function l_f on Δ, positive on Δ − {0}, and Δ* = {l_f = 1} is a compact rational polyhedral complex with integral structure. For e ≥ 1, let X_e be the normalisation of X ×_{Spec Z[f]} Spec Z[s], where f ↦ s^e, and let U_e be the preimage of U. Then U_e ⊂ X_e is a toroidal embedding of the same kind, and the slice {l_s = 1} of its complex is eΔ*, with the integral structure of Δ*. Then there are e ≥ 1 and a projective subdivision {σ_α} of eΔ* into unimodular lattice simplices, and the toroidal modification Z → X_e attached to the subdivision {ℝ_{≥0} × Cone(σ_α)} of the complex of X_e has the following properties. (a) Z → X_e is proper and is an isomorphism over U_e. (b) Z → X_e is the normalisation of the blowup of X_e along a coherent ideal sheaf that is locally a sum of sheaves O(−D), for Cartier divisors D supported on X_e − U_e. (c) Z is smooth over R, and étale locally on Z there is a smooth morphism Z → Spec R[s][T_1, …, T_m]/(s − T_1⋯T_m) over R[s]. Hence, for every discrete valuation ring R' and every ring map R[s] → R' sending s to a uniformiser, Z ⊗_{R[s]} R' has semistable reduction over R': étale locally it is smooth over R'[T_1, …, T_m]/(T_1⋯T_m − s). (d) Suppose a finite group H acts on X by R-automorphisms that preserve U and f and map every boundary Cartier divisor to itself. Then H acts on X_e, trivially on s, and on Z, and Z → X_e is H-equivariant.
items.locator: Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat, Toroidal embeddings I (Lecture Notes in Math. 339, 1973): 'Semi-stable reduction', pp. 53–108 (the case over a field, pp. 95–108); Knudsen, 'Construction of nice polyhedral subdivisions', pp. 109–164; and 'Further applications', pp. 165–209 (parts (d) and (e), pp. 197–198); in the form used in arXiv:2103.00106v1, proof of Theorem 2.3, pp. 9–12
items.note: Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.4, whose description covers it: 'semistable reduction and alterations' and 'a model records its base, generic fiber and allowable base extension'. It is the general theorem behind item 092, which applies it to 𝕏_d over W with f = R and H = H_0; Remark 2.2 shows that H_0 fixes every boundary Cartier divisor. Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat was not available at source level. The statement follows the form used in arXiv:2103.00106v1, pp. 9–12, including the product condition on cones that the companion imposes ('σ has the form ℝ_{≥0} × σ'', p. 9). The companion also derives the H_0-equivariance from the blowup description in (b); it follows as well from the uniqueness of the toroidal modification. The item should reuse cones, regular cones, fans and subdivisions from Tau Ceti Analytic toric geometry, Layer 0, and coordinate with the proposed nonarchimedean Part II of that roadmap if it is accepted. Searched: Mathlib has the Rees algebra but no blowups of schemes, toroidal embeddings or log structures; the pinned Tau Ceti library has none either. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Hyodo–Kato description of D_st for the Dwork eigenpart near infinity
items.statement: Let F be a finite extension of Q_p containing ζ_N, with p odd and p ∤ N, and let F^0 = W(k)[1/p] be its maximal unramified subfield, which contains ζ_N. Let H_0 = {(ξ_i) ∈ μ_N^N : ∏ ξ_i = 1}/μ_N act on the Dwork family X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N = N s X_1⋯X_N by X_i ↦ ξ_i X_i, and let χ(ξ) = ∏ ξ_i^{a_i} with Σ a_i ≡ 0 mod N. Let λ be a prime of Z[1/2N, ζ_N] above p, let E be an algebraic closure of Q(ζ_N)_λ, and let V_{λ,s} be the fibre at s of (R^{N−2}π_* Z[ζ_N]_λ)^{χ,H_0}. Let t ∈ F with v(t) = d > 0. Let e, F' = F(π^{1/e}) and the semistable model 𝒴 over O_{F'} of the fibre at s = t^{-1} be as in item 092; F' also has maximal unramified subfield F^0. Then H_0 acts on the Hyodo–Kato cohomology H^{N−2}_HK of the log special fibre (𝒴̄, 𝒩̄) (item 095). The restriction V_{λ,t^{-1}}|G_{F'} is semistable, and for every embedding σ: F^0 ↪ E, D_st,σ(V_{λ,t^{-1}}) := ((V_{λ,t^{-1}} ⊗_{Z[ζ_N]_λ} E) ⊗_{σ,F^0} B_st)^{G_{F'}} ≅ (H^{N−2}_HK)^{H_0 = σ^{-1}∘χ} ⊗_{F^0,σ} E. This isomorphism is compatible with N, and with φ and the filtration as in item 102. Here χ is viewed as E-valued through Z[ζ_N] → Z[ζ_N]_λ ⊂ E, and σ^{-1}∘χ: H_0 → μ_N(F^0).
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, §4: definition of D_st,σ at the foot of p. 20 and the first display on p. 21, applying Tsuji's comparison theorem to the model of Theorem 1.4
items.note: This is the Dwork case of the general equivariant comparison (item 102, planned at CohomologyComparisons CP.4). It belongs to the Dwork switching-motives Part II, which owns the family and the model of item 092, and it is used by item 105 and by the companion's main theorem. It was checked against the page images of pp. 20–21. Searched: Mathlib has B_dR^+ and B_dR, but no B_st and no Hyodo–Kato cohomology. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Log-crystalline cohomology computed by a log-smooth embedding (Hyodo–Kato)
items.statement: Let S be a scheme on which p^n = 0, with a fine log structure L and a quasi-coherent ideal I carrying a PD structure γ; in the application I = (p) with its usual divided powers, which extend to every S-scheme. Let (X, M) be a fine log scheme over (S, L) to which γ extends. Suppose i: (X, M) ↪ (Z, N) is a closed immersion into a log scheme (Z, N) that is log smooth over (S, L), with log PD envelope (D, M_D). Then there is a complex C_{X,Z/S}: O_D → O_D ⊗_{O_Z} ω^1_{Z/S} → O_D ⊗_{O_Z} ω^2_{Z/S} → ⋯. Its differential is determined by ∇(f ⊗ ω) = ∇(f) ∧ ω + f ⊗ dω for f ∈ O_D and ω ∈ ω^j_{Z/S}. The complex represents Ru_{X/S,*}O_{X/S} in D(X_ét), so its hypercohomology is H^*(((X,M)/(S,L))_crys, O_{X/S}). It is natural in the system (X, M) → (Z, N) → (S, L, I, γ). If i is exact and its ideal is generated by p, then D = Z and C_{X,Z/S} is the log de Rham complex of (Z, N)/(S, L); an example is Ȳ_1 ↪ Ȳ_n over (W_n, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0).
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, Proposition 3.3 and Remark 3.4, p. 15, quoting Hyodo–Kato (2.17)–(2.18)
items.note: CR.5 plans: 'Construct exactification and the log PD envelope, followed by the log crystalline site and crystals with log connections. Prove the log PD Poincare lemma and its descent.' The description of log-crystalline cohomology by the de Rham complex of a PD envelope is the standard consequence of that Poincaré lemma. Step (i) of the proof of Theorem 3.2 (item 098) uses it. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Hyodo–Kato monodromy as a connecting homomorphism
items.statement: Let W_n⟨T⟩' be the PD envelope of W_n[T]' along (T). Let (X, M) be a log scheme over (W_n, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0), and let (X, M) ↪ (Z, N) be a closed immersion over (W_n[T]', ℕ, 1 ↦ T) lying over T = 0, with (Z, N) log smooth over (W_n[T]', ℕ, 1 ↦ T). Let Z⟨⟩ be the base change of Z to W_n⟨T⟩' and Z̄ its base change along T ↦ 0, both with the pullback log structures. Hyodo–Kato (3.6) give an exact triangle C_{X,Z⟨⟩/(W_n⟨T⟩',ℕ,1↦T)}[−1] → C_{X,Z/(W_n,(0))} → C_{X,Z⟨⟩/(W_n⟨T⟩',ℕ,1↦T)} →. Applying ⊗^L_{W_n⟨T⟩'} W_n gives a triangle C_{X,Z̄/(W_n,ℕ,1↦0)}[−1] → C_{X/(W_n,(0))} ⊗^L W_n → C_{X,Z̄/(W_n,ℕ,1↦0)} →. The monodromy operator N on H^i(((X,M)/(W_n,ℕ,1↦0))_crys, O_{X/W_n}) is the degree-i connecting homomorphism of this triangle. For X = Ȳ_1 and Z = Y_n, the first triangle is realised by the chain maps (3.3). These are obtained by tensoring with O_{Y_n⟨⟩} the exterior powers of the locally split sequence 0 → O_{Y_n} → ω^1_{Y_n/(W_n,(0))} → ω^1_{Y_n/(W_n[T]',ℕ,1↦T)} → 0, whose first map is multiplication by dlog T.
items.locator: arXiv:2103.00106v1, Proposition 3.5, pp. 15–16, and display (3.3) with the following diagram, pp. 16–17, quoting Hyodo–Kato (3.6)
items.note: CR.6 plans: 'form log-crystalline cohomology of the special fiber over the standard log Witt base (N→W(k),1↦0), and its rational Hyodo–Kato complex. Construct Frobenius and monodromy N, prove nilpotence in the finite-dimensional range and the relation N phi=p phi N in the chosen convention.' Hyodo–Kato (3.6) is their construction of N. In step (i) of the proof of Theorem 3.2 (item 098), N-equivariance is proved by comparing this triangle with the dlog 1 triangle of item 097. Added by the review REV-PAPER-QIAN-23.
